Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Yes, we love Diwali and everything that comes with it. But wait. How exactly do you embrace the festive spirit at your workplace without going overboard? We are here to help you with your dilemma. Here is a list of some fun outfits that you can flaunt at your workplace without hassle. Pair with palazzos Palazzos are effortlessly stylish and comfortable. They are an undeniable fashion must-have. Pair them up with a stylish silk or georgette blouse with traditional prints. Add a chunky beaded ethnic necklace to complete your look. How about a long, elegant kurti to go along with a pair of flared palazzos? We love this look because it is sophisticated and oh-so-stunning. Go ahead and throw on some bangles to amp up the ethnic quotient. Now that we're talking about comfort, what are your thoughts on rocking a pair of smart and versatile cigarette pants with that long kurti? Easy on the eyes and tasteful, cigarette pants look good with almost every type of kurti! Fancy donning a long embroidered jacket along with your palazzos? These jackets will add extra definition and detail to your ensemble. Here's a quick example for you to nail this look. Pair a long white kurti with white palazzos and add a long, printed jacket over it. Throw on a pair of Kolhapuris for that extra oomph. Complete your ensemble by wearing a pair of stunning chandelier or drop earrings. Sari, not sorry!Timelessly beautiful, saris are something that Indian women love wearing. Fabrics like cotton, khadi, silk, and linen promise comfort and look extremely graceful. Similarly, chiffon saris are light and scream elegance. Stick to the pastel palette if you're not entirely comfortable with wearing bold colours to work. Add a cute little bindi and you will be good to go! Not comfortable wearing your regular sari blouse to the office? Worry not! How about a shirt blouse instead? Our Bollywood divas have been in love with this trend for quite some time now and we think it's time that you did too! Pair a crisp full-sleeved shirt blouse with a cotton or linen sari and voila! You have yourself a drop-dead gorgeous outfit that you can comfortably flaunt at your workplace. Cute and quirky peplum blouses are all the rage in town these days. Go ahead and try one out with your sari.  Twist to the originalsKurti dresses are pretty much like the 'LBD' of ethnic fashion; you must have at least one in your wardrobe! Angarakha and shirt-style kurtis make us swoon. Also, they look great with every body type! Wear a smart shirt with a printed long skirt… Who says skirts can't be worn with a buttoned shirt? This look has been all the rage in town this festive season. Pair a flared long skirt with a crisp, well-fitted shirt and get ready to make heads turn all day. Oh! Tasselled earrings work exceptionally well with this outfit. Back to the basicsHow can we not mention the quintessential ethnic work-fashion piece? Ladies, the quaint and angelic white Chikankari kurti can be your lifesaver during the festivities. Throw on a bright coloured dupatta over it for that happy burst of colour. Bandhani and Phulkari dupattas are our personal favourite! You can try on a statement neckpiece or a pair of oxidised jhumkas to go with it. Not feeling experimental? Stick to the classic anarkali. Ladies, you can never go wrong with this one. Opt for floor length and heavily flared anarkalis. The high raised A-line cut makes them look exquisite no matter the body type. How about going one step ahead with some mesmerising chaandbali earrings? You can also wear a nice front open anarkali kurti with your favourite pair of dark jeans. So there you have it! Your very own handy guide for flaunting ethnic wears at your workplace this Diwali! Text: Sanika Tamhane  Got too much to do with almost no time? Well, don’t worry as we have a look book of your next five days right here! Pick your favourite looks and shine on this Diwali. Femina puts together a variety of looks, ensuring that women of all ages get to look their best self this very Diwali. DAY ONE: DHANTERAS Raisin Option AStyle: We recommend an asymmetric kurta. A kurta is not only comfortable to wear but looks oh-so-chic, especially if there is a design element that adds to the look. The asymmetric style gives it an edgy look. If the neckline is low, then team it up with a chunky choker and mid-sized studs in the ear. If the neckline is high, leave the neck jewellery-less and wear chunky earrings. Add some bangles and finger rings and you're set.Makeup: Rosy glow makeup would look perfect with this. Apply subtle blush strokes that make your cheeks pop by adding a touch of extra blush along cheekbones, blending out toward your temples. Nude lips with defined eyes will complete the look. Punit BalanaOption BStyle: For the same vibe, but a different look, go for a layered dhoti pant teamed with a fitted top. The dhoti pant can be of a single colour and the top with it can be in a traditional print, or vice versa. The juxtaposition of plain and print makes for an interesting visual, and balances the look. Drape a long scarf around your neck, or tie it like a turban on your head to quirk it up. Round hoops at your ears and chunky bangles will complete the look.Makeup: To compliment this look we would suggest mauve accents as a preferred makeup looks. Mauve is one of those perfect shades for transitioning from warm weather to cooler temperatures because it feels more dramatic than summery shades. DAY TWO: NARKACHATRUDASHI Option AStyle: Try a sharara with a matching short kurta and dupatta. A monotone colour scheme looks subtle yet striking with the embellishments. Accessories with chaandbaalis and multiple bangles in contrasting colour.  Makeup: Highlight the eyes and the lashes with thick eyeliner and long lashes. Add faux lashes if needed. Keep the rest of the makeup nude, with just a gloss over the lips. MishruOption BStyle: Make your regular kurta stand out with an interesting bottom! Diwali , the festival of light, is a perfect celebration of all things bright. Want to know which Diwali trends to pick that suit your innate style? Scroll below:Diwali Fashion Trends: Minimum Is MaximumThis Diwali, try your hands on some exhilarating minimalistic fashion . Minimalistic outfits are all the rage this season, and this Diwali, you can make the most of it. The basic principle of minimalistic fashion is to keep it simple. You can endorse a simple sari look, clubbed with natural makeup and light jewelry to mark the occasion. This Diwali fashion trend  will help you keep light and would make your celebration free of fuss. And whoever said, less is more, are obviously right. Try and find out! Tip:  You can use the art of layering to add charm to your minimalistic approach. Play up your look by mixing different textures. Diwali Fashion Trends: PalazzosPalazzos have made a distinct place in our hearts with their easy-breezy appeal and ultra-comfortable carryings. The best part about this Diwali fashion trend is that you can pair it with a crop top, tunic, kurta, Anarkali or even with a choli, and would eventually emerge out as the fashionista . Palazzos are also a top fave outfit style favored by celebs. Tip:  With a wide-legged palazzo pant , try long kurtas to add dimension to your outfit. If you're pairing it up with a tunic or long top, glam up with accessories like belts for add some definition to your look. This Diwali, show off some printed perfection Printed Maxi dresses are everybody's top favorite outfit, no matter the occasion. Take cues from your favorite celebs and up your festive style game in printed maxi dresses .Tips: Don't go overboard by mixing too many different prints. However, if you're mixing patterns, don't blend more than two types of prints in your look. From sequined saris to skirts and even kurta, there's nothing that can't handle the sequin shine with elan. Ethnic pants are in vogue this DiwaliGone are the days when bottom wears cam with a limited range of varieties. This Diwali put your fashionable foot forward in ethnic pants. Crop top and lehenga - the perfect trend to pick this DiwaliEndorsed by all your fave celebs, crop top and lehenga combination tops our list of traditional yet spunky Diwali wear . Which dress code fits for the Diwali festival? Ideally, people generally prefer wearing traditional outfits like saris, lehengas and salwar-kameer. Take a moment and reminisce about the days when we would send out anxious messages to our gang asking them about their outfits. What they were donning for the night? What if our outfits matched? The horror! These momentous precautions have a taken a back seat with changing times.  Matching outfits with your friend is no more a faux pas. Instead, it has become a raging and super fun trend that is here to stay! Twinning as a trend first emerged in South Korea’s K-pop culture. While coordinating your outfits completely is not an anomaly entirely, it can overpower the essence of your real personality and make you look, umm, a little too alike. But hey! We’ve got you covered. Have a look at these simple tips and tricks to ace the twinning game. Go ahead and make that winning statement with your fashion twin! One colour palette, multiple outfitsThis is a great way to flaunt the twin-win look without being too discernible. No worries even if you and bestie have different taste when it comes to styling your clothes. The main idea is to predominantly stay within the same colour palette and explore varied outfits. Think Gigi Hadid’s and Kendal Jenner’s iconic twin ensembles Match your fabricsHere’s an easy breezy example to help you get a better idea about this tip.  You can wear a chic eyelet white cotton dress with and your twin can throw on a white top having a similar eyelet detail. Dressing in tandem with your friend in this way leaves a lot of room for experimentation.  Top to bottom! Bottom to top!Interchanging the colours of your outfit with your BFF can be really fun. Fancy sporting a cute baby pink skirt with a pastel blue top? Your BFF, on the other hand, can rock a baby pink top with a pastel blue skirt. Think out of the boxWhat’s the first thing that comes to your mind when you think about twinning? Matching your garbs, right? While this is the most popular choice, there are some other subtle ways in which you can strut your way into the twin parade. How about getting matching phone covers? You are your fashion twin will be carrying around your phone pretty much everywhere. Bring out those accessories There are a myriad of ways in which you can elevate your twinning game without synchronizing your outfits from head to toe. Add a pair of matching oxidized tribal jhumkas to your ensemble for that subtle yet classy twinning look.  So there you have it! Your very own handy guide which will aid you in conquering this super-fun trend. Lastly, we would just want to remind you that twinning is not about replicating each other’s clothes. Don’t strive to look identical! It is one thing to twin your outfit with a person and another to look like their clone. Maintaining your identity is of crucial importance. Reflect on of your personal sense of style. Ensure that your individual personality shines through your matching outfit. A lot is shouldered by the details therein. The aim is not to look like identical twins. You want to alike but different. You can wear the same shirt but pair it up with different bottoms. Wear dresses with a similar length but different prints. Yes, twinning can be that effortless. She had a Cinderella moment, where the ‘fairy godfather’ flicked his wand, and the black and blue gown by Tommy Hilfiger lit up in blue! This was made possible with technology; the structure inside the dress was made up of metallic plates, LED lights, batteries and wire. At the same event, musician Janelle Monáe wore an exaggerated Christian Siriano balloon-hipped dress that had a motorised blinking eye on one breast! This too was an amalgamation of fashion and technology at its chicest! Katy Perry was one of the foremost though and had worn a LED dress at the Met Gala and during her tour in 2014. It’s not just the celebs that get to wear such high-tech ensembles, even daily wear is getting its fair share of technological advancement. Wrist-worn smart watches or bands have become common in recent years. But, according to a research carried out by UK-based Juniper Research, the trend is shifting to ‘connected clothing’, which is forecasted by them to become $1 billion industry in 2020! Here are some of such cool garments that you can choose from.Jacket phone: What if you could pick up calls, control music volume, and get directions by just taping or brushing the sleeves? Levi and Google have collaborated for a jacket that does just that! Digital yogi: If you’re learning yoga, and want to refine your poses and get them right, these yoga pants are just for you! Brand Nadi X has come up with the pants that sense when your yoga pose needs refining and uses haptic feedback to create small vibrations on the body part you need to adjust.Swimming in sun: We’re always worried about just how much sunscreen to apply when on the beach, wearing swimwear. Brand Neviano has come up with stylish swimsuits that have a water-proof a UV sensor that detects if the UV rays are high and if you need more sunscreen to be applied! Research is also being done on how else to incorporate technology into fashion in order to make our life easier. At Deakin University’s Institute for Frontier Materials, they’re looking into developing fibres that can store energy. They’re hoping to make garments that can be used to charge phones and other small devices. Imagine slipping your discharged phone into your pocket, and it comes out charged! Well, with more and more of our lives getting touched by technology, is this tech-forward fashion really a surprise? You’ll be shedding those heavy jackets and coats and finally be able to show off the latest trends in fashion as you step out. Here’s looking at the trends this season that will have you turn heads. While the previous year was all sorts of the frivolous extravaganza, this year is more about practical functionality with a generous dollop of extra. Animal printsAnimal prints started making the rounds of runways sometime early last year and in filtered into our closets in full force by the end of the year. The predatory prints from the ’80s had made a massive comeback but with the much-needed makeover! The well-known prints are so much chic and oh so covetable now. What was once considered a bold statement for the wild-hearted is now being sported at ease by the shy too. Cheetah, leopard, snake, zebra, you name it and the print is available at your go-to an e-commerce site. Styling an animal print is a little tricky as you do not want to look like you belong to the circus! Steer clear of heavy fabrics like wools and velvets and opt for smooth and silky outfits such as silks and cotton. Start with a skinny leopard printed bodysuit and boyfriend jeans with boots and work your way up to a snakeskin evening gown with strappy black heels and minimalistic jewellery and you’re all set.  Utility dressingRemember days you were looked down upon for leaving your house in oversized sweats and cargo pants? Well, it turns out that you can proudly flaunt your baggy cargo pants and sneaks this year, all thanks to the utility dressing rage! Welcome to 2019 where function meets fashion in the form of unpolished practicality. It is nothing but practical, laid back and super comfortable clothing. 2019 has functionality written all over it. Imagine practical oversized clothing in muted tones. Combat trousers, chic overalls, trench coats, baggy sweats, sneakers are taking the fashion world with a storm and we aren’t complaining one bit. The key to nailing the perfect utility look is to style the pieces. If you haven’t experimented yet, start with styling functional clothing with tailored pieces. Start with layering an army jacket over a solid black jumpsuit or playsuit with black boots and move ahead. Also, you can jazz up your khaki trench coat with a red lip and a silk scarf for the perfect date look or can sport those ‘ugly’ trainers with a sleep skirt suit at work and be practical, comfortable and oh so chic at the same time. Win-win!  Cycling shortsCycling shorts are nothing new; in fact, Princess Diana regularly sported them with crew necks long ago. Fast forward to 2019, and they are easily the biggest trend of the year. They were unmissable on the runaways and have been marking territory in online and offline stores in abundance. And not, not just in the regular black spandex garment we’ve grown up with but jazzed up in pretty colours and prints and embroidery. It goes without saying that the humble piece of sportswear has graduated the fashion ladder by heaps and how. The garment that was once worn for physical activities is now being sported under blazers to the boardroom. And oh, it is Kim Kardashian approved too! Women all across the globe have taken a fancy for these bodycon shorts and are pairing it off with anything and everything. From boardrooms to date nights to soirees, these shorts are hard to miss. You too could dip your toes in the water by the pairing of a solid coloured one with a loose oversized tee for your regular coffee runs and upgrade by sporting metallic ones underneath blingy long blazers. It isn’t clear on if the trend is here to stay or not, but that doesn’t stop it from being everywhere at the moment! Oversized2019 revolves around the word oversized! From oversized unstructured jackets and t-shirts to oversized huge sunnies and hats, there’s no stopping really! (Yep, that means we would have to put away our skinny sunglasses from last season!) While last season was more sleek and minimal in terms of accessories, this season is all about exaggeration in terms of hats, belts, bags, etc. The tote bag has gotten a makeover and has blown out really big! Loud hair bands- studded, leather, satin etc too seem to have maximized. Sunglasses are big and bold with added adornments. Chunky jewellery in a more natural form rather than being polished would be a hit this year. Belts too are broad and oversized. 80’s fashionThe thumb rule of fashion is that each trend resurfaces after a few years. There are some that we can’t stand and some we welcome with open arms, like the 80’s fashion. The retro fashion has gotten a redo and we can’t wait to see it on the streets. Imagine belted high waist denim and power suits in neon (remember Priyanka Chopra?) and fringed mullets and big hair. Puffy sleeves, ruffles and shoulder pads are more fashionable than you thought. Although the style is more refined and structured than what it was before. Shoulder pads blazers mean business and are definitely not going anywhere for a long time. Bipasha Basu Singh GroverIn Falguni Mehta.					 It’s time for all of us to make a resolution to not fall prey to body figure stereotyping and make it all about self-love. Not trying to hide behind frumpy clothes that do you no justice is one way to do that. Finding out and understanding your body type is something to be thankful for, however making it a stereotype is not. So all the apple body-shaped woman, pear body-shaped and also the full-sized hourglass body-shaped ladies, stop being used to the embarrassing yourself, rather start embracing yourself! With numerous brands breaking the beauty taboo with real-body campaigns and policies we celebrate every woman with perfection. If you are curvy, it is important to dress according to your size. Say goodbye to every oversized clothes and slide into the outfits with the right fit that will hide your problem areas and highlight the right angles of your frame. Styling from top to bottom can bring a vast change in your look. Have a look at some great style tips for real girls who felt too voluptuous to wear certain items, and we're here to blow those myths right out of the water. LINES AND SHAPES You need your first impression to be fab-worthy, and it is all about your lines and shapes that draw the eye. One great trick is to wear monochrome ensembles. This makes the viewer’s eye move up to down, or vice versa, forming one uninterrupted line, which makes you look tall and slim. If you’re looking to enhance those curves, then opt for a bodycon dress in the right fabric like jersey. You can also wear ensembles that have lines narrowing at the waist and spreading away at the bust and the hips. The lines can be in the form of a print, stitches, pleats, etc. A dress with a plunging V-neck and a cinched waist which then flairs out below, also gives the illusion of an hourglass figure.  THE RULE OF THE HEM Knowing where hems or borders should be on your body can help you lengthen the frame. A knee-length skirt, for example, should sit just right under the knee, never around the biggest part of the calf.  The hem of the jeans should be at the ankle, or (even better) an inch or two below. If you are not of average height, buy your clothes, specifically the bottoms from a retailer that gives you perfect length options. Well, hems can be tricky sometimes but the best thing is to not to have a clue about it and find a tailor with a good eye, trust them and learn as you go.  SAY 'NO' TO OVERSIZED CLOTHES Just beanpoles look great in larger than the average dress size! Don’t add volume to your body by wearing oversized dresses. Instead, pick the clothes that are body-skimming (not too tight) and show your curvy side. Say no to a giant t-shirt, but a maxi or kaftans that skim the curves and have some belt at the waist is cool. If you want an easy profile, or if you got your favourite graphic on a tee or tunic then pair it with tighter trousers or jeans and make it to your advantage. MIND THE SHOES It’s always a head-to-toe thing and what you put on your feet that matters. Pointy tips and low heels can make you look slim, whether you are pairing it with a skirt or a pair of pants. Try to find a shoe with a vamp the ends at the top of your toes, other than halfway around. Shoe styles with low vamps include ballet flats and pumps. High-vamp shoes include Mary Janes and loafers. WHAT NOW, ACCESSORIES? Long chains, not chokers are good to go, especially if you got classic apple shape and short neck. Your focus should be on creating long, unbroken lines along your body. No mood of jewellery? Grab a long scarf helps for the same effect. Layering your jewellery is another way of drawing the eye vertically. From choker to long chains, layer with a couple of them together. Even when wearing bangles and bracelets, stack them up.  VOTE FOR LAYERS Contrary to stereotypes, layering doesn’t necessarily add volume. Instead, it sometimes gives your body a definition. Wearing a tank top with a pretty cardigan instead of one-piece dress or T-shirt can help to underline your shape.  Ensure though that you don’t layer with bulky garments.  EMBRACE YOUR HIGH WAIST High-waisted pants are your companion. They help tuck in folds and fat and minimize muffin tops since they end at the slimmest part of the waist. Ensure they're long, finishing at the lower leg or underneath, following the rule of the hemline.  Dress to make yourself feel good, and you will make heads turn!  Text: Akruti Khandkar 													Step into summers with a fresh hair style to set the tone of the season right. Only issue: You’ve worn them a number of times last season and they just don’t feel that special anymore. How you wish your boots had some colour or a fringe or even a shiny buckle. Sigh! Fret not. With some easy fix tricks, you can upgrade your boots to the latest fashion trends of this season and always stay in style! Buckle up!What you need: Belts, scissors, hot glue.How to make: Cut your belt measured according to the roundness of your boot at the calf. Use hot glue to attach your belt onto your boot. Hold it in place and let it dry. Cut off any unwanted extra belt length and buckle it around your boot. Add extra notches if required. You can repeat the same procedure using more belts with different colours or textures and you have your very own cowgirl boots! Cool cutsWhat you need: Ruler, penknife, chalk.How to make: Draw or trace the design of your choice onto your boot using chalk. Size your grid according to your liking. Use the pen knife to cut out the parts you wish to keep hollow. Once done, wipe off the chalk marks with a damp cloth and you cut out boots are ready. This DIY is easier to work with semi-thick leather that won’t lose shape or tear after cutting. Dazzling tipsWhat you need: Paintbrush, gold/silver pearl shine paint, a thick masking tape, fixative sprayHow to make: Add masking tape a few centimetres away from the tip of the boot. Press firmly. Paint using the gold or silver paint making sure the paint doesn’t go under the tape. Paint smooth and even coats to get a smooth surface. Allow it to dry for a couple of hours and remove the tape. Wipe off any stray dried up paint. Spray on the fixative spray and let it dry for 24 hours. And voila! Lace all dayWhat you need: Lace, pins (if required) and fabric glue.How to make: Cut strips of lace that is long enough to go around your boot. Arrange your pattern and pin it so it holds your desired shape. Using tiny amounts of glue, attach it to your boot. Let it dry completely. You can even add a few beaded chains and feathers for a complete boho look. Retro kicksWhat you need: Masking tape, matte finish paint, brush, scissors.How to make: Cut pieces of the masking tape and stick them onto your boot in any desired shape. You can make a star shape or go abstract and stick the tape onto your boot in any way you like. Once this is done, paint over the design you've created using any matte finish paint of your choice. Let it dry and peel the tape off slowly to reveal your design. Continue making more designs or simply stick the tape in equidistant parallel lines to create stripes for a sporty look.Text: Yvonne Jacob 													The glamour industry revolves around fashion cycles and trends that dominated once, have returned to claim their spot again. After changing three flights and taking a three-hour bus ride, we landed in Montepuez—the second largest city in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique. The day had been a whirlwind, as we hopped on and off different vehicles. The moment we landed in Mozambique, however, a burst of fresh, clean air welcomed us. The quaint city is home to Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM), which is a Mozambican company developing operations at the ruby deposits in the city, and covers approximately 33,600 hectares. A leading supplier of responsibly-sourced coloured gemstones across the globe, MRM is owned by UK-based natural resource company Gemfields (75 per cent), and Mozambican company Mwiriti (25 per cent). We spent two days in the heart of the most recently discovered ruby deposit in the world, and unearthed more than just these precious crimson stones. 													The journey beginsOver 500 million years in the making, ruby, or ratnaraj (meaning king of the gemstones in ancient Sanskrit), is an extremely rare stone, cherished by royalty, social A-listers, and collectors alike. We went to see one of the mine pits on the first day, where rubies are deposited as alluvial or colluvial material over a weathered bedrock.Rubies were first discovered in Montepuez in 2009, following which, Gemfields and Mwiriti signed an agreement in 2011 to officiate the mining process. MRM uses a multidisciplinary approach for mining—geological (rubies that are typically associated with certain rocks or minerals), geophysical (airborne survey—magnetic and radiometric), and geochemical (determining chemical signatures of hidden mineral deposits). The sheer size of the mine pit was staggering, and it brought forth the concern of what happens to it once it has been exhausted.Mining with a conscienceMRM is committed to mining in a way that has the least environmental impact. Jack Cunningham, Sustainability, Policy and Risk Director at Gemfields, explains, “Before we mine an area, we collect seeds of the indigenous plants and trees from the top soil and create a seed bank. We then grow the seeds in a nursery for replanting as we complete mining.” Along with encouraging biodiversity, old pits are back-filled and rehabilitated, and no harmful chemicals are used during the mining process. “Machine oil is carefully managed and stored, machines and vehicles are maintained by our in-house teams, and all spills are cleaned up and the contaminated soil is bioremediated,” says Cunningham.The road to development was not an easy one, and initially, the company faced resistance from the inhabitants. Cunningham recalls, “There was uncertainty from the local community about what the benefits would be and how quickly they would receive those. An influx of thousands of illegal miners also caused social problems at a time when we weren’t yet in a position to help the community. Since 2014, however, we have had a dedicated team on the ground that carries out community engagement, and addresses their needs and grievances, and the relationship with them has vastly improved.” MRM has provided employment to 1,110 people, both directly and via contractors, 95 per cent of whom are Mozambican nationals. The mining company has also helped nine farming associations (two of which are dedicated to empowering women and in total represent 290 partner farmers), and taught them new techniques that have increased yields. Looking at the community as a whole, the company has invested in infrastructure for four primary schools (three of which are new), providing education to 1,000 primary school-aged children. “Schooling is the responsibility of the state, however our infrastructure atleast helps the government with a costly aspect of public education. Once established, we hand over the schools to the government for their onward management as a national asset,” elucidates Cunningham. The establishment of two mobile health clinics serves thousands of people across six villages. Isac Rafael, Director of the Namanhumbir Health Center, Mozambique, stated, “With these mobile clinics, it’s possible to care for patients in the most remote areas without sanitary units. This also gives easy access to pregnant women, children, and the elderly, who don’t have to travel long distances.”The final stepWe spent the last leg of our journey in the wash plant and sorting house, where the raw stones are processed and graded according to their colour, size, and clarity. We witnessed how a team of highly skilled sorters picked rubies from the rubble, in a secure environment. Their hands worked like machines as they separated the precious stones in silent harmony. The final pieces are then auctioned off by Gemfields and till June 2017, a total of eight ruby auctions have generated a revenue of US$280 million.We entered the city with a bunch of preconceived notions, and after spending two days in the shoes of a miner, left with hope for the Montepuez community. That’s what you get in this city of Mozambique, along with beautiful never-ending blue skies, and a warm community that believes in co-existence. FASHIONHigh glossNothing screams power more than high shine fabrics worn appropriately. While last season was all about plastics in apparel, this season is all about high gloss on any and every fabric texture such as leather, satin etc. Right from long wrap-around coats to pants to even see-through dresses, high shine is marking its territory everywhere. But beware if worn out of proportion or styled incorrectly, the trend sure can fall back easily. The best way to start would be with a high shine statement belt on a solid outfit and move upwards to high gloss trimmings on outfits and then take the plunge! “I feel high gloss fabrics can somehow add sheer sexiness to the look. I personally love wearing statement gloss t-shirt dresses and black or nude shoes,” says lifestyle blogger Naina Ahluwalia. Plaid and simpleThe key to play with plaid is to not go overboard with it and style it with colourful bright accessories to brighten up the look. “If you ask me about plaid, I can only and only think of the term classic yet trendy. Plaid can be played around with prints and colours but it's not a trend, I would call it an evergreen print that everyone needs to have in their closet. Of course, every year something or the other trendy using plaid comes up and those make good additions to the closet,” shares lifestyle blogger Aleena Macker. You can try your hand at plaid button-down skirts or bright plaid co-ordinates or even plaid mules, there’s no stopping this season. EMPIRE STATE OF MINDEmpire waistlineThe first and most recognisable waistline there is the empire waistline also popularly referred to as the empire silhouette, empire line or just empire style. The basic structure of this waist pattern is categorised by the tightly fitted bodice that ends just below the bust to deliver the whole high-waisted look. The obsession with the high-waisted line began during the 18th century and was brought to fame by the empress of the first French Empire, Napoleon Bonaparte’s wife, Empress Josephine de Beauharnais; which is where the whole regal reference is sourced from. If a style was good enough for an empress, you can be sure it’s good enough for you as well. The entire style is part of the neoclassical style that was obsessed with imitating and replicating or rather reviving the style that could be seen in the ancient Greek and Roman which portrayed women wearing long gowns clinched under the bust.Perhaps it's old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the style a wonderfully romantic appeal. The flowy and really luxurious feel it imparts makes your inner Greek goddess preen with appreciation, accompanied with the fact that it’s incredibly comfy with zero constriction is an advantage that has very women sighing in absolute relief. Its old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the empire waistline style a wonderfully romantic appeal.Match-maker: The empire waist is designed in such a way that it sits above a woman's natural waistline and generally accentuates the bust which is why it is ideally always accompanied with deep scoop necklines or sweetheart and V-necklines.   This style is perfect for those with pear-shaped bodies i.e. having a slim upper body and a more voluptuous lower body. As such if you don’t want to draw attention to your hips then empire waistline is the way to go. The waist tends to emphasise the narrowest part of the body and camouflaging the wider lower body. It’s also great for short people because the raised waistline creates the appearance of extra height. Now, for the don’ts - avoid the billowy, voluminous fabrics. Pleats and gathers are another no-nos.It is best to stick to with A-line structures or sheath that help to highlight your body’s best features instead of hiding it under too much fabric. When wearing an empire waist top, the best choice of bottom wear is either skinny or straight legged pants. Pairing it up with voluminous wide-legged tend it delivers a rather frumpy, disproportionate look. Empire waist dresses are ideal for pregnant women as its flowy and comfortable. DROP DOWNDrop waistAfter the waistline was pulled up to new heights, the winds of change eventually made their way through the world of fashion and according to the laws of the universal: what goes up must come down. So after the waistline enjoyed the lofty highs, during the roaring 20s, it dropped down to become the distinctive dropped waist style. Around the time when women were finally breaking free from a vile instrument of torture also known as the corset, they decided to adopt more masculine silhouettes. It was believed to be seen as female liberation from traditionally-accepted shapes. A dropped waist sits below the actual natural waistline of a woman and is characterised by the line across the hips instead of the waist thereby providing the illusion of a longer torso. The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival. During then the look took on a sportier feel rather than the elegantly sleek feminine look of the 20’s. Designers have experimented around with it for years and while the basic construct was never tampered with, there were several add-ons like belts, pleated and ruffled skirts to give it a little extra something every time.The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival.Match-maker: Dropped waisted looks aren’t quite as popular today as they were before but they haven’t faded into obscurity completely because the whole ‘shapeless’ look is on the prowl and is extremely favoured. The waist makes quite a statement and, if you know just how to wear and accessorise it, it can turn you into an über fashionista who knows how to work any style like a boss. Short drop-waisted look looks fantastic on women with the tall slender willowy figures and narrow hips. With the addition of a ruffled skirt for a flouncy free-flowing look or an A-line skirt for a sleeker formal look, it could swing either way. It would be prudent for women who have a heavier lower half to stay away from the ruffles as it would be super counterproductive and make the lower body look even wider.For those with long legs and a short torso, drop-waisted dress - with moderate heels - works well. And for those with a long torso and short legs, drop waists with high heels will help to balance out the long torso and deliver a balanced, symmetrical look. BASQUE IN ITBasque waistlineWhat could you have in common with a woman who lived during the American Civil War? Nothing much; except maybe your dress’s waistline. The Basque waistline, which is also referred to as the antebellum waistline is a waistline that emerged when the hourglass figure was the shape every woman was vying for. This waistline served to flatter the equally proportioned body of an hourglass shape and has merits for other body types as well.A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures. The style forms a noticeable ‘V’ on the front of the body coming 2-3 inches below the normal waistline. If the pronounced V-shape is too sharp for one’s taste and then the style can also be modified to a softer U-shape. It is a generally flattering style that provides a slimmer and longer torso due to its low ‘V’ and reduces the width of the hips and waist. Though the idea is to love your body no matter what, wanting to take off a couple for inches every now and then using illusionary means is perfectly acceptable. The style originally began as French-fitted bodice or jacket that eventually become part of the dress rather than a separate piece altogether. A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures.Matchmaker: A Basque waistline is flattering for many body shapes; the low V-shaped line lengthens the torso and creates a wonderfully slim silhouette. However, due to the shape of the waistline, the style tends to draw distinct attention to the lower tummy region and if you aren’t comfortable with that then it's best to avoid this style. Pear-shaped bodies or square shaped bodies should not go for this kind of waistline as it would not be able to appropriately accentuate and flatter those kinds of body types. Hourglass and other body types would be able to carry it off perfectly as it helps to balance out the hips and waist due to the elongation illusion the waist creates.   LOSE THE SYMMETRYAsymmetric waistlineThings that are straight and simple are thoroughly uninteresting after a while. In order to shake things up, the fashion industry developed an obsession with everything that was off-centre and unbalanced. And that is because things like that tend to be more interesting. There is more depth, character and visual appeal. From hemlines with varying lengths to slanted necklines, there is something about asymmetrical patterns in an attire that just make the whole look more sophisticated and bold while breaking free from the rigid symmetry.Though an asymmetrical waistline is not as radical as some of the other things in the same school of thought, it is an interesting style to incorporate. An asymmetrical waistline is a style that sits diagonally across the natural waistline. It originates from a point in the natural waistline and then extends down in a slant to the opposite end. In other words, it is just a slanted waistline across your body, high on one side and low on the other.Asymmetrical waistline creates a slimming effect for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies.Match-maker: Asymmetrical waistline is a type of waistline that will create a slimming effect. Thus, it is great for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. WAIST NOT, WANT NOTPrincess seamThe absence of something is often beneficial as well. Though there exist several types of waistlines to go with every kind of body, there is a particular style that does not need a visible waistline. A style that is much beloved and which is about as timeless as the name itself - the princess seam style. It is a style that will probably never go out of style and is an epitome of soft feminity.A princess seam or line is characterised by the long seams that start from below the arm, or under the shoulder and curves delicately over the bust and down the body to give a prominent long look that that associated with A-line dresses. The seam can be stitched into blouses or dresses to have the desired structure and shape. Due to the way it is designed, the style does not need a waistline since it runs along panels down the body. The princess seam was associated with Charles Frederick Worth, a prominent English fashion designer of the 19th and 20th century who is also acknowledged by many as the ‘Father of Haute Couture’. The style was of course created for Princess Alexandra of Denmark, the wife of King Edward VII. Due to its fitted and figure-hugging design, it was believed to be the first ‘bodycon’ (who are we to deny that fact?).The princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.Match-maker: The princess seam works remarkably well for those with hourglass figures, the long, shapely seams that gather in at the waist and flare out again at the hips. However, the princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.  It’s a wardrobe staple for every lady, kind of like a good pair of shoes or an LBD. Or better yet an LBD with princess seams is a very acceptable option as well.  Either way, knowing what looks good on your unique body is the first step to being fashionably perfect every day but the personal interpretations and add-ons are what make the outfit your identity.  Text: Crystal SymssImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock					Cover storyMonochrome jackets look both trendy and sophisticated. Co-founded by Jayesh Sachdev, it was a venture to bring his art to many through fashion and décor. What he didn’t know was that all their products will be sold out within the first week. Their quirky – as their name rightly suggests – designs are well appreciated and have had many takers even amongst the celebs like Deepika Padukone, Ranveer Singh, Priyanka Chopra, Alia Bhatt, Parineeti Chopra, Amitabh and Abhishek Bachchan, Kangana Ranaut and Kajol. The brand defines itself as a fashion and lifestyle label that exudes wearable eccentricity. “That, in addition to rich colour, graphic art and playful sophistication define our essence,” Sachdev mentions in the brand information, “We are synonymous with all things fun, offbeat and quirky. Our exuberant approach to the everyday encourages personal style with a dash of incandescent charm. We call it life in technicolor.” An artist by passion, a designer by choice and a creative entrepreneur by vocation, Sachdev talks about the brand, his journey and making people a walking gallery. It shouldn’t have been such a surprise though. Sachdev is an artist, designer and entrepreneur. He graduated with a Degree in Visual Communication at Lasalle College of the Arts, Singapore and holds the national record for having painted India’s largest concept artwork. Alongside running the Quirk Box, he continues to practice as an artist, exhibiting through New York to Bombay. He has won many awards including British Council Young Arts Entrepreneurs India 2008, Tiger Translate India Arts Awards and Crow Bar Asia Advertising Awards and he is also a credited TEDx speaker. Apart from his art, he is an avid photographer and loves to play tennis. Quirk Box also, is an award-winning label, alongside its founder. It won the Best Urban Wear Label – India award at Grazia Young India Fashion Awards in 2015. They have showcased their collection at the Lakme Fashion Week since 2013. In previous interviews, the artist-designer who is inspired by Sabyasachi and Manish Arora told the story behind Quirk Box, “There is an oddity and sense of innovation that is a virtue of Quirk Box. This oddity, this quirkiness, and this implicit need to be original and fun put together are what we like to call the Quirk Box. We’re here to be different and carve a niche of our own in this ever-growing industry. The strategy is to only provide fresh, quirky and unimaginable designs to our customers and reach out to prospects that haven’t yet been exposed to quirky fashion and lifestyle.” Living up to its story and its name, each collection by this brand has been unique and out-of-the-box. Not one to follow trends, but to set them, he has kept true to the essence of the brand with each collection, having come up with new and interesting prints every time. “Our USP is our strong understanding of design and fashion and our inherent traits of wanting to create something original each time,” he explains, “We are not aping trends, even though our works have a very strong ‘pop art’ essence, we are neither imitating designs, nor finding inspiration from Bollywood/Hollywood or popular culture, we are constantly striving to create innovative art that spells individuality.” Sachdev and his brand are all about expressing their art through various mediums, and thus was the Quirk Box Design Studio born. “I am primarily a visual artist,” tells the man who believes that ‘design is art with a function and business is applying that design into context’, “I have no formal understanding of fashion. My art and illustration aesthetic are what makes Quirk Box distinguished. The art that is made for Quirk Box is put into fashion, but fashion is only one such medium onto which my art can be applied to. We can design your space, your business identity, textile prints, wedding cards… the scope is diverse and limitless.” Through this independent design studio, the design style that is inherently Quirk Box can be hired as a service and not just as a product. We have a tête-à-tête with Sachdev talking of the milestones he’s reached in his journey till now, his inspirations and aspirations. Can you tell in brief about your journey to date?It's been a decade that I've been an artist; so it’s clearly been a long and exciting one. I started out as a Jr. Art Director at an agency in Singapore, after graduating from an art school. I eventually moved back to India to start Emblem, my design studio. That didn’t initially kick off the way I'd have imagined and I occupied myself painting. Before I knew it, I'd become a full-time artist. I founded Emblem Tee, and the Emblem Art Gallery and later Quirk Box. I like to believe I'm a creative entrepreneur as much as an artist. Along the way I picked up a few accolades and awards, it's been a frustrating, enriching and a learning journey, and I'm probably not even close to halfway where I'd like to be. Were art and design something you wanted to pursue from the start?I wanted to write. I wanted to play tennis and football. When I didn’t end up pursuing those as career options, I had a strong idea that I would be inclined towards a Visual Arts career. What inspires you to create?There is something magical and whimsical about creation. You have freedom. I enjoy this freedom of being a creator.  What inspired you to start Quirk Box?As an artist, you tend to have a limited audience. Often affluent or far too niche and restricted. This meant all my creative ideas and visions would manage to reach a small audience. I hoped that a lot more people could firstly, witness my art and secondly, afford it. Quirk Box was started to be a functional art label. Instead of buying my art on a canvas, you could now buy it as a garment. When you wear Quirk box, you are a walking gallery of my imagination. You started with an online store, and haven’t gone for the traditional retail format. Was that a conscious decision? Do you plan to have your own store in the future?The idea was always the penetration of the market. If you've lived in one place too long, you become a frog in a pond. You have to go out there and tell your story to everyone. I didn’t want to be tied to a physical space. I needed my art to be everywhere. And online allows me to reach 200 countries as opposed to one specific location that a brick and mortar are about.Since the start, you have come up with out-of-the-box designs. How has the response been?We turned seven in April. It's been wonderful. We've dressed commoners and celebrities alike. Won the awards that mattered and got the features that matter. We've sold from Pune to Peru. I have much to be grateful for. How’s the Quirk Box journey been till date? Can you tell us in brief about the milestones in this journey?When we started out seven years ago, we started out wanting to create something exciting. We had unrealistic ambitions, we wanted to reach the entire country, but a part of me believed I was being delusional to expect it. A week into our launch we were sold out and we realised we had created something larger than we knew. It has been a learning curve. Meeting incredibly talented people, incredible experiences, winning relevant awards, dressing fashion goddesses, it opened new windows of opportunities and experiences, from the fashion weeks to dressing A-listers. It's been a long tough exciting ride.Where do you get your inspiration from when you come up with new collections?Inspiration is everywhere. We find inspiration from our experiences and surroundings. There is no preset for this. Every day is a new experience and ideas are ever evolving. The fabrics you choose, the prints, the colours… Why do you choose what you do?I make art that I chose to make. We do not restrict ourselves with the art. The freedom of creating is why we started this. This is not trending determined. The fabrics that are chosen based on the season, cotton would work in warmer weathers, crepe and silks in the festive season. Since we print a multitude of colour, we also need to pick fabrics that allow us to print the kind of art we make. We also try to keep our prices in-check so the fabrics determine the same. Can you tell us about your latest collection?Our summer collection Chikanobu was inspired by the 18th-century Woodcut Artworks of the Japanese Artist Toyohara. I love all things Japanese, and Japanese art was something I've always been intrigued by. My wife Priyanka who is now the Chief Illustrator at Quirk Box was truly inspired by the idea of recreating his works in a contemporary context. The artworks of Emperor Meiji, the Japanese Cranes, Waves and Geisha's all features as artworks in the series of our Summer Resort wear. We used Crepe this season. It is light in weight and the blend we use is easy on sweat, heat and wash care.Who is your inspiration? I am inspired by my travel experiences. Food, small, the unknown that is exciting brings with it new stories to tell. Stories that we tell through art and fashion. Your most and least favourite parts of designing?Every day at work is a challenge; a new challenge. The amalgamation of art and business is something I am excited by. I thrive on this. Having to solve internal conflicts of tailor/labour is a rather annoying part of the profession though.What in your opinion is your biggest achievement so far?That I am able to sustain art in a country that has no value for it, is my biggest achievement. Quirk Box was one of the first of its kind with the designs that you came up with. These days there are many who do similar or “inspired” designs. Your take on plagiarism in the industry.Everything is an inspiration, and everything is a copy… some more than others. I see a tree and I draw it. I copy from nature. Some see the drawing of my tree and copy it. Unfortunately, due to the weak intellectual property laws and ambiguities, this won’t change anytime soon. In the meanwhile, we have to believe that imitation is the best form of flattery.Being an artiste and a designer, how do you balance the two facets?They are integrated. One fuels a passion, one fuels the bills. Can you tell us a little about Quirk Box Design?Quirk Box is an independent boutique art-based design studio. It offers crafted solutions for all your design needs.  With over 10 years of experience in the design space, including branding, graphics and fashion, the studio offers the same philosophy and principle of its original art and design and strong aesthetic essence, that is no longer limited to its in-house label, but to anyone that would like to hire its service. having worked with fashion, art, graphic design, branding, advertising, space design, the brand now offers you a design language you need, keeping intact the graphic art and playful sophistication that defines our essence. Can you tell us a little about your next collection?Our next is our most ambitious collection yet. Given the detail of the work, we are still working against the clock to release it in time for August. But hopefully, it will see the light of day soon.What do you envision the future holding for you?I wish I could foretell the future. But I can only hope. Hope to create good work, hope that it continues to be appreciated. Hope that I can sustain a lifestyle that allows me to travel extensively.What is your advice to the upcoming designers and fashion entrepreneurs?They don't need my advice. They need self-belief, courage and perseverance.					Sleeves are an element of fashion that has undergone some drastic upgrades, variations and evolutions in the last century. So whether you want to channel the Elizabethan age of over-the-top opulence or free-spirited bohemian vibes, there is a sleeve for every kind of whim and fancy. Like everything in the fashion industry, there is a time when some styles rise above the rest to become the look and talk of the season and the sleeves making waves (literally) this season are a mix of delightful throwbacks and modern sophisticated elegance. Bell of the ballBell sleeve is a super cute and fun style that is making a comeback to the fashion scene. The bell sleeves have been much beloved for their flowy design that allows easy movement and for their uber-graceful feminine appearance. In its previous lives, bell sleeves started their journey out by simply being a flared sleeve that was a part of the Japanese Heian period. A long dramatic flared sleeve was a classic feature and style norm back in the day. It then migrated across the world into the European medieval era and was predominately a style that was seen in the outfits of members of the church clergy. And it was around that time that the sleeve slowly and steadily developed its signature bell structure.The elite class of the Elizabethan era adored the bell sleeves. And as 'less is more' was not a phrase that the stylists of the Elizabethan era particularly believed in at the time, they decided to make it more extravagant (because, why not?) By adding on various embellishments like frills, lace and pleats . After which, the sleeves safely made their way into the modern world wherein the bell shape became more distinct and was synonymous with gentle femininity.The bell sleeves have been around for a long time and are likely to be around for a good bit more too considering the comebacks it makes every few years, seamlessly incorporating itself into the latest fashion trends. Though the bell structure is highly appreciated in the form of sleeves, its other variant 'the bell bottoms' weren't so lucky. But the world of fashion is a strange and unpredictable place. You never know what might pop up again.Why, though? Why has this simple little style managed to stick around for so long? Well, it because bell sleeves are enormously versatile. They have comfortably made themselves a perfectly fashionable asset in every area. From chic work wear to flirty casual and elegant evening wear, bell sleeves can be brought to every area of ââinterest. (Multipurpose utility? Yes, please). It is also wearable in a range of different fabrics as well as wool, lace and silk.How to style: Bell sleeves are great for any kind of occasion. And they come in several different variations, the fitted sleeve with bell flare starting only at the wrist or at the elbow. This is great for people wanting a combination of two styles; full-fitted sleeve and bell sleeve. When it comes to styling it for a classy, ââhigh fashion workwear ensemble, bell sleeves that tie at the elbow add that dash of sleek with a mild dose of flounce. Paired with some tailored pants make an effortless fashionable work-wear look that will help get rid of those Monday blues. Sheer silk blouses sporting bell sleeves are perfect for decadent evening wear and is super comfortable. Cap-tain of styleIf there was ever a voting poll to decide which is the 'all-time favorite sleeve' then cap sleeves would probably win hands down. Cap sleeves give us a feel of soft femininity, throwing it back to those long dreamy gowns with adorable cap sleeves that Keira Knightley wore to the ball in Pride and Prejudice (Who wouldn't want to pretend to be in that situation?). It is a representation of simple, uncomplicated design that is made for everyone. Their modest design is probably why they have been a part of bridal gowns and bridesmaids dress for a long time. The first record of cap sleeves being included into wedding attire has been traced back to the roaring 1920s and then made their way into everyday party wear fashion as well (flapper dresses anyone?).After that, the beloved cap sleeves cruised their way into the 30s, 40s and 50s. Clearly, fashion couldn't let them go and for good reason. It was made widely popular and sealed its place as timeless style when the biggest celebrities showcased their little cap sleeves of the most important day of their lives: their wedding. Scores of celebrities and royalty have sported cap-sleeved wedding gowns and strengthened its reputation as a favored design. When Jackie Kennedy Onassis wed John Kennedy in 1953 in her beautiful cap-sleeved gown, the style's popularity shot through the roof. Mega style icon Audrey Hepburn wore a cap-sleeve wedding dress in her movie 'Funny Face' in 1957 and that made it official, the cap sleeves were here to stay.The most recent ambassador for the beloved cap sleeve is the ever popular sister of the Duchess of Cambridge herself, Pippa Middleton. The fashion world will probably never forget the day she stepped out in that immaculate form-fitting cap-sleeved white gown on the day of the royal wedding. The wedding was not the only historic thing that happened that day. Pippa, with endless grace and panache, brought the caps back into the fashion scene. And it did not end there. When it was Pippa's turn to tie the knot, she dazzled the world again with another cap-sleeved beauty. Cap-sleeved elegance at its finest ladies!How to style: Though it is extremely favored in the wedding scene, bell sleeves are also quite flexible and can be showcased in everyday fashion as well. Along with it being a part of the usual suspects of western wear ie dresses and tops, you can even bring this style a little closer to home. Embellished high-necked sari blouses with cap-sleeves are exceptionally gorgeous and are a great way to amp up your traditional wear. Bishop sleeveBishop sleeves are sleeves that are quite similar to a bell sleeve, however, they have one defining feature. The full-length sleeves have a familiar flare that flows from the shoulder but it ends with a wide cuff that is gathered and cinched at the wrist. The style emulates a luxurious vintage feel. And it should rightfully because this style has been around for a long time. Though the sleeves are similar to the shape to the sleeves worn by bishops of the church- hence the name - but traces of the flouncy sleeves go even further back in time to the sixth-century Byzantine era (Kudos to them for probably being the oldest sleeve style ever). Though they were not all that prevalent during that time, bishop sleeves become a lot more common during the 1800s.Bishop sleeves got major traction back in the mid-60s during the time when the free-spirited hippie culture was making a statement in society. The relaxed flowing look it created coincided perfectly with the hippie style and they were all for it. Further on, in the 70s and 80s, the sleeves were made of lycra and polyesters to maintain the soft bouncy look that was its biggest selling point. Bishop sleeves created a flattering, balanced silhouette that made a person's shoulders look smaller in comparison. The cuff, historically, is a wide button cuff but over the years, it went through many reconstructions. Elasticized cuffs, embellished cuffs and cuffs with decorative trimmings were all a part of the advancements the bishop sleeves underwent to meet the ever-changing fashion demands.The distinctive shape of the bishop sleeve also attributes it to be known as balloon sleeves. They are also believed to be similar to peasant sleeves due to the fact that they both gather around the wrist. However, the difference is that peasant sleeves ideally tend to puff out at the shoulders, while bishop sleeves just flow smoothly from the shoulder down the arm for a nice draped effect. Peasant sleeves also do not possess a wide cuff but rather have a simple elastic band.How to style: Bishop sleeves are very distinctive and make quite a statement with their classically vintage look. Hence, they are great for formal blouses. Paired with a fitted high-waisted pant to emphasize the sleeves and create a stunning silhouette that just all of the soft sophistication; in other words, high fashion boss lady. For a look that's more casual Fridays, pair it with jeans instead. Draped bishop sleeves add a perfect little dramatic flair to a short loose dress with some strappy wedges or flats and you've basically got you're boho-chic on. Or a fitted dress that flatters your natural curves along with flowing sleeves is perfect for desk to dinner days. Keeping up with the kimono sleeveJapan's foremost export into the world of fashion is the traditional kimono and most popularly the kimono sleeve has carved its place into the fashion scene for the smooth elegant effect that it gave. Traditionally, the type of kimono a person wore would be a marker that officially denoted their social standing, rank and occupation. Well, clothes tend to have that effect even now in a rather unofficial, unspoken way. Nevertheless, the sleeve style eventually made its way across to the western world towards the end of the 1940s.Traditional Japanese wide kimono sleeves are varied in lengths. The sleeves of the kimono's that were used in theatrical performances tending to almost 3 feet long and would drag across the floor for spectacularly dramatic effect. Imagine walking into a party with 3 foot long sleeves (instant show stopper). Unfortunately, that wouldn't be the most practical thing to wear in the real world, so the sleeves were cut down to size to suit more normal measurements. Ideally, kimono sleeves have a deep armhole and the sleeve does not have a definite shoulder seam or armhole seam, which is its peculiarity. The main body of the garment and the sleeve are created from the same continuous piece of material, it, therefore, is also known as a 'grown-on' sleeve.How to style: Kimono sleeves are the trend this season and are perfect for wrap dresses, cinched-in waist secured with a sash that completely the whole traditional kimono look as a whole. Kimono sleeves are also great for sheer or silk blouses that go well with pants or pencil skirts. Shrugs with long kimono sleeves are an excellent way of adding a chic layer to casual jeans and tank top outfit. Cape wonder sleeveCape sleeves and capes are on the list of trending items this season. It's a cool look that speaks of elevated style and if you know just how to wear it and accessorize it, it can be a striking feature in your fashion diaries. Cape sleeves are can be traced back to the past with the introduction of the cloak. Capes were basically an outer garment that draped over the wearer and covered the shoulders, arms and was fastened at the neck. They were super popular back in medieval Europe (Try not to think of long Dracula-esque cape). After their heyday back in the dark ages, capes are back in the modern age to make a style statement unlike any other with designers offering new spins and innovations on trend to make classy and impart a sense of regality because every girl deserves to be a queen .Cape sleeves are most popularly seen on jackets - as the cape is essentially made for outerwear - that has been upgraded with bold new patterns, interesting new fabrics and showcased in varying lengths for every kind of occasion. The sleeves can either in be flared if made with softer fabrics or can be straight and sleek for a more defined structure.How to style: Cape sleeves are great on blazers and because the fabric is stiffer, the silhouette you acquire is impeccably sleek and very flattering; perfect for when you evolve from boss lady to modern queen! It is ideal for smart elegant formal wear or can be used to dress up a basic and top ensemble for a night out. Long flared, looser cape sleeves work well on dresses for an ultra-majestic look or on light pastel colored tops for those casual brunch days. Pick out any one of this season's trendiest sleeves and work it like a boss. Text: Crystal Symss Images: Yogen Shah Like history, fashion sure has a way of resurrecting back. Of staple stringsThis quite modest piece of string worn across the neck dates back to 2500 BC! From denoting prostitution to denoting lesbianism, the choker has travelled quite practically everywhere. The choker, now sitting proudly in jewellery cases gained its due attention in the 1900’s because of Queen Alexandra of England when she flaunted one to hide a small scar. It further garnered attention when people started wearing plastic chokers in 1990’s. From Gwyneth Paltrow flashing one at the 1999 Academy Awards to Paris Hilton and Rihanna, every fashion diva has surrendered to the choker game. Back home, Zeenat Aman was one of the first celebrities to rock a choker. Of course, these days the humble choker has enjoyed popularity as celebrities such as Sonam Kapoor, Priyanka Chopra, etc. exhibit various types of choker including diamonds, lace, velvet, beads, leather, shoelace (Yep, even a shoelace can be worn as a choker!) Not only is it super stylish, it is also easy on the pocket and comes with a guarantee of making you seem like an Insta- goddess! Chokers are literally the easiest way to make you seem like you belong to the ‘you can’t sit with us’ tribe. The 90s saw the ‘it’ crowd styling their plastic cord with denim shorts and crops.Style guide: Chokers are something that could be worn throughout the day and beyond.  The strand science is pretty easy to grasp. (No Einstein IQ required here!). The only deciding factor to keep in mind to wear one is the neckline of the outfit that you would be wearing it with. Return of the coy cropA moment of applause for Madeline Vionnet for if it wasn’t her, we really wouldn’t have been offered the cropped fashion. In 1932, Madeline Vionnet designed an evening gown with strategically cut openings at the waist. The design was accepted by the masses and how! By the 1940’s, women’s magazine had further enhanced the trend by exposing degrees of midriff. Teen magazines of late 1940’s and 1950’s too weren’t far behind and happily participated in the movement by flaunting midriff barring suits and tops. Although it was restricted to swimwear initially, since the trend was so widely accepted, it was only natural for it to have an upgrade and move into women’s wear.This was only the beginning for the coy crop top. Crop tops further moved ahead to become “the look” of the 1980’s. The midriff-baring piece of clothing found a fan in Madonna, who wore it in a lot of her albums. She even made it a part of her signature look. It further garnered tons of exposure on silver screen and was part of many iconic films such as Dirty Dancing and Flash Dance. Crop tops conquered the pop culture and became a major part of it all throughout the 90’s. The low rise jeans paired with belly shirts became a classic duo especially in the sector of music and television. Britney Spears too was seen parading around in the same quite often. While they were initially worn during daily workouts with leggings, the crop top progressed to being worn with denim for a casual look.Style guide: Fortunately, styling a crop top isn’t all that demanding as it is quite a versatile piece and each one of us can find a variant to work around with.  Cropped fashion isn’t restricted to the 20 something’s or to the women with washboard abs.  The beauty of it is that it can blend into your business wardrobe as efficiently as it can belong to your vacation travel suitcase. If you aren’t comfortable with taking a leap forward by sporting a short crop, you could always work your way up by taking a shirt or top and giving it a DIY crop makeover by tying it! Full sleeved short tops paired with full skirts are another way of toning down the flash. You could also pair one with a high-waisted pant or knife pleated palazzo and add a blazer to rock that conference at 3 pm at the workplace. “Who’s not a fan of crop tops? It pairs well with high-waisted bottoms. Throw on a shrug to avoid showing off too much (if you want to tone down the look),” shares Sharma. Matching separates like a crop and a skirt with heels and a colour pop sling could have you looking like a million bucks – that too, without having to spend it. Doesn’t it look like it’s time for you to head down to the store and invest in some crop tops now? Denim dramaMost of us are positively familiar with how denim came into existence; it worked its way up from being worn solely by labourers to being warmly accepted by the masses. High-waisted denim is a different thing altogether. It was invented in 1940 when brand Levis produced clothing keeping in mind the women working on land and in factories. The particular style allowed them to retain their modesty as they had to bend down to work. In the 60s, Marilyn Monroe donned one with a belt and shirt tucked right in and starred in the movie called The Misfits. You probably don’t need us telling you how well the look was accepted and followed. Most of us still wear it the Monroe way even today. Banavalikar-Kulkarni makes note, “In the 90s, high-waisted jeans were worn with crop tops and that’s come as-is as a trend now. You can just pull over an open shirt for daily wear.”The brand Guess made denim all the more popular with its campaigns starring Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell, Drew Barrymore, and the late Anna Nicole Smith. High-waisted denim is being offered in a lot of different washes and styles which is why most everybody succumbed to the trend. Full speed to 2018 and a quick peep to today’s fashion scenario and you would notice how so many people are embracing the high-waisted trend. Style guide: You really cannot go wrong with this piece of clothing. Not only does it make you look curvier, it also makes you look slimmer, curvy and tall. Easy to wear, and low-maintenance is what makes them a must-have. “Denims emphasize the curves so well; they look graceful,” informs Molo. Wearing a dark wash denim with a white V-neck and some hoops makes you look oh-so-sassy and effortless; throw in some tan handbag and nude blocks and you are ready to kill! Pair it off with a bling bralette and you’ve got your Saturday night OTTN ready! Try heading to the workplace in a pair with a satin floral shirt with these denims and be ready to nail the Friday dressing OOTD! Hues of black, white and sand dominated her apparels along with dramatic stripes. Designer Nikasha’s collection was dominated by the gold-foil print on beautiful tones of gold, red and white. Day 3 of Amazon India Fashion Week saw designer Abhi Singh display his collection which consisted of collared dresses in muted tones. Day 4, the last day of AIFW saw designer Shruti Sancheti display layered fashion in her latest collection. There was a explosion of different patterns in her outfits. Designer Kanika Goyal showcased some edgy outfits on the ramp in a mix of pastel and vibrant hues. We might be able to tell you which type you are, only based on your fashion choices! Yes, it’s really that simple. Take the quiz and find out. 1. You need to make a solid first impression on a blind date. What do you do? a) You head to the mall with a clear idea of what your ensemble will be, with backups in case you don’t find what you’re looking for.b) You look through your closet, pick out clothes that will work, but shop for new accessories that will up the glam. c) You put together a look using your favourites from your closet. The idea of a date is to get to know the real you, right?  2. Which of these phrases best describes your wardrobe?a) Organised and filled with sensible separatesb) Timeless and covering a wide range of stylesc) Eclectic and full of colour 3. How do you usually shop for new clothes or accessories? a) You make a list of things you need and adhere to it strictlyb) You head out with an open mind and buy a few things that you really likec) You buy EVERYTHING you see on impulse! 4. How much time would you say you spend getting ready?a) You’re always the one that’s ready first. You don’t need much time if you know what you’re doing. b) It depends on the occasion. You take minutes for a casual outing but hours for a wedding. c) You’re notoriously (and unapologetically) late because you don’t step out until you’ve changed three times. 5. If you find someone wearing the same outfit as you, how do you react?a) You get annoyed and want to make sure that you’re pulling off the look better than them.b) You’re not a fan of the idea, so you spend the day avoiding being seen next to them.c) You’re #Twinning! This calls for a selfie! Mostly As  Type A Personality: Type As are ambitious and proactive. You love planning ahead and go over and above what is expected of you. The fact that you put so much time and effort into everything you do means that you’re fiercely competitive, and sometimes invite unnecessarily stressful situations. You’ve probably been called a control freak before, and you know the title is well deserved. You pride yourself in your ability to be organised, on time and efficient. Mostly Bs  Somewhere in between: You are all about adapting to circumstances. Falling on neutral ground between competitive and laidback, you are well-adjusted and change your approach based on what is called for. You are capable of being both a fearless leader and a willing team player. When you commit to something, you go all in, but you also know when it’s time to take a step back and detach yourself from a situation.  Mostly Cs  Type B Personality: You’re relaxed and believe in going with the flow. You are the kind of person to stop to smell the roses, and are known to enjoy the little things. People often mistake your laidback nature for inefficiency, but you know you can get things done without stressing yourself out. You’re not so much about the results as you are about the process, which is why you are good at tasks that require creativity and innovation. We demystify the main types so you can pull them off like the women of Bollywood.GinghamGingham is one of the most common variants you can wear. It’s a basic, evenly-sized checkered pattern with no more than two colours. While it’s most commonly used on shirts, you could also pair matching separates like this bandeau-skirt combo on Alia Bhatt.Play with the size of the print for different results, like this mini-check jacket on Bhumi Pednekar.Windowpane checksWindowpane checks are exactly what they sound like – thin, spaced out checks that form a graph-like pattern. Since they’re subtle, they work great when you’re wearing print-on-print, like this checked blouse and striped sari on Jacqueline Fernandez.Vidya Balan sports the thicker variant of the windowpane check in this Kanjeevaram sari.Bend the rules and wear dotted checks instead of stripes like this cropped top on Tamannaah Bhatia.TartanTraditionally used for Scottish kilts, tartan is formed with unequally-sized checks, in two or more colours. Sonakshi Sinha wears a tartan slip dress over a plain white tee for a casual ensemble.This gathered-waist tartan skirt on Sonam Kapoor pays tribute to the original Scot kiln.If you’re looking for something more feminine, this tartan off-shoulder dress on Huma Qureshi is a good place to start.
