The final day of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 gave an indication of what’s going to impact your sartorial choices in spring and summer. Take a look. RufflesSpring catwalks around the world are cascading with ruffles and the Capital wasn’t an exception. While Rina Dhaka included the frilly detail in her saris, kurtas and dresses at the finale, Ashish N Soni juxtaposed them on clean and classic silhouettes to make his ready-to-wear line look young, fun and sensuous. Flash dance shoulderThis is an evolution of the off shoulder trend. Designer Sulakshana Monga adapted the peekaboo treatment for her clothes, flash dance or the ‘accidental’ shoulder show that reveals a little flesh without showing too much was a predominant trend. Monga used Half-on, half-off tops and dresses with single ruffled shoulders exposing only a slice of skin. If you wear this, keep the rest of the outfit simple and let your shoulder do the talking. Sheer fabricSheer fabrics such as chiffon, tulle, mesh, organza and chanderi have been summer staples for long and they made an impactful appearance on the runway at the Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018. From hemlines, tops with sheer insets, skirts and dresses at Monga’s to sheer in Indian wear--embellished sheer lehengas and blouses and saris at the Suneet Varma’s show--the trend was ubiquitous. Traditional embroideryIndian culture and craftsmanship were both profusely showcased on the ramp via traditional motifs and intricate embroideries. From thread embroidery at Pankaj and Nidhi, Krishna Mehta and Charu Parashar to intricate zardozi embroidery seen at Suneet Varma’s show, this ethnic element is here to stay though the silhouettes may vary from western contemporary to Indian. Day four of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 saw an abundance of clashing prints, all-white ensembles, dramatic hemlines and statement sleeves. Here’s a round up of the trends that is sure to get your attention: Shades of whiteMany shades of white were spotted on the runway. They offered a stark contrast to the multitude of prints and colours. From Madhu Jain, Kavita Bhartia to Abhi Singh and Ekta Jaipuria and Ruchira Kandhari paired white with white in their collections. If you’re not big on white-on-white, add a few loose fitted casual styles from Payal Jain, frilly and flirty skirts from Kavita Bhartia or a few traditional cotton kurtas from Madhu Jain to your wardrobe and mix and match it with other colours. Shirts under spaghetti strapsStylistas Kim Kardashian and Kendall and Kylie Jenner have been doing this for a while now and designers Dhruv Kapoor and Abhi Singh seemed to have got the drift. Models sashayed down the ramp wearing risqué spaghetti dresses and tank tops over shirts in different sizes and shapes. So ladies, it’s time to bring out your slinky dresses. Print on printThe runway saw an abundance of clashing patterns and prints, proving that this trend for the brave will be big in the upcoming season. While Shivan and Narresh had matching top and bottom sets with prints boasting of forest sights, Dhruv Kapoor matched ditsy florals with vintage prints. Exaggerated sleevesThis is one of the biggest trends for spring summer. And there are so many different types of statement sleeves to suit different types of arms. From billowy bell shaped, ultra long and oversized to ruffled, cinched at the wrist to exaggerated cuffs, there’s enough to last you more than one season. Asymmetrical hemlinesEverything isn’t straight and narrow for summers, designers played with geometry and courted the asymmetrical hemlines in myriad ways. Anju Modi brought the mullet back in fashion—her kurtas had hemlines that were short at the front and long in the back. Meanwhile, Kavita Bhartia, Dhruv Kapoor and Bhanuni by Jyoti experimented with the handkerchief hemline.																		Summery trenches, feminine florals, restrained monochromes and classic plaids, were trending on day 3 of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018.  Lay the trenchesThe summer trench coat is going to be one wardrobe classic in the coming season. The classic trench coat was exquisitely upgraded with thread embroidery by Payal Pratap, deconstructed and made feminine with floral prints by Shruti Sancheti and kept sombre with single tones by Pallavi Dhyanee. Flower powerFloral prints are no longer a surprise for summer, but next season brings big blossoms in all kinds of styles as seen at Shruti Sancheti, Payal Pratap and Pallavi Singhee shows. Pratimaa Pandey, however, used it judiciously by decorating the hems and necklines with floral embroidery. Black and white worldMonochrome is one of the strongest trends this spring summer season. Designers Abraham & Thakore, Rajesh Pratap Singh and Medha Khosla of Anomaly championed the stark black and white contrast. The two shades were interpreted in abstract and clashing prints, stripes and panels. Get creative and work the trend by opting for block separates, a monochrome dress or a monochrome print.  Woven handloomsWoven handlooms are clearly the fabric of the future. With sustainable fashion topping the agenda of most designers, an urban sensitivity was introduced to the fabric. From clean, minimalist work wear to luxurious day and evening wear, handlooms found an easy expression in the spring summer lines of Anomaly, Rajesh Pratap Singh, Abraham and Thakore and Payal Pratap.  Plaid and simplePlaids had a major moment on the runaway of day 3. Checked patterns have been a winter favourite for long, but designers such as Payal Pratap, and Teresa Liasom and Utsav Pradhan of Munkee See and Munkee Do and Pallavi Dhyani gave it fun and colourful interpretation for spring. But Rajesh Pratap Singh decided to keep it staid by taking the conventional way for his shirts, jackets and trousers.																		The collections showcased on day 2 of Amazon India fashion Week SS/18 seemed to have comfort on the top of their priority list. Rimzim Dadu infused metallic hues in silver, gold and blue into her range of re-imagined saris, sculpted statement tops jackets and skater dresses. If you aren’t sure of metallic outfits, begin with accessories. A hint of metallic is sure to get you noticed. Sorbet coloursPassionate pastels or sorbet shades have been making quite a wave on international runways and they made a strong appearance in Anupama Dayal’s show. She used lilacs, lavender, melons and sunset hues on gossamer and light fabrics such as chiffons and Chanderis. A deviation from the pop and neon colours, these shades will add a breath of fresh air to your summer wardrobe. Shoulder obsessionFashion’s fascination with shoulders rages on. As the growing popularity of cruise shows indicates, between Instagram-worthy beach escapes, destination weddings and glamping, resort fashion has indeed come a long way. Whether you’re reclining on sun loungers or cruising over gorgeous landscapes in a hot air balloon, there’s no excuse to look sloppy anymore, especially when you travel. While the island state of mind is just that—a state of mind—the allure of a glorious coverup, a feather-light kaftan or one of those hand-woven, basket totes is real, palpable and, suddenly, everywhere.  Spring/summer 2017 runways are proof that resortwear can go well beyond throw-on-and-go pieces. Take Miu Miu’s retro Italy-inspired collection, which comprise a line of ruched bikinis, patterned robe-style dresses and teensy twinsets, accompanied by embossed pool slides and appliqued swim caps. Miuccia Prada understands the value of a chic escape. “It’s a celebration of summer and its pleasures,” she mused during the post-show interview. Dolce & Gabbana also sought inspiration from the Italian tropics for its covered sundresses, bralets and miniskirts in fun prints (think pasta, seafood and gelato). The show venue even had a counter serving fresh tender coconut water and models strutted down the runway to the rhythms of the tarantella. Giorgio Armani presented a line of slouchy bloomers, sheer cover-ups and short suits, featuring painterly prints and tassels—just what we need for those soirées under the stars. The accessories followed suit; the flatforms at Prada and Chloé would make for stylish accoutrements on a holiday. For their spring/summer 2017 collection, Delhi-based designer duo Hemant and Nandita elevated holiday basics like swimsuits, shorts, crop tops and sarong-esque skirts using Victorian ruffles and vibrant print play. Nishka Lulla set out to reinvent the pantsuit, working with softer fabrics and delicate embellishments to transform it into a resort essential. Lulla says, “I used lightweight, everyday materials like cotton and tulle in relaxed comfy silhouettes, with frills and flounces thrown in for good measure.” Aparna Badlani, curator and co-owner of multi-designer boutique Atosa, Mumbai, has long recognised the potential of well-made resortwear. “At a point when destination weddings are such a huge phenomenon, the category is finally getting its due,” she says. If there’s one image that captures the exquisite charm of travel, it’s got to be that of actor and socialite Talitha Getty hanging out on the terrace of her Marrakech home, immortalised by photographer Patrick Lichfield in the late ’60s.  It even inspired Yves Saint Laurent to design a line of kaftans that he called Une Passion Marocaine. Designer and TV personality Nicole Richie, who has a perpetual vacation vibe about her, best embodies this spirit today. Her style reminiscent of LA’s boho-luxe aesthetic from the ’60s and the ’70s. Whether it’s through pictures of Taylor’s Swift’s glamorous squad chilling together on a yacht or Olivia Palermo and beau Johannes Huebl’s romantic romp in Greece, travel continues to fire our imagination and inform fashion in the most powerful ways.  Much like with eveningwear, building a bankable resortwear wardrobe takes work. “Start with the basics and build from there. Think kaftans, palazzos, shorts, day dresses and strappy sandals,” says Badlani. According to Lulla, the trick is to invest in lightweight, versatile separates that can be paired with other items from your wardrobe. “Take, for instance, bustiers that you can wear on the beach or with high-waisted bottoms for a night out,” she says. It’s always a good idea to mix luxe pieces with exotic finds from local boutiques and markets to create a look that is uniquely yours. Abaya is an outer garment worn by Muslim women. It also called burqa in certain countries. This garment is a long robe or cloak, which covers the body except for head, feet, and hands. The traditional abayas are black in colour. But now, these abayas have now got a fashion makeover.    The women, who are style savvy women and love to boast the tradition and trend can try the updated versions. We got in touch with LimeRoad's fashion stylist, Rina S Walia to talk about the new styles:   1. Denim love The long denim abaya is the best for the all-denim look. This can be paired with printed or solid cotton head scarf for any easy outdoor look. Add a pop of colour, by carrying a neon sling bag.    2. Pick the Pleats Pleats are always going to be on trend. Try a black one with colourful pleats at the bottom. Complete the look with a pair of pumps and a black sling bag.     3. Pretty pastels Pastel shades have become the talk of the town. Try a beautiful pastel pink abaya as the go-to attire for days when you want to look effortlessly stylish.    4. Cape Craze Capes are totally ruling the ramps this season. Don't lag! Wear a cape abaya and tune up your feminine charm. It's perfect for summer day outs.     (Abaya images: Limeroad.com)  Gabriela Hearst: Gabriela Hearst is a true-blue Instagram success story. The clothes were a mix of billowing silhouettes, couture, and all the summer hues.    (All images: PTI) One of the most definitive trends for fall is the return of shine on the runways. As designers get nostalgic for the flamboyant ’80s, sequins go gangsta and shiny vinyl finds its way back into our closet. This season sparkle comes imbued with a street sensibility as the more-is-more mantra from our favourite decade clashes with athleisure’s fluid dynamism. Cue the season’s sharpest plissé skirts teamed with a pair of equally luxe sneakers. Designers drummed up a host of options that make an easy transition from the cubicle to the dance floor. We’re looking to Michael Kors’ slashed sequinned mini dresses and Phoebe Philo’s egg-shaped lurex pullovers at Céline for inspiration. “I like bare legs in winter; I like night for day. I like Alexa Chung mixing with Nan Kempner. It’s about the interesting mix,” said Kors in an interview post his show. At Kenzo, Humberto Leon and Carol Lim sent out a line of vinyl dresses and skirts, foil-print trousers and oversized metallic jackets. Isabel Marant flirted with vinyl too in retro styles, adding animal prints and plaid to the mix. “It really goes back to when I would sneak out, aged 15, to punk clubs like Le Palace and Les Bains Douches,” said the Parisian designer. Between Marc Jacobs’ subversive separates at NYFW and Rajesh Pratap Singh’s gilded army closer home, the message is loud and clear—street glamour is here to stay. Designer Sanchita Ajjampur’s futuristic mash of foil, mesh and paillettes, and Gaurav Jai Gupta’s street-style spin on metallic handlooms, further confirm the mood of the times. It’s evident that fashion is making no bones about its Ziggy Stardust-meets-Beyoncé philosophy, and the pop culture influencers are lapping it up. Historically, the first image that comes to mind in this category is that of  ’60s fashion icon and rocker Keith Richards’s then girlfriend Anita Pallenberg who took to the Cannes red carpet in a lurex jumper. Leave it to the Kardashian-Jenner clan to reinvent Pallenberg’s louche luxe uniform as they elevate street style basics like sweatshirts, lace-up boots and trackpants. Kendall Jenner even brought back the chainmail dress from the ’90s. Closer home Alia Bhatt is having a go with unexpected pairings like a camo shirt and a plissé skirt, offering us a fresh take on the trend.      Which brings us to the question of how to do it right. Archana Walavalkar, celebrity stylist and co-founder Stylecracker, says that styling is everything here. “It’s important to blend the look seamlessly, not letting the shiny piece acquire hero status at any point.” It’s a good idea to stock up on basics like hologram sweatshirts, sequinned numbered tees, slip dresses with a glamorous sheen, and metallic denims. If you’re shine-shy, begin with a statement accessory. Let the gleaming heels from Demna Gvasalia’s debut at Balenciaga or Fendi’s festive-edition gold totes give you some ideas. “Go casual with jeans and a tee teamed with embellished sandals. This is easier to pull off if you don’t quite dare to go all guns blazing,” says Ajjampur. Fine jewellery is also following suit by putting a casual spin to sparkle. Case in point: Nirav Modi’s Embrace range of diamond bangles, which stretch like a dream, offer a snug fit and are best worn with denims and a boyfriend shirt. The writing’s on the wall: Whatever your glittery vice may be, it’s time to wear it on your sleeve.   Wendell Rodricks is a man credited with many firsts. At a time when Indian fashion was all about opulence and grandeur, he introduced the idea of minimalism. He was one of the few Indian designers to bring eco-friendly textiles to the forefront and also pioneered resortwear in India. To commemorate his contributions to the fashion industry, Rodricks was awarded the Padma Shri title in 2014. While contemporaries are predictably passing on their legacies and labels to family members, the designer has entrusted it into the hands of young prodigy Schulen Fernandes. And he did it in his inimitable style, bang in the middle of the runway at his label's fall/winter showing at the 2016 Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW). In a fun, free-wheeling chat, Rodricks and Fernandes tell us about what's in store for the legendary label.Wendell, after holding the reins for 28 years, you've decided to hand them over to Schulen. Schulen, how did he break it to you and what was your reaction?Wendell Rodricks: I always wanted the label to go to somebody I trusted. Schulen came to me straight from college and she has been with me for four years. She had already started taking a lot of creative decisions for the label. For instance, last season we did the Indica Emporia presentation at LFW with vintage Indian garments. It was completely her vision and work from start to end. I wanted to slowly take the backseat with this label so that I could make time for my other passions. I felt the time was just right for her to take the label and fly with it.Schulen Fernandes: It obviously didn't happen out of the blue. The handover was always on the cards and it took two years of work laying the foundation. However, when the actual moment arrived, it was hard to believe. How are your roles divided in the new scheme of things?WR: I’d like to think of myself as a benevolent dictator (laughs). On a serious note, Schulen has complete freedom to realise her creative vision at the label now and I am happy to have her take over.SF: Wendell will obviously be the mentor. My work will now involve everything from conceptualising collections to actually bringing it to life. I am also excited about the business end of it and we have a competent team to help us on that front.Schulen, tell us a little bit about your debut collection, Trapezoid, for the Wendell Rodricks label presented at LFW. And, Wendell, what did you think of it?SF: I have always loved architecture and geometry. The trapezoid form has been used in architecture from ancient times and it is so versatile. We decided to explore it in fashion with this collection. We used a mix of structured shapes and fluid fabrics working with paper silks, chanderis and a lot of eco-friendly materials. WR: I was really surprised when Schulen came up with the idea. It is a form that I've seen in Inca and Aztec architecture and in our temple gopurams. The Indian woman's body which is narrow at the shoulders and wide at the hips also follows the trapezoid form. This was particularly relevant because for the first time we introduced a size chart specific to the Indian woman at LFW this season. I felt really proud watching the show. The biggest compliment to me and to Schulen was when people told us it (the collection) looked like Wendell Rodricks. When a new creative leader takes charge at a fashion house, change is afoot—what can we expect from the label?WR: I've always focussed on high-end fashion and have never been able to cater to the mid-range. I hope Schulen will be able to expand the reach of this label to more people the way my colleague Anita Dongre has done very successfully. I also want her to take risks with the label and be more experimental.SF: We will definitely retain the minimalistic language and eco-friendly DNA of the label as we move forward. I would like to introduce newer, younger silhouettes and experiment heavily with materials. What lies ahead for both of you? Wendell, do you miss being behind the wheel? Schulen, are you at all daunted?WR: I don’t miss being behind the wheel at all. I can finally dedicate time to things that I’ve been waiting to do. The work on the museum is underway (Rodricks is turning his Goa home into a space dedicated to Goan costumes). The dogs are taking it well but my three cats are giving me grief about the move! I would like to write a lot more. My next book Poskem is about Goa. I hope I’ll be able to turn it into a movie like Chetan Bhagat (laughs). I’d like to teach a lot more too.SF: I am excited about what lies ahead and loving every minute of my new job. You can convert this to a day look by wearing a more subtle jacket. With a trench: Like Kim Kardashian. She dressed in Balenciaga from head to toe at the Paris Fashion Week in a belted trench and a pair of bondage style leather boots. A kurta is not only comfortable to wear but looks oh-so-chic, especially if there is a design element that adds to the look. The asymmetric style gives it an edgy look. Add some bangles and finger rings and you're set.Makeup: Rosy glow makeup would look perfect with this. Round hoops at your ears and chunky bangles will complete the look.Makeup: To compliment this look we would suggest mauve accents as a preferred makeup looks. What to wear for Diwali Diwali is the time to celebrate with your family. It is also about celebrating our colorful traditions and vibrant culture. However, what you choose to wear should stem out from your idea of âÂÂâÂÂcomfort. If you're comfortable in salwar-kameer or sari or a pant-suit or shorts, you should totally rock it with all your confidence, and fashion and trends would follow! 2. Which dress code fits for the Diwali festival? Ideally, people generally prefer wearing traditional outfits like saris, lehengas and salwar-kameer. There are several other varieties of ethnic outfits from regional areas that can be totally your pick this Diwali. If you're celebrating the festival at home, you can go for something that gives you comfort and mobility as well as style. However, if you're spending this festive time outside the home, you can try new trends and styles like ethnic pants, dhoti salwar, among others. Our advice would be to blend comfort and fashion to have a great time. 3. Is it ok to wear a black color dress on Diwali? Several people in Indian people believe that black should not be picked up to wear on Diwali day. Independently, you can decide to wear the color that you want. But, the festive feeling is all about joy and celebration with your loved ones. It's best if you take advice from a family member to avoid hurting any sentiments on this auspicious day. Take a moment and reminisce about the days when we would send out anxious messages to our gang asking them about their outfits. What they were donning for the night? What if our outfits matched? The horror! These momentous precautions have a taken a back seat with changing times.  Matching outfits with your friend is no more a faux pas. Instead, it has become a raging and super fun trend that is here to stay! Twinning as a trend first emerged in South Korea’s K-pop culture. While coordinating your outfits completely is not an anomaly entirely, it can overpower the essence of your real personality and make you look, umm, a little too alike. But hey! We’ve got you covered. Have a look at these simple tips and tricks to ace the twinning game. Go ahead and make that winning statement with your fashion twin! One colour palette, multiple outfitsThis is a great way to flaunt the twin-win look without being too discernible. No worries even if you and bestie have different taste when it comes to styling your clothes. The main idea is to predominantly stay within the same colour palette and explore varied outfits. Think Gigi Hadid’s and Kendal Jenner’s iconic twin ensembles Match your fabricsHere’s an easy breezy example to help you get a better idea about this tip.  You can wear a chic eyelet white cotton dress with and your twin can throw on a white top having a similar eyelet detail. Dressing in tandem with your friend in this way leaves a lot of room for experimentation.  Top to bottom! Bottom to top!Interchanging the colours of your outfit with your BFF can be really fun. Fancy sporting a cute baby pink skirt with a pastel blue top? Your BFF, on the other hand, can rock a baby pink top with a pastel blue skirt. Think out of the boxWhat’s the first thing that comes to your mind when you think about twinning? Matching your garbs, right? While this is the most popular choice, there are some other subtle ways in which you can strut your way into the twin parade. How about getting matching phone covers? You are your fashion twin will be carrying around your phone pretty much everywhere. Bring out those accessories There are a myriad of ways in which you can elevate your twinning game without synchronizing your outfits from head to toe. Add a pair of matching oxidized tribal jhumkas to your ensemble for that subtle yet classy twinning look.  So there you have it! Your very own handy guide which will aid you in conquering this super-fun trend. Lastly, we would just want to remind you that twinning is not about replicating each other’s clothes. Don’t strive to look identical! It is one thing to twin your outfit with a person and another to look like their clone. Maintaining your identity is of crucial importance. Reflect on of your personal sense of style. Ensure that your individual personality shines through your matching outfit. A lot is shouldered by the details therein. The aim is not to look like identical twins. You want to alike but different. You can wear the same shirt but pair it up with different bottoms. Wear dresses with a similar length but different prints. Yes, twinning can be that effortless. She had a Cinderella moment, where the ‘fairy godfather’ flicked his wand, and the black and blue gown by Tommy Hilfiger lit up in blue! This was made possible with technology; the structure inside the dress was made up of metallic plates, LED lights, batteries and wire. At the same event, musician Janelle Monáe wore an exaggerated Christian Siriano balloon-hipped dress that had a motorised blinking eye on one breast! It’s not just the celebs that get to wear such high-tech ensembles, even daily wear is getting its fair share of technological advancement. Wrist-worn smart watches or bands have become common in recent years. But, according to a research carried out by UK-based Juniper Research, the trend is shifting to ‘connected clothing’, which is forecasted by them to become $1 billion industry in 2020! Here are some of such cool garments that you can choose from.Jacket phone: What if you could pick up calls, control music volume, and get directions by just taping or brushing the sleeves? Research is also being done on how else to incorporate technology into fashion in order to make our life easier. At Deakin University’s Institute for Frontier Materials, they’re looking into developing fibres that can store energy. They’re hoping to make garments that can be used to charge phones and other small devices. Imagine slipping your discharged phone into your pocket, and it comes out charged! You’ll be shedding those heavy jackets and coats and finally be able to show off the latest trends in fashion as you step out. Here’s looking at the trends this season that will have you turn heads. While the previous year was all sorts of the frivolous extravaganza, this year is more about practical functionality with a generous dollop of extra. Animal printsAnimal prints started making the rounds of runways sometime early last year and in filtered into our closets in full force by the end of the year. The predatory prints from the ’80s had made a massive comeback but with the much-needed makeover! The well-known prints are so much chic and oh so covetable now. What was once considered a bold statement for the wild-hearted is now being sported at ease by the shy too. Cheetah, leopard, snake, zebra, you name it and the print is available at your go-to an e-commerce site. Styling an animal print is a little tricky as you do not want to look like you belong to the circus! Steer clear of heavy fabrics like wools and velvets and opt for smooth and silky outfits such as silks and cotton. Start with a skinny leopard printed bodysuit and boyfriend jeans with boots and work your way up to a snakeskin evening gown with strappy black heels and minimalistic jewellery and you’re all set.  Utility dressingRemember days you were looked down upon for leaving your house in oversized sweats and cargo pants? Well, it turns out that you can proudly flaunt your baggy cargo pants and sneaks this year, all thanks to the utility dressing rage! Welcome to 2019 where function meets fashion in the form of unpolished practicality. It is nothing but practical, laid back and super comfortable clothing. 2019 has functionality written all over it. Imagine practical oversized clothing in muted tones. Combat trousers, chic overalls, trench coats, baggy sweats, sneakers are taking the fashion world with a storm and we aren’t complaining one bit. The key to nailing the perfect utility look is to style the pieces. If you haven’t experimented yet, start with styling functional clothing with tailored pieces. Start with layering an army jacket over a solid black jumpsuit or playsuit with black boots and move ahead. Also, you can jazz up your khaki trench coat with a red lip and a silk scarf for the perfect date look or can sport those ‘ugly’ trainers with a sleep skirt suit at work and be practical, comfortable and oh so chic at the same time. Win-win!  Cycling shortsCycling shorts are nothing new; in fact, Princess Diana regularly sported them with crew necks long ago. Fast forward to 2019, and they are easily the biggest trend of the year. They were unmissable on the runaways and have been marking territory in online and offline stores in abundance. And not, not just in the regular black spandex garment we’ve grown up with but jazzed up in pretty colours and prints and embroidery. It goes without saying that the humble piece of sportswear has graduated the fashion ladder by heaps and how. The garment that was once worn for physical activities is now being sported under blazers to the boardroom. And oh, it is Kim Kardashian approved too! Women all across the globe have taken a fancy for these bodycon shorts and are pairing it off with anything and everything. From boardrooms to date nights to soirees, these shorts are hard to miss. You too could dip your toes in the water by the pairing of a solid coloured one with a loose oversized tee for your regular coffee runs and upgrade by sporting metallic ones underneath blingy long blazers. It isn’t clear on if the trend is here to stay or not, but that doesn’t stop it from being everywhere at the moment! Oversized2019 revolves around the word oversized! From oversized unstructured jackets and t-shirts to oversized huge sunnies and hats, there’s no stopping really! (Yep, that means we would have to put away our skinny sunglasses from last season!) While last season was more sleek and minimal in terms of accessories, this season is all about exaggeration in terms of hats, belts, bags, etc. The tote bag has gotten a makeover and has blown out really big! Loud hair bands- studded, leather, satin etc too seem to have maximized. Sunglasses are big and bold with added adornments. Chunky jewellery in a more natural form rather than being polished would be a hit this year. Belts too are broad and oversized. 80’s fashionThe thumb rule of fashion is that each trend resurfaces after a few years. There are some that we can’t stand and some we welcome with open arms, like the 80’s fashion. The retro fashion has gotten a redo and we can’t wait to see it on the streets. Imagine belted high waist denim and power suits in neon (remember Priyanka Chopra?) and fringed mullets and big hair. Puffy sleeves, ruffles and shoulder pads are more fashionable than you thought. Although the style is more refined and structured than what it was before. Shoulder pads blazers mean business and are definitely not going anywhere for a long time. Ruffles trims tops and dress continue selling like hot cakes. Statement sleeves too are in the running. Expect to see a lot more of the 80’s fashion this year! Text by Ravina SachdevImages by Yogen Shah Some of the colour trends of the year, ruling the ramps and streets alike, are fiesta (red-orange), jester red, turmeric, living coral, pink peacock, pepper stem (yellow-green) and Aspen gold. Bipasha Basu Singh GroverIn Falguni Mehta.					 It’s time for all of us to make a resolution to not fall prey to body figure stereotyping and make it all about self-love. Not trying to hide behind frumpy clothes that do you no justice is one way to do that. Finding out and understanding your body type is something to be thankful for, however making it a stereotype is not. So all the apple body-shaped woman, pear body-shaped and also the full-sized hourglass body-shaped ladies, stop being used to the embarrassing yourself, rather start embracing yourself! With numerous brands breaking the beauty taboo with real-body campaigns and policies we celebrate every woman with perfection. If you are curvy, it is important to dress according to your size. Say goodbye to every oversized clothes and slide into the outfits with the right fit that will hide your problem areas and highlight the right angles of your frame. Styling from top to bottom can bring a vast change in your look. Have a look at some great style tips for real girls who felt too voluptuous to wear certain items, and we're here to blow those myths right out of the water. LINES AND SHAPES You need your first impression to be fab-worthy, and it is all about your lines and shapes that draw the eye. One great trick is to wear monochrome ensembles. This makes the viewer’s eye move up to down, or vice versa, forming one uninterrupted line, which makes you look tall and slim. If you’re looking to enhance those curves, then opt for a bodycon dress in the right fabric like jersey. You can also wear ensembles that have lines narrowing at the waist and spreading away at the bust and the hips. The lines can be in the form of a print, stitches, pleats, etc. A dress with a plunging V-neck and a cinched waist which then flairs out below, also gives the illusion of an hourglass figure.  THE RULE OF THE HEM Knowing where hems or borders should be on your body can help you lengthen the frame. A knee-length skirt, for example, should sit just right under the knee, never around the biggest part of the calf.  The hem of the jeans should be at the ankle, or (even better) an inch or two below. If you are not of average height, buy your clothes, specifically the bottoms from a retailer that gives you perfect length options. Well, hems can be tricky sometimes but the best thing is to not to have a clue about it and find a tailor with a good eye, trust them and learn as you go.  SAY 'NO' TO OVERSIZED CLOTHES Just beanpoles look great in larger than the average dress size! Don’t add volume to your body by wearing oversized dresses. Instead, pick the clothes that are body-skimming (not too tight) and show your curvy side. Say no to a giant t-shirt, but a maxi or kaftans that skim the curves and have some belt at the waist is cool. If you want an easy profile, or if you got your favourite graphic on a tee or tunic then pair it with tighter trousers or jeans and make it to your advantage. MIND THE SHOES It’s always a head-to-toe thing and what you put on your feet that matters. Pointy tips and low heels can make you look slim, whether you are pairing it with a skirt or a pair of pants. Try to find a shoe with a vamp the ends at the top of your toes, other than halfway around. Shoe styles with low vamps include ballet flats and pumps. High-vamp shoes include Mary Janes and loafers. WHAT NOW, ACCESSORIES? Long chains, not chokers are good to go, especially if you got classic apple shape and short neck. Your focus should be on creating long, unbroken lines along your body. No mood of jewellery? Grab a long scarf helps for the same effect. Layering your jewellery is another way of drawing the eye vertically. From choker to long chains, layer with a couple of them together. Even when wearing bangles and bracelets, stack them up.  VOTE FOR LAYERS Contrary to stereotypes, layering doesn’t necessarily add volume. Instead, it sometimes gives your body a definition. Wearing a tank top with a pretty cardigan instead of one-piece dress or T-shirt can help to underline your shape.  Ensure though that you don’t layer with bulky garments.  EMBRACE YOUR HIGH WAIST High-waisted pants are your companion. They help tuck in folds and fat and minimize muffin tops since they end at the slimmest part of the waist. Ensure they're long, finishing at the lower leg or underneath, following the rule of the hemline.  Dress to make yourself feel good, and you will make heads turn!  Text: Akruti Khandkar 													Step into summers with a fresh hair style to set the tone of the season right. Swara BhaskerIn a Mango dress.					 Winters see you bring out those old boots and show them the light of the day. Only issue: You’ve worn them a number of times last season and they just don’t feel that special anymore. How you wish your boots had some colour or a fringe or even a shiny buckle. Sigh! Fret not. With some easy fix tricks, you can upgrade your boots to the latest fashion trends of this season and always stay in style! Buckle up!What you need: Belts, scissors, hot glue.How to make: Cut your belt measured according to the roundness of your boot at the calf. Use hot glue to attach your belt onto your boot. Hold it in place and let it dry. Cut off any unwanted extra belt length and buckle it around your boot. Add extra notches if required. You can repeat the same procedure using more belts with different colours or textures and you have your very own cowgirl boots! Cool cutsWhat you need: Ruler, penknife, chalk.How to make: Draw or trace the design of your choice onto your boot using chalk. Size your grid according to your liking. Use the pen knife to cut out the parts you wish to keep hollow. Once done, wipe off the chalk marks with a damp cloth and you cut out boots are ready. This DIY is easier to work with semi-thick leather that won’t lose shape or tear after cutting. Dazzling tipsWhat you need: Paintbrush, gold/silver pearl shine paint, a thick masking tape, fixative sprayHow to make: Add masking tape a few centimetres away from the tip of the boot. Press firmly. Paint using the gold or silver paint making sure the paint doesn’t go under the tape. Paint smooth and even coats to get a smooth surface. Allow it to dry for a couple of hours and remove the tape. Wipe off any stray dried up paint. Spray on the fixative spray and let it dry for 24 hours. And voila! Lace all dayWhat you need: Lace, pins (if required) and fabric glue.How to make: Cut strips of lace that is long enough to go around your boot. Arrange your pattern and pin it so it holds your desired shape. Using tiny amounts of glue, attach it to your boot. Let it dry completely. You can even add a few beaded chains and feathers for a complete boho look. Retro kicksWhat you need: Masking tape, matte finish paint, brush, scissors.How to make: Cut pieces of the masking tape and stick them onto your boot in any desired shape. You can make a star shape or go abstract and stick the tape onto your boot in any way you like. Once this is done, paint over the design you've created using any matte finish paint of your choice. Let it dry and peel the tape off slowly to reveal your design. Continue making more designs or simply stick the tape in equidistant parallel lines to create stripes for a sporty look.Text: Yvonne Jacob 													The glamour industry revolves around fashion cycles and trends that dominated once, have returned to claim their spot again. After changing three flights and taking a three-hour bus ride, we landed in Montepuez—the second largest city in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique. The day had been a whirlwind, as we hopped on and off different vehicles. The moment we landed in Mozambique, however, a burst of fresh, clean air welcomed us. The quaint city is home to Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM), which is a Mozambican company developing operations at the ruby deposits in the city, and covers approximately 33,600 hectares. A leading supplier of responsibly-sourced coloured gemstones across the globe, MRM is owned by UK-based natural resource company Gemfields (75 per cent), and Mozambican company Mwiriti (25 per cent). We spent two days in the heart of the most recently discovered ruby deposit in the world, and unearthed more than just these precious crimson stones. 													The journey beginsOver 500 million years in the making, ruby, or ratnaraj (meaning king of the gemstones in ancient Sanskrit), is an extremely rare stone, cherished by royalty, social A-listers, and collectors alike. We went to see one of the mine pits on the first day, where rubies are deposited as alluvial or colluvial material over a weathered bedrock.Rubies were first discovered in Montepuez in 2009, following which, Gemfields and Mwiriti signed an agreement in 2011 to officiate the mining process. MRM uses a multidisciplinary approach for mining—geological (rubies that are typically associated with certain rocks or minerals), geophysical (airborne survey—magnetic and radiometric), and geochemical (determining chemical signatures of hidden mineral deposits). The sheer size of the mine pit was staggering, and it brought forth the concern of what happens to it once it has been exhausted.Mining with a conscienceMRM is committed to mining in a way that has the least environmental impact. Jack Cunningham, Sustainability, Policy and Risk Director at Gemfields, explains, “Before we mine an area, we collect seeds of the indigenous plants and trees from the top soil and create a seed bank. We then grow the seeds in a nursery for replanting as we complete mining.” Along with encouraging biodiversity, old pits are back-filled and rehabilitated, and no harmful chemicals are used during the mining process. “Machine oil is carefully managed and stored, machines and vehicles are maintained by our in-house teams, and all spills are cleaned up and the contaminated soil is bioremediated,” says Cunningham.The road to development was not an easy one, and initially, the company faced resistance from the inhabitants. Cunningham recalls, “There was uncertainty from the local community about what the benefits would be and how quickly they would receive those. An influx of thousands of illegal miners also caused social problems at a time when we weren’t yet in a position to help the community. Since 2014, however, we have had a dedicated team on the ground that carries out community engagement, and addresses their needs and grievances, and the relationship with them has vastly improved.” MRM has provided employment to 1,110 people, both directly and via contractors, 95 per cent of whom are Mozambican nationals. The mining company has also helped nine farming associations (two of which are dedicated to empowering women and in total represent 290 partner farmers), and taught them new techniques that have increased yields. Looking at the community as a whole, the company has invested in infrastructure for four primary schools (three of which are new), providing education to 1,000 primary school-aged children. “Schooling is the responsibility of the state, however our infrastructure atleast helps the government with a costly aspect of public education. Once established, we hand over the schools to the government for their onward management as a national asset,” elucidates Cunningham. The establishment of two mobile health clinics serves thousands of people across six villages. Isac Rafael, Director of the Namanhumbir Health Center, Mozambique, stated, “With these mobile clinics, it’s possible to care for patients in the most remote areas without sanitary units. This also gives easy access to pregnant women, children, and the elderly, who don’t have to travel long distances.”The final stepWe spent the last leg of our journey in the wash plant and sorting house, where the raw stones are processed and graded according to their colour, size, and clarity. We witnessed how a team of highly skilled sorters picked rubies from the rubble, in a secure environment. Their hands worked like machines as they separated the precious stones in silent harmony. The final pieces are then auctioned off by Gemfields and till June 2017, a total of eight ruby auctions have generated a revenue of US$280 million.We entered the city with a bunch of preconceived notions, and after spending two days in the shoes of a miner, left with hope for the Montepuez community. That’s what you get in this city of Mozambique, along with beautiful never-ending blue skies, and a warm community that believes in co-existence. FASHIONHigh glossNothing screams power more than high shine fabrics worn appropriately. While last season was all about plastics in apparel, this season is all about high gloss on any and every fabric texture such as leather, satin etc. Right from long wrap-around coats to pants to even see-through dresses, high shine is marking its territory everywhere. But beware if worn out of proportion or styled incorrectly, the trend sure can fall back easily. The best way to start would be with a high shine statement belt on a solid outfit and move upwards to high gloss trimmings on outfits and then take the plunge! “I feel high gloss fabrics can somehow add sheer sexiness to the look. EMPIRE STATE OF MINDEmpire waistlineThe first and most recognisable waistline there is the empire waistline also popularly referred to as the empire silhouette, empire line or just empire style. The basic structure of this waist pattern is categorised by the tightly fitted bodice that ends just below the bust to deliver the whole high-waisted look. The obsession with the high-waisted line began during the 18th century and was brought to fame by the empress of the first French Empire, Napoleon Bonaparte’s wife, Empress Josephine de Beauharnais; which is where the whole regal reference is sourced from. If a style was good enough for an empress, you can be sure it’s good enough for you as well. The entire style is part of the neoclassical style that was obsessed with imitating and replicating or rather reviving the style that could be seen in the ancient Greek and Roman which portrayed women wearing long gowns clinched under the bust.Perhaps it's old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the style a wonderfully romantic appeal. The flowy and really luxurious feel it imparts makes your inner Greek goddess preen with appreciation, accompanied with the fact that it’s incredibly comfy with zero constriction is an advantage that has very women sighing in absolute relief. Its old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the empire waistline style a wonderfully romantic appeal.Match-maker: The empire waist is designed in such a way that it sits above a woman's natural waistline and generally accentuates the bust which is why it is ideally always accompanied with deep scoop necklines or sweetheart and V-necklines.   This style is perfect for those with pear-shaped bodies i.e. having a slim upper body and a more voluptuous lower body. As such if you don’t want to draw attention to your hips then empire waistline is the way to go. The waist tends to emphasise the narrowest part of the body and camouflaging the wider lower body. It’s also great for short people because the raised waistline creates the appearance of extra height. Now, for the don’ts - avoid the billowy, voluminous fabrics. Pleats and gathers are another no-nos.It is best to stick to with A-line structures or sheath that help to highlight your body’s best features instead of hiding it under too much fabric. When wearing an empire waist top, the best choice of bottom wear is either skinny or straight legged pants. Pairing it up with voluminous wide-legged tend it delivers a rather frumpy, disproportionate look. Empire waist dresses are ideal for pregnant women as its flowy and comfortable. DROP DOWNDrop waistAfter the waistline was pulled up to new heights, the winds of change eventually made their way through the world of fashion and according to the laws of the universal: what goes up must come down. So after the waistline enjoyed the lofty highs, during the roaring 20s, it dropped down to become the distinctive dropped waist style. Around the time when women were finally breaking free from a vile instrument of torture also known as the corset, they decided to adopt more masculine silhouettes. It was believed to be seen as female liberation from traditionally-accepted shapes. A dropped waist sits below the actual natural waistline of a woman and is characterised by the line across the hips instead of the waist thereby providing the illusion of a longer torso. The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival. During then the look took on a sportier feel rather than the elegantly sleek feminine look of the 20’s. Designers have experimented around with it for years and while the basic construct was never tampered with, there were several add-ons like belts, pleated and ruffled skirts to give it a little extra something every time.The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival.Match-maker: Dropped waisted looks aren’t quite as popular today as they were before but they haven’t faded into obscurity completely because the whole ‘shapeless’ look is on the prowl and is extremely favoured. The waist makes quite a statement and, if you know just how to wear and accessorise it, it can turn you into an über fashionista who knows how to work any style like a boss. Short drop-waisted look looks fantastic on women with the tall slender willowy figures and narrow hips. With the addition of a ruffled skirt for a flouncy free-flowing look or an A-line skirt for a sleeker formal look, it could swing either way. It would be prudent for women who have a heavier lower half to stay away from the ruffles as it would be super counterproductive and make the lower body look even wider.For those with long legs and a short torso, drop-waisted dress - with moderate heels - works well. And for those with a long torso and short legs, drop waists with high heels will help to balance out the long torso and deliver a balanced, symmetrical look. BASQUE IN ITBasque waistlineWhat could you have in common with a woman who lived during the American Civil War? Nothing much; except maybe your dress’s waistline. The Basque waistline, which is also referred to as the antebellum waistline is a waistline that emerged when the hourglass figure was the shape every woman was vying for. This waistline served to flatter the equally proportioned body of an hourglass shape and has merits for other body types as well.A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures. The style forms a noticeable ‘V’ on the front of the body coming 2-3 inches below the normal waistline. If the pronounced V-shape is too sharp for one’s taste and then the style can also be modified to a softer U-shape. It is a generally flattering style that provides a slimmer and longer torso due to its low ‘V’ and reduces the width of the hips and waist. Though the idea is to love your body no matter what, wanting to take off a couple for inches every now and then using illusionary means is perfectly acceptable. The style originally began as French-fitted bodice or jacket that eventually become part of the dress rather than a separate piece altogether. A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures.Matchmaker: A Basque waistline is flattering for many body shapes; the low V-shaped line lengthens the torso and creates a wonderfully slim silhouette. However, due to the shape of the waistline, the style tends to draw distinct attention to the lower tummy region and if you aren’t comfortable with that then it's best to avoid this style. Pear-shaped bodies or square shaped bodies should not go for this kind of waistline as it would not be able to appropriately accentuate and flatter those kinds of body types. Hourglass and other body types would be able to carry it off perfectly as it helps to balance out the hips and waist due to the elongation illusion the waist creates.   LOSE THE SYMMETRYAsymmetric waistlineThings that are straight and simple are thoroughly uninteresting after a while. In order to shake things up, the fashion industry developed an obsession with everything that was off-centre and unbalanced. And that is because things like that tend to be more interesting. There is more depth, character and visual appeal. From hemlines with varying lengths to slanted necklines, there is something about asymmetrical patterns in an attire that just make the whole look more sophisticated and bold while breaking free from the rigid symmetry.Though an asymmetrical waistline is not as radical as some of the other things in the same school of thought, it is an interesting style to incorporate. An asymmetrical waistline is a style that sits diagonally across the natural waistline. It originates from a point in the natural waistline and then extends down in a slant to the opposite end. In other words, it is just a slanted waistline across your body, high on one side and low on the other.Asymmetrical waistline creates a slimming effect for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies.Match-maker: Asymmetrical waistline is a type of waistline that will create a slimming effect. Thus, it is great for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. WAIST NOT, WANT NOTPrincess seamThe absence of something is often beneficial as well. Though there exist several types of waistlines to go with every kind of body, there is a particular style that does not need a visible waistline. A style that is much beloved and which is about as timeless as the name itself - the princess seam style. It is a style that will probably never go out of style and is an epitome of soft feminity.A princess seam or line is characterised by the long seams that start from below the arm, or under the shoulder and curves delicately over the bust and down the body to give a prominent long look that that associated with A-line dresses. The seam can be stitched into blouses or dresses to have the desired structure and shape. Due to the way it is designed, the style does not need a waistline since it runs along panels down the body. The princess seam was associated with Charles Frederick Worth, a prominent English fashion designer of the 19th and 20th century who is also acknowledged by many as the ‘Father of Haute Couture’. The style was of course created for Princess Alexandra of Denmark, the wife of King Edward VII. Due to its fitted and figure-hugging design, it was believed to be the first ‘bodycon’ (who are we to deny that fact?).The princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.Match-maker: The princess seam works remarkably well for those with hourglass figures, the long, shapely seams that gather in at the waist and flare out again at the hips. However, the princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.  It’s a wardrobe staple for every lady, kind of like a good pair of shoes or an LBD. Or better yet an LBD with princess seams is a very acceptable option as well.  Either way, knowing what looks good on your unique body is the first step to being fashionably perfect every day but the personal interpretations and add-ons are what make the outfit your identity.  Text: Crystal SymssImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock					Cover storyMonochrome jackets look both trendy and sophisticated. Spotted time and again during Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW) Winter/Festive 2018, we know that monotone is the trend of the season. Even the Indian bridal wear designers are not spared and are often seen experimenting with the trend. The best thing about it? B-town fashionistas like Kangana Ranaut, Alia Bhatt and Anushka Sharma are often seen in these fresh, sporty looks. The trend has been embraced by major high-fashion brands and has been spotted on the runways for a few seasons now. There are three things you definitely need to flaunt this look—a comfortable outfit, a cool pair of sneakers and a major dose of attitude. Let’s see five different ways of sporting athleisure: Pair a printed short sleeve T-shirt with track pants for a casual day out with friends. You can complete the look by wearing white sneakers for women or sport shoes.   A plain T-shirt paired with printed track pants is an ideal combination for a lazy college day. You can accessorise a simple athleisure outfit by adding a cool backpack to it. Pair a tank top with classic joggers and you are ready for a movie date followed by a shopping spree. Complete the look with either white sneakers or sport shoes. Pair a casual tank top with training tights to look gym-ready. Add boots to your outfit instead of sneakers and you are good to hit the club at night.  					The one piece of clothing that can make any outfit look well-styled instantly is denim. Believed to be invented in 1873 by Jacob Devis and Levi Strauss, denim has come a long way since its inception. Today, it has forayed into footwear, accessories, furniture and even vehicles as seat covers. From the most eminent designers in the fashion fraternity to celebrities and even influencers, denim has spared no one and is everyone’s go-to clothing item. We tell you five ways you can style denim this season and look stunningly fashionable:What comes to your mind when you think of comfort and style together? A stylish pair of casual jeans indeed! Considered a wardrobe must-have, a pair of casual jeans could be styled with a simple, embellished T-shirt. To make the outfit look swish and smart, add-on a pair of white sneakers or flats.  When our favourite skinny jeans become a big no-no in the monsoon season, bootcut jeans come to our rescue. Pair them with a printed, chiffon shirt to keep your look easy-breezy. Complete this look by wearing crocs or slip-ons.  Wearing denim-on-denim is one fashion combination that can never go wrong. Style a well-fitted denim shirt with a slightly lighter shade of denim culottes and you’re ready to take on the world. Complete the look with floater sandals.   A-line skirts are in vogue! And what’s better than having them in denim. Don an off-shoulder, striped top over an A-line denim skirt to look perfect for a casual day out with friends. Pair the outfit with monsoon boots to complete the look. What is the perfect colour-combination you ask for women's fashion? White and denim hands down! Wear a printed white T-shirt, on skinny white jeans and pair them with a denim jacket. The entire ensemble exudes chicness. Complete the look with white sneakers. With the recent incident at Cannes 2018, where American actor Kristen Stewart was seen removing her heels on the red carpet as a protest against the film festival’s dress code—all female guests should wear heels–the message was crystal clear: No more telling us what to wear! With well-being as the topmost priority, women have consciously replaced the gut-wrenching experience of wearing stilettos with congenial foot candies, sneakers! According to a report by NPD’s group retail tracking service, sales of heels dropped by 12 per cent in the year 2017, while the sneakers market witnessed a boom of 37 per cent. Experts claim that other than factors like comfort and health concerns among women, one rationale seen for the decrease in the sales of heels is casualisation of every occasion. Co-founded by Jayesh Sachdev, it was a venture to bring his art to many through fashion and décor. What he didn’t know was that all their products will be sold out within the first week. Their quirky – as their name rightly suggests – designs are well appreciated and have had many takers even amongst the celebs like Deepika Padukone, Ranveer Singh, Priyanka Chopra, Alia Bhatt, Parineeti Chopra, Amitabh and Abhishek Bachchan, Kangana Ranaut and Kajol. The brand defines itself as a fashion and lifestyle label that exudes wearable eccentricity. “That, in addition to rich colour, graphic art and playful sophistication define our essence,” Sachdev mentions in the brand information, “We are synonymous with all things fun, offbeat and quirky. Our exuberant approach to the everyday encourages personal style with a dash of incandescent charm. We call it life in technicolor.” An artist by passion, a designer by choice and a creative entrepreneur by vocation, Sachdev talks about the brand, his journey and making people a walking gallery. It shouldn’t have been such a surprise though. Sachdev is an artist, designer and entrepreneur. He graduated with a Degree in Visual Communication at Lasalle College of the Arts, Singapore and holds the national record for having painted India’s largest concept artwork. Alongside running the Quirk Box, he continues to practice as an artist, exhibiting through New York to Bombay. He has won many awards including British Council Young Arts Entrepreneurs India 2008, Tiger Translate India Arts Awards and Crow Bar Asia Advertising Awards and he is also a credited TEDx speaker. Apart from his art, he is an avid photographer and loves to play tennis. Quirk Box also, is an award-winning label, alongside its founder. It won the Best Urban Wear Label – India award at Grazia Young India Fashion Awards in 2015. They have showcased their collection at the Lakme Fashion Week since 2013. In previous interviews, the artist-designer who is inspired by Sabyasachi and Manish Arora told the story behind Quirk Box, “There is an oddity and sense of innovation that is a virtue of Quirk Box. This oddity, this quirkiness, and this implicit need to be original and fun put together are what we like to call the Quirk Box. We’re here to be different and carve a niche of our own in this ever-growing industry. The strategy is to only provide fresh, quirky and unimaginable designs to our customers and reach out to prospects that haven’t yet been exposed to quirky fashion and lifestyle.” Living up to its story and its name, each collection by this brand has been unique and out-of-the-box. Not one to follow trends, but to set them, he has kept true to the essence of the brand with each collection, having come up with new and interesting prints every time. “Our USP is our strong understanding of design and fashion and our inherent traits of wanting to create something original each time,” he explains, “We are not aping trends, even though our works have a very strong ‘pop art’ essence, we are neither imitating designs, nor finding inspiration from Bollywood/Hollywood or popular culture, we are constantly striving to create innovative art that spells individuality.” Sachdev and his brand are all about expressing their art through various mediums, and thus was the Quirk Box Design Studio born. “I am primarily a visual artist,” tells the man who believes that ‘design is art with a function and business is applying that design into context’, “I have no formal understanding of fashion. My art and illustration aesthetic are what makes Quirk Box distinguished. The art that is made for Quirk Box is put into fashion, but fashion is only one such medium onto which my art can be applied to. We can design your space, your business identity, textile prints, wedding cards… the scope is diverse and limitless.” Through this independent design studio, the design style that is inherently Quirk Box can be hired as a service and not just as a product. We have a tête-à-tête with Sachdev talking of the milestones he’s reached in his journey till now, his inspirations and aspirations. Can you tell in brief about your journey to date?It's been a decade that I've been an artist; so it’s clearly been a long and exciting one. I started out as a Jr. Art Director at an agency in Singapore, after graduating from an art school. I eventually moved back to India to start Emblem, my design studio. That didn’t initially kick off the way I'd have imagined and I occupied myself painting. Before I knew it, I'd become a full-time artist. I founded Emblem Tee, and the Emblem Art Gallery and later Quirk Box. I like to believe I'm a creative entrepreneur as much as an artist. Along the way I picked up a few accolades and awards, it's been a frustrating, enriching and a learning journey, and I'm probably not even close to halfway where I'd like to be. Were art and design something you wanted to pursue from the start?I wanted to write. I wanted to play tennis and football. When I didn’t end up pursuing those as career options, I had a strong idea that I would be inclined towards a Visual Arts career. What inspires you to create?There is something magical and whimsical about creation. You have freedom. I enjoy this freedom of being a creator.  What inspired you to start Quirk Box?As an artist, you tend to have a limited audience. Often affluent or far too niche and restricted. This meant all my creative ideas and visions would manage to reach a small audience. I hoped that a lot more people could firstly, witness my art and secondly, afford it. Quirk Box was started to be a functional art label. Instead of buying my art on a canvas, you could now buy it as a garment. When you wear Quirk box, you are a walking gallery of my imagination. You started with an online store, and haven’t gone for the traditional retail format. Was that a conscious decision? Do you plan to have your own store in the future?The idea was always the penetration of the market. If you've lived in one place too long, you become a frog in a pond. You have to go out there and tell your story to everyone. I didn’t want to be tied to a physical space. I needed my art to be everywhere. And online allows me to reach 200 countries as opposed to one specific location that a brick and mortar are about.Since the start, you have come up with out-of-the-box designs. How has the response been?We turned seven in April. It's been wonderful. We've dressed commoners and celebrities alike. Won the awards that mattered and got the features that matter. We've sold from Pune to Peru. I have much to be grateful for. How’s the Quirk Box journey been till date? Can you tell us in brief about the milestones in this journey?When we started out seven years ago, we started out wanting to create something exciting. We had unrealistic ambitions, we wanted to reach the entire country, but a part of me believed I was being delusional to expect it. A week into our launch we were sold out and we realised we had created something larger than we knew. It has been a learning curve. Meeting incredibly talented people, incredible experiences, winning relevant awards, dressing fashion goddesses, it opened new windows of opportunities and experiences, from the fashion weeks to dressing A-listers. It's been a long tough exciting ride.Where do you get your inspiration from when you come up with new collections?Inspiration is everywhere. We find inspiration from our experiences and surroundings. There is no preset for this. Every day is a new experience and ideas are ever evolving. The fabrics you choose, the prints, the colours… Why do you choose what you do?I make art that I chose to make. We do not restrict ourselves with the art. The freedom of creating is why we started this. This is not trending determined. The fabrics that are chosen based on the season, cotton would work in warmer weathers, crepe and silks in the festive season. Since we print a multitude of colour, we also need to pick fabrics that allow us to print the kind of art we make. We also try to keep our prices in-check so the fabrics determine the same. Can you tell us about your latest collection?Our summer collection Chikanobu was inspired by the 18th-century Woodcut Artworks of the Japanese Artist Toyohara. I love all things Japanese, and Japanese art was something I've always been intrigued by. My wife Priyanka who is now the Chief Illustrator at Quirk Box was truly inspired by the idea of recreating his works in a contemporary context. The artworks of Emperor Meiji, the Japanese Cranes, Waves and Geisha's all features as artworks in the series of our Summer Resort wear. We used Crepe this season. It is light in weight and the blend we use is easy on sweat, heat and wash care.Who is your inspiration? I am inspired by my travel experiences. Food, small, the unknown that is exciting brings with it new stories to tell. Stories that we tell through art and fashion. Your most and least favourite parts of designing?Every day at work is a challenge; a new challenge. The amalgamation of art and business is something I am excited by. I thrive on this. Having to solve internal conflicts of tailor/labour is a rather annoying part of the profession though.What in your opinion is your biggest achievement so far?That I am able to sustain art in a country that has no value for it, is my biggest achievement. Quirk Box was one of the first of its kind with the designs that you came up with. These days there are many who do similar or “inspired” designs. Your take on plagiarism in the industry.Everything is an inspiration, and everything is a copy… some more than others. I see a tree and I draw it. I copy from nature. Some see the drawing of my tree and copy it. Unfortunately, due to the weak intellectual property laws and ambiguities, this won’t change anytime soon. In the meanwhile, we have to believe that imitation is the best form of flattery.Being an artiste and a designer, how do you balance the two facets?They are integrated. One fuels a passion, one fuels the bills. Can you tell us a little about Quirk Box Design?Quirk Box is an independent boutique art-based design studio. It offers crafted solutions for all your design needs.  With over 10 years of experience in the design space, including branding, graphics and fashion, the studio offers the same philosophy and principle of its original art and design and strong aesthetic essence, that is no longer limited to its in-house label, but to anyone that would like to hire its service. having worked with fashion, art, graphic design, branding, advertising, space design, the brand now offers you a design language you need, keeping intact the graphic art and playful sophistication that defines our essence. Can you tell us a little about your next collection?Our next is our most ambitious collection yet. Given the detail of the work, we are still working against the clock to release it in time for August.
