So whether you want to channel the Elizabethan age of over-the-top opulence or free-spirited bohemian vibes, there is a sleeve for every kind of whim and fancy. Like everything in the fashion industry, there is a time when some styles rise above the rest to become the look and talk of the season and the sleeves making waves (literally) this season are a mix of delightful throwbacks and modern sophisticated elegance. Bell of the ballBell sleeve is a super cute and fun style that is making a comeback to the fashion scene. The bell sleeves have been much beloved for their flowy design that allows easy movement and for their uber-graceful feminine appearance. In its previous lives, bell sleeves started their journey out by simply being a flared sleeve that was a part of the Japanese Heian period. A long dramatic flared sleeve was a classic feature and style norm back in the day. It then migrated across the world into the European medieval era and was predominately a style that was seen in the outfits of members of the church clergy. And it was around that time that the sleeve slowly and steadily developed its signature bell structure.The elite class of the Elizabethan era adored the bell sleeves. And as 'less is more' was not a phrase that the stylists of the Elizabethan era particularly believed in at the time, they decided to make it more extravagant (because, why not?) By adding on various embellishments like frills, lace and pleats . After which, the sleeves safely made their way into the modern world wherein the bell shape became more distinct and was synonymous with gentle femininity.The bell sleeves have been around for a long time and are likely to be around for a good bit more too considering the comebacks it makes every few years, seamlessly incorporating itself into the latest fashion trends. Though the bell structure is highly appreciated in the form of sleeves, its other variant 'the bell bottoms' weren't so lucky. But the world of fashion is a strange and unpredictable place. You never know what might pop up again.Why, though? Why has this simple little style managed to stick around for so long? Well, it because bell sleeves are enormously versatile. They have comfortably made themselves a perfectly fashionable asset in every area. From chic work wear to flirty casual and elegant evening wear, bell sleeves can be brought to every area of ââinterest. (Multipurpose utility? Yes, please). It is also wearable in a range of different fabrics as well as wool, lace and silk.How to style: Bell sleeves are great for any kind of occasion. And they come in several different variations, the fitted sleeve with bell flare starting only at the wrist or at the elbow. This is great for people wanting a combination of two styles; full-fitted sleeve and bell sleeve. When it comes to styling it for a classy, ââhigh fashion workwear ensemble, bell sleeves that tie at the elbow add that dash of sleek with a mild dose of flounce. Paired with some tailored pants make an effortless fashionable work-wear look that will help get rid of those Monday blues. Sheer silk blouses sporting bell sleeves are perfect for decadent evening wear and is super comfortable. Cap-tain of styleIf there was ever a voting poll to decide which is the 'all-time favorite sleeve' then cap sleeves would probably win hands down. Cap sleeves give us a feel of soft femininity, throwing it back to those long dreamy gowns with adorable cap sleeves that Keira Knightley wore to the ball in Pride and Prejudice (Who wouldn't want to pretend to be in that situation?). It is a representation of simple, uncomplicated design that is made for everyone. Their modest design is probably why they have been a part of bridal gowns and bridesmaids dress for a long time. The first record of cap sleeves being included into wedding attire has been traced back to the roaring 1920s and then made their way into everyday party wear fashion as well (flapper dresses anyone?).After that, the beloved cap sleeves cruised their way into the 30s, 40s and 50s. Clearly, fashion couldn't let them go and for good reason. It was made widely popular and sealed its place as timeless style when the biggest celebrities showcased their little cap sleeves of the most important day of their lives: their wedding. Scores of celebrities and royalty have sported cap-sleeved wedding gowns and strengthened its reputation as a favored design. When Jackie Kennedy Onassis wed John Kennedy in 1953 in her beautiful cap-sleeved gown, the style's popularity shot through the roof. Mega style icon Audrey Hepburn wore a cap-sleeve wedding dress in her movie 'Funny Face' in 1957 and that made it official, the cap sleeves were here to stay.The most recent ambassador for the beloved cap sleeve is the ever popular sister of the Duchess of Cambridge herself, Pippa Middleton. The fashion world will probably never forget the day she stepped out in that immaculate form-fitting cap-sleeved white gown on the day of the royal wedding. The wedding was not the only historic thing that happened that day. Pippa, with endless grace and panache, brought the caps back into the fashion scene. And it did not end there. When it was Pippa's turn to tie the knot, she dazzled the world again with another cap-sleeved beauty. Cap-sleeved elegance at its finest ladies!How to style: Though it is extremely favored in the wedding scene, bell sleeves are also quite flexible and can be showcased in everyday fashion as well. Along with it being a part of the usual suspects of western wear ie dresses and tops, you can even bring this style a little closer to home. Embellished high-necked sari blouses with cap-sleeves are exceptionally gorgeous and are a great way to amp up your traditional wear. Bishop sleeveBishop sleeves are sleeves that are quite similar to a bell sleeve, however, they have one defining feature. The full-length sleeves have a familiar flare that flows from the shoulder but it ends with a wide cuff that is gathered and cinched at the wrist. The style emulates a luxurious vintage feel. And it should rightfully because this style has been around for a long time. Though the sleeves are similar to the shape to the sleeves worn by bishops of the church- hence the name - but traces of the flouncy sleeves go even further back in time to the sixth-century Byzantine era (Kudos to them for probably being the oldest sleeve style ever). Though they were not all that prevalent during that time, bishop sleeves become a lot more common during the 1800s.Bishop sleeves got major traction back in the mid-60s during the time when the free-spirited hippie culture was making a statement in society. The relaxed flowing look it created coincided perfectly with the hippie style and they were all for it. Further on, in the 70s and 80s, the sleeves were made of lycra and polyesters to maintain the soft bouncy look that was its biggest selling point. Bishop sleeves created a flattering, balanced silhouette that made a person's shoulders look smaller in comparison. The cuff, historically, is a wide button cuff but over the years, it went through many reconstructions. Elasticized cuffs, embellished cuffs and cuffs with decorative trimmings were all a part of the advancements the bishop sleeves underwent to meet the ever-changing fashion demands.The distinctive shape of the bishop sleeve also attributes it to be known as balloon sleeves. They are also believed to be similar to peasant sleeves due to the fact that they both gather around the wrist. However, the difference is that peasant sleeves ideally tend to puff out at the shoulders, while bishop sleeves just flow smoothly from the shoulder down the arm for a nice draped effect. Peasant sleeves also do not possess a wide cuff but rather have a simple elastic band.How to style: Bishop sleeves are very distinctive and make quite a statement with their classically vintage look. Hence, they are great for formal blouses. Paired with a fitted high-waisted pant to emphasize the sleeves and create a stunning silhouette that just all of the soft sophistication; in other words, high fashion boss lady. For a look that's more casual Fridays, pair it with jeans instead. Draped bishop sleeves add a perfect little dramatic flair to a short loose dress with some strappy wedges or flats and you've basically got you're boho-chic on. Or a fitted dress that flatters your natural curves along with flowing sleeves is perfect for desk to dinner days. Keeping up with the kimono sleeveJapan's foremost export into the world of fashion is the traditional kimono and most popularly the kimono sleeve has carved its place into the fashion scene for the smooth elegant effect that it gave. Traditionally, the type of kimono a person wore would be a marker that officially denoted their social standing, rank and occupation. Well, clothes tend to have that effect even now in a rather unofficial, unspoken way. Nevertheless, the sleeve style eventually made its way across to the western world towards the end of the 1940s.Traditional Japanese wide kimono sleeves are varied in lengths. The sleeves of the kimono's that were used in theatrical performances tending to almost 3 feet long and would drag across the floor for spectacularly dramatic effect. Imagine walking into a party with 3 foot long sleeves (instant show stopper). Unfortunately, that wouldn't be the most practical thing to wear in the real world, so the sleeves were cut down to size to suit more normal measurements. Ideally, kimono sleeves have a deep armhole and the sleeve does not have a definite shoulder seam or armhole seam, which is its peculiarity. The main body of the garment and the sleeve are created from the same continuous piece of material, it, therefore, is also known as a 'grown-on' sleeve.How to style: Kimono sleeves are the trend this season and are perfect for wrap dresses, cinched-in waist secured with a sash that completely the whole traditional kimono look as a whole. Kimono sleeves are also great for sheer or silk blouses that go well with pants or pencil skirts. Shrugs with long kimono sleeves are an excellent way of adding a chic layer to casual jeans and tank top outfit. Cape wonder sleeveCape sleeves and capes are on the list of trending items this season. It's a cool look that speaks of elevated style and if you know just how to wear it and accessorize it, it can be a striking feature in your fashion diaries. Cape sleeves are can be traced back to the past with the introduction of the cloak. Capes were basically an outer garment that draped over the wearer and covered the shoulders, arms and was fastened at the neck. They were super popular back in medieval Europe (Try not to think of long Dracula-esque cape). After their heyday back in the dark ages, capes are back in the modern age to make a style statement unlike any other with designers offering new spins and innovations on trend to make classy and impart a sense of regality because every girl deserves to be a queen .Cape sleeves are most popularly seen on jackets - as the cape is essentially made for outerwear - that has been upgraded with bold new patterns, interesting new fabrics and showcased in varying lengths for every kind of occasion. The sleeves can either in be flared if made with softer fabrics or can be straight and sleek for a more defined structure.How to style: Cape sleeves are great on blazers and because the fabric is stiffer, the silhouette you acquire is impeccably sleek and very flattering; perfect for when you evolve from boss lady to modern queen! It is ideal for smart elegant formal wear or can be used to dress up a basic and top ensemble for a night out. Long flared, looser cape sleeves work well on dresses for an ultra-majestic look or on light pastel colored tops for those casual brunch days. Pick out any one of this season's trendiest sleeves and work it like a boss. Text: Crystal Symss Images: Yogen Shah Like history, fashion sure has a way of resurrecting back. Of staple stringsThis quite modest piece of string worn across the neck dates back to 2500 BC! From denoting prostitution to denoting lesbianism, the choker has travelled quite practically everywhere. The choker, now sitting proudly in jewellery cases gained its due attention in the 1900’s because of Queen Alexandra of England when she flaunted one to hide a small scar. It further garnered attention when people started wearing plastic chokers in 1990’s. From Gwyneth Paltrow flashing one at the 1999 Academy Awards to Paris Hilton and Rihanna, every fashion diva has surrendered to the choker game. Back home, Zeenat Aman was one of the first celebrities to rock a choker. Of course, these days the humble choker has enjoyed popularity as celebrities such as Sonam Kapoor, Priyanka Chopra, etc. exhibit various types of choker including diamonds, lace, velvet, beads, leather, shoelace (Yep, even a shoelace can be worn as a choker!) Not only is it super stylish, it is also easy on the pocket and comes with a guarantee of making you seem like an Insta- goddess! Chokers are literally the easiest way to make you seem like you belong to the ‘you can’t sit with us’ tribe. The 90s saw the ‘it’ crowd styling their plastic cord with denim shorts and crops.Style guide: Chokers are something that could be worn throughout the day and beyond.  The strand science is pretty easy to grasp. (No Einstein IQ required here!). The only deciding factor to keep in mind to wear one is the neckline of the outfit that you would be wearing it with. Now, you could wear a dainty ribbon cord for a super casual day out in denim and a tee or could go glam displaying an extravagant bold crystal version with an off-shoulder gown. You could also parade around in multi-layered chokers by pairing them with low neckline outfits. “Chokers are in but can get common these days. Mix it up with a layer of other neck pieces of various lengths to give it a new and different look,” shares designer Neha Sharma. Moving on to traditional outfits, nothing like an Indian-ised version of a choker to pair with a lehenga for your oh-so-important mehendi function. Put together a statement piece of a pearl droplet choker with a sheer black sari and be prepared to make heads turn at the soiree! Return of the coy cropA moment of applause for Madeline Vionnet for if it wasn’t her, we really wouldn’t have been offered the cropped fashion. In 1932, Madeline Vionnet designed an evening gown with strategically cut openings at the waist. The design was accepted by the masses and how! By the 1940’s, women’s magazine had further enhanced the trend by exposing degrees of midriff. Teen magazines of late 1940’s and 1950’s too weren’t far behind and happily participated in the movement by flaunting midriff barring suits and tops. Although it was restricted to swimwear initially, since the trend was so widely accepted, it was only natural for it to have an upgrade and move into women’s wear.This was only the beginning for the coy crop top. Crop tops further moved ahead to become “the look” of the 1980’s. The midriff-baring piece of clothing found a fan in Madonna, who wore it in a lot of her albums. She even made it a part of her signature look. It further garnered tons of exposure on silver screen and was part of many iconic films such as Dirty Dancing and Flash Dance. Crop tops conquered the pop culture and became a major part of it all throughout the 90’s. The low rise jeans paired with belly shirts became a classic duo especially in the sector of music and television. Britney Spears too was seen parading around in the same quite often. While they were initially worn during daily workouts with leggings, the crop top progressed to being worn with denim for a casual look.Style guide: Fortunately, styling a crop top isn’t all that demanding as it is quite a versatile piece and each one of us can find a variant to work around with.  Cropped fashion isn’t restricted to the 20 something’s or to the women with washboard abs.  The beauty of it is that it can blend into your business wardrobe as efficiently as it can belong to your vacation travel suitcase. If you aren’t comfortable with taking a leap forward by sporting a short crop, you could always work your way up by taking a shirt or top and giving it a DIY crop makeover by tying it! Full sleeved short tops paired with full skirts are another way of toning down the flash. You could also pair one with a high-waisted pant or knife pleated palazzo and add a blazer to rock that conference at 3 pm at the workplace. “Who’s not a fan of crop tops? It pairs well with high-waisted bottoms. Throw on a shrug to avoid showing off too much (if you want to tone down the look),” shares Sharma. Matching separates like a crop and a skirt with heels and a colour pop sling could have you looking like a million bucks – that too, without having to spend it. Doesn’t it look like it’s time for you to head down to the store and invest in some crop tops now? From functional to fashionableGiven fashion’s fixation on everything mini this year, it was only a matter of time that this completely charming backpack came back marching into our lives with drum rolls. If you are a 90’s kid, you probably remember owning at least one of these bags that was then imprinted with your favourite cartoon character and taking it for a day out at the annual picnic or at the local dance class sessions. What once proudly sat proudly on our study tables is back yet again only looking fresher than ever. The backpack (the bigger version) came into existence in the 1920’s solely as a functional carrier. It was only much later when designers realized that they could transform it from being just functional to being more fashionable and mint money!  The mini backpack gained massive popularity when it materialized on screen in Amy Heckerling’s Clueless in 1995 slung over the shoulder of the fictional Cher and there was no looking back after that. Alicia Silverstone donned one with her plaid miniskirts and knee socks and carried it so well that it became a must-have accessory for everybody.While it did not have a lot of variants back then, today you have a number of varieties to choose from. Ranging from leather goodies to satin to even denim, the mini backpack does not disappoint. This super fun and chic miniature not only can be worn as a backpack but also serves well as a handbag (all you have to do is hold it by its handle on the top!) so yes, you can enjoy the best of two worlds effortlessly. Style guide: Heading for a movie? Take along a mini backpack in a bright shade that stands out, whilst going super casual in denim and a V-neck. You could probably never imagine cocktails and mini backpacks in the same sentence but yes, you could invest in a fancier leather mini backpack handbag and take it for a night out with the girlfriends. It looks good and keeps your hands free to hold your drink easily. While satin backpacks could be taken while shopping, you could resort to the denim ones for game night at the arcade or while cheating on the diet at the pizza parlour. “Not only could you carry them with western outfits but you could even pair a bling-y mini with a sari to a kitty party!” points out Molo. There really is no stopping this fun-sized bag this season, we really advise you to go grab one of these and join the tribe! Also, you’re welcome!  Denim dramaMost of us are positively familiar with how denim came into existence; it worked its way up from being worn solely by labourers to being warmly accepted by the masses. High-waisted denim is a different thing altogether. It was invented in 1940 when brand Levis produced clothing keeping in mind the women working on land and in factories. The particular style allowed them to retain their modesty as they had to bend down to work. In the 60s, Marilyn Monroe donned one with a belt and shirt tucked right in and starred in the movie called The Misfits. You probably don’t need us telling you how well the look was accepted and followed. Most of us still wear it the Monroe way even today. Banavalikar-Kulkarni makes note, “In the 90s, high-waisted jeans were worn with crop tops and that’s come as-is as a trend now. You can just pull over an open shirt for daily wear.”The brand Guess made denim all the more popular with its campaigns starring Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell, Drew Barrymore, and the late Anna Nicole Smith. High-waisted denim is being offered in a lot of different washes and styles which is why most everybody succumbed to the trend. Full speed to 2018 and a quick peep to today’s fashion scenario and you would notice how so many people are embracing the high-waisted trend. Style guide: You really cannot go wrong with this piece of clothing. Not only does it make you look curvier, it also makes you look slimmer, curvy and tall. Easy to wear, and low-maintenance is what makes them a must-have. “Denims emphasize the curves so well; they look graceful,” informs Molo. Wearing a dark wash denim with a white V-neck and some hoops makes you look oh-so-sassy and effortless; throw in some tan handbag and nude blocks and you are ready to kill! Pair it off with a bling bralette and you’ve got your Saturday night OTTN ready! Try heading to the workplace in a pair with a satin floral shirt with these denims and be ready to nail the Friday dressing OOTD!  Majorly monochromeThis is a classic that has seen many versions through the years. Not only did this trend get plenty of space in the Chanel collection of yore but it was also a big time hit with its current design head, Karl Lagerfeld and featured regularly in his collections. The designer liked the winning blend so much that he wears the combination himself. The 60’s went gaga over anything and everything edgy. The black and white optical illusions were a hit. Women went on to adopt the black and white, simple yet stunning pieces and felt that it came equipped with power. Back then, polka dotted dresses paired with hats sold like hot cakes (and polka dots' trend is back again!). Down the eras, designers including Victoria Beckham, Carolina Herrerra were smitten by the monochrome bug too. The 90s saw this trend with a twist. It was not just about the black-and-whites, which themselves were in vogue, but monochrome also caught attention in its coloured version. Ensembles in varying tones of the same colour became a rage. And this trend in monochrome is back this season, with its own twist. “Monochrome in the 90s was more of bright colours, but these days, people have turned to pastels,” informs Banavalikar-Kulkarni.Style guide: “Styling monochrome is quite simple, a little tricky but mostly the end result is nothing short of remarkable,” shares Azmeen. Monochrome does require a thought before but looks really chic and classy once styled in the correct manner. Let’s brave the 2018 summer by keeping it simple in a white shirt and black jeggings and statement accessories like a bold neckpiece or earrings and some chunky bracelets. Black body con dresses worn with white capes make you look like nothing short of a fashion diva. Steer clear of prints and keep it simple as prints could break the look. If you find someone wearing the same outfit as you, how do you react?a) You get annoyed and want to make sure that you’re pulling off the look better than them.b) You’re not a fan of the idea, so you spend the day avoiding being seen next to them.c) You’re #Twinning! This calls for a selfie! Mostly As  Type A Personality: Type As are ambitious and proactive. You love planning ahead and go over and above what is expected of you. The fact that you put so much time and effort into everything you do means that you’re fiercely competitive, and sometimes invite unnecessarily stressful situations. You’ve probably been called a control freak before, and you know the title is well deserved. You pride yourself in your ability to be organised, on time and efficient. Mostly Bs  Somewhere in between: You are all about adapting to circumstances. Falling on neutral ground between competitive and laidback, you are well-adjusted and change your approach based on what is called for. You are capable of being both a fearless leader and a willing team player. When you commit to something, you go all in, but you also know when it’s time to take a step back and detach yourself from a situation.  Mostly Cs  Type B Personality: You’re relaxed and believe in going with the flow. You are the kind of person to stop to smell the roses, and are known to enjoy the little things. People often mistake your laidback nature for inefficiency, but you know you can get things done without stressing yourself out. You’re not so much about the results as you are about the process, which is why you are good at tasks that require creativity and innovation. We demystify the main types so you can pull them off like the women of Bollywood.GinghamGingham is one of the most common variants you can wear. It’s a basic, evenly-sized checkered pattern with no more than two colours. While it’s most commonly used on shirts, you could also pair matching separates like this bandeau-skirt combo on Alia Bhatt.Play with the size of the print for different results, like this mini-check jacket on Bhumi Pednekar.Windowpane checksWindowpane checks are exactly what they sound like – thin, spaced out checks that form a graph-like pattern. Since they’re subtle, they work great when you’re wearing print-on-print, like this checked blouse and striped sari on Jacqueline Fernandez.Vidya Balan sports the thicker variant of the windowpane check in this Kanjeevaram sari.Bend the rules and wear dotted checks instead of stripes like this cropped top on Tamannaah Bhatia.TartanTraditionally used for Scottish kilts, tartan is formed with unequally-sized checks, in two or more colours. Sonakshi Sinha wears a tartan slip dress over a plain white tee for a casual ensemble.This gathered-waist tartan skirt on Sonam Kapoor pays tribute to the original Scot kiln.If you’re looking for something more feminine, this tartan off-shoulder dress on Huma Qureshi is a good place to start. Irresistible features like music control, battery life of up to 24 hours, LED flashlight and water-resistant make it a must-have for every woman. The final day of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 gave an indication of what’s going to impact your sartorial choices in spring and summer. Take a look. RufflesSpring catwalks around the world are cascading with ruffles and the Capital wasn’t an exception. While Rina Dhaka included the frilly detail in her saris, kurtas and dresses at the finale, Ashish N Soni juxtaposed them on clean and classic silhouettes to make his ready-to-wear line look young, fun and sensuous. Flash dance shoulderThis is an evolution of the off shoulder trend. Designer Sulakshana Monga adapted the peekaboo treatment for her clothes, flash dance or the ‘accidental’ shoulder show that reveals a little flesh without showing too much was a predominant trend. Monga used Half-on, half-off tops and dresses with single ruffled shoulders exposing only a slice of skin. If you wear this, keep the rest of the outfit simple and let your shoulder do the talking. Sheer fabricSheer fabrics such as chiffon, tulle, mesh, organza and chanderi have been summer staples for long and they made an impactful appearance on the runway at the Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018. From hemlines, tops with sheer insets, skirts and dresses at Monga’s to sheer in Indian wear--embellished sheer lehengas and blouses and saris at the Suneet Varma’s show--the trend was ubiquitous. Traditional embroideryIndian culture and craftsmanship were both profusely showcased on the ramp via traditional motifs and intricate embroideries. From thread embroidery at Pankaj and Nidhi, Krishna Mehta and Charu Parashar to intricate zardozi embroidery seen at Suneet Varma’s show, this ethnic element is here to stay though the silhouettes may vary from western contemporary to Indian. Day four of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 saw an abundance of clashing prints, all-white ensembles, dramatic hemlines and statement sleeves. Here’s a round up of the trends that is sure to get your attention: Shades of whiteMany shades of white were spotted on the runway. They offered a stark contrast to the multitude of prints and colours. From Madhu Jain, Kavita Bhartia to Abhi Singh and Ekta Jaipuria and Ruchira Kandhari paired white with white in their collections. If you’re not big on white-on-white, add a few loose fitted casual styles from Payal Jain, frilly and flirty skirts from Kavita Bhartia or a few traditional cotton kurtas from Madhu Jain to your wardrobe and mix and match it with other colours. Shirts under spaghetti strapsStylistas Kim Kardashian and Kendall and Kylie Jenner have been doing this for a while now and designers Dhruv Kapoor and Abhi Singh seemed to have got the drift. Models sashayed down the ramp wearing risqué spaghetti dresses and tank tops over shirts in different sizes and shapes. So ladies, it’s time to bring out your slinky dresses. Print on printThe runway saw an abundance of clashing patterns and prints, proving that this trend for the brave will be big in the upcoming season. While Shivan and Narresh had matching top and bottom sets with prints boasting of forest sights, Dhruv Kapoor matched ditsy florals with vintage prints. Exaggerated sleevesThis is one of the biggest trends for spring summer. And there are so many different types of statement sleeves to suit different types of arms. From billowy bell shaped, ultra long and oversized to ruffled, cinched at the wrist to exaggerated cuffs, there’s enough to last you more than one season. Asymmetrical hemlinesEverything isn’t straight and narrow for summers, designers played with geometry and courted the asymmetrical hemlines in myriad ways. Anju Modi brought the mullet back in fashion—her kurtas had hemlines that were short at the front and long in the back. Meanwhile, Kavita Bhartia, Dhruv Kapoor and Bhanuni by Jyoti experimented with the handkerchief hemline.																		Summery trenches, feminine florals, restrained monochromes and classic plaids, were trending on day 3 of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018.  Lay the trenchesThe summer trench coat is going to be one wardrobe classic in the coming season. The classic trench coat was exquisitely upgraded with thread embroidery by Payal Pratap, deconstructed and made feminine with floral prints by Shruti Sancheti and kept sombre with single tones by Pallavi Dhyanee. Flower powerFloral prints are no longer a surprise for summer, but next season brings big blossoms in all kinds of styles as seen at Shruti Sancheti, Payal Pratap and Pallavi Singhee shows. Pratimaa Pandey, however, used it judiciously by decorating the hems and necklines with floral embroidery. Black and white worldMonochrome is one of the strongest trends this spring summer season. Designers Abraham & Thakore, Rajesh Pratap Singh and Medha Khosla of Anomaly championed the stark black and white contrast. The two shades were interpreted in abstract and clashing prints, stripes and panels. Get creative and work the trend by opting for block separates, a monochrome dress or a monochrome print.  Woven handloomsWoven handlooms are clearly the fabric of the future. With sustainable fashion topping the agenda of most designers, an urban sensitivity was introduced to the fabric. From clean, minimalist work wear to luxurious day and evening wear, handlooms found an easy expression in the spring summer lines of Anomaly, Rajesh Pratap Singh, Abraham and Thakore and Payal Pratap.  Plaid and simplePlaids had a major moment on the runaway of day 3. Checked patterns have been a winter favourite for long, but designers such as Payal Pratap, and Teresa Liasom and Utsav Pradhan of Munkee See and Munkee Do and Pallavi Dhyani gave it fun and colourful interpretation for spring. But Rajesh Pratap Singh decided to keep it staid by taking the conventional way for his shirts, jackets and trousers.																		The collections showcased on day 2 of Amazon India fashion Week SS/18 seemed to have comfort on the top of their priority list. From billowy silhouettes and wide-leg pants to utilitarian jumpsuits and bomber jackets, there was adequate inspiration for girl-next-door. The new bomberDesigner Aarti Vijay Gupta combined sports luxe with her signature quirky prints and easy anti-fit silhouettes. The baggy pants leave about enough room for your legs to not stick to the fabric in summer months. We liked the ones we saw on the runway at Ikai, Patine and Love Bird’s shows.   StripesThe predominant pattern at the Amazon India Fashion Week, this season was the ubiquitous stripes – big, bold, subtle, horizontal, and vertical and in all shapes and sizes. While Ragini Ahuja explored stripes in all its avatars from bold to zig zag, Love Birds and Aarti Vijay Gupta resorted to subtle versions. Billowy silhouettesThis one-size-fit-all trend comes as good news for all Indian women on the heavier side. It is evident from the ramp that designers paid enough attention to the fact that some women need more relaxed styles. Our top picks are the ant-fit dresses seen in Love Birds’s show, the jackets, kurtas and cropped tops in Ragini Ahuja’s collection and the loose, free-flowing tops and dresses from Rina Dhaka’s new line.  Reinvented jumpsuitsDesigner Ashish N Soni expressed his signature creativity in his spring summer line that also marked his 25th year in the industry. This season, wear the reinvented jumpsuit to the formal evening parties and watch heads turn.																		Warm weather may be months away but comfortable, fuss-free clothes are always on our mind. Who doesn’t wish to get into easy-breezy outfits and hit the outdoors? To help you make sound fashion decisions, we have put together some runway trends from the ongoing Amazon India Fashion Week SS/18 that you can actually wear in real life. From exaggerated lines, metallic hints to bright candy colours, Day 1 had all the inspiration you need for your summer wardrobe. Take a look.Metallic hintsIt's always a good time to be experimental. A good way to add fun and excitement to your wardrobe is to introduce metallic hints to your outfits or accessories. Rimzim Dadu infused metallic hues in silver, gold and blue into her range of re-imagined saris, sculpted statement tops jackets and skater dresses. If you aren’t sure of metallic outfits, begin with accessories. A hint of metallic is sure to get you noticed. Sorbet coloursPassionate pastels or sorbet shades have been making quite a wave on international runways and they made a strong appearance in Anupama Dayal’s show. She used lilacs, lavender, melons and sunset hues on gossamer and light fabrics such as chiffons and Chanderis. A deviation from the pop and neon colours, these shades will add a breath of fresh air to your summer wardrobe. Shoulder obsessionFashion’s fascination with shoulders rages on. The off-shoulder trend manifested itself in Samant Chauhan’s Victorian gowns and Anupama Dayal’s playful jumpsuits. Rock the trend by adding your own clever twists to it--sport the silhouette on your top and pair it with skirts and pants or go the traditional way by teaming a sari with the top. Athleisure boomWearing workout gear as a part of your casual outfit is the new in thing. Nida Mahmood fused age-less Indian art from around the country onto sporty silhouettes to create an athlesiure range in collaboration with active lifestyle brand Deivee. There were cycling shorts, leggings and running saris strutting down the ramp. Oversized ruffle collarsRuffle collars bring to mind images of the erstwhile queens of England. The aristocratic ruffle collar made a comeback in the Indigofera collection by Schulen Fernandes for Wendell Rodricks. They added a sharp colour contrast and an element of intrigue to fluid silhouettes. Outfit topperJackets in varying lengths are the current flavour of the season and are expected to enjoy the exalted status in the next season too. While JJ Valaya used long jackets with streamlined silhouettes over traditional saris, anarkalis and lehenga cholis, the brand Aureole paired hand woven cropped jackets and shrugs with dresses for maximum impact in its show.					Day 4 had some stellar shows by ace designers Anju Modi and Rahul Mishra. From classic silhouettes to traditional embroideries and from understated elegance to new age detailing, there was no dearth of fashion inspiration. Here’s what reigned the ramp. Floral storyThe floral story this season is whimsical, elegant and rooted to tradition. Rahul Mishra used resham threads to recreate intricate floral motifs of the Mughal era and mixed them with geometric and abstract patterns, giving them a contemporary twist. Anju Modi too followed the historical route and brought alive floral patterns from Rajasthan. Perfectly imperfect hemlinesAnju Modi added a bohemian yet sophisticated touch to her ensembles by introducing uneven hemlines on her long kurtas. The quintessentially laid-back style lent a certain nonchalance to her classic designs. As the growing popularity of cruise shows indicates, between Instagram-worthy beach escapes, destination weddings and glamping, resort fashion has indeed come a long way. Whether you’re reclining on sun loungers or cruising over gorgeous landscapes in a hot air balloon, there’s no excuse to look sloppy anymore, especially when you travel. While the island state of mind is just that—a state of mind—the allure of a glorious coverup, a feather-light kaftan or one of those hand-woven, basket totes is real, palpable and, suddenly, everywhere.  Spring/summer 2017 runways are proof that resortwear can go well beyond throw-on-and-go pieces. Take Miu Miu’s retro Italy-inspired collection, which comprise a line of ruched bikinis, patterned robe-style dresses and teensy twinsets, accompanied by embossed pool slides and appliqued swim caps. Miuccia Prada understands the value of a chic escape. “It’s a celebration of summer and its pleasures,” she mused during the post-show interview. Dolce & Gabbana also sought inspiration from the Italian tropics for its covered sundresses, bralets and miniskirts in fun prints (think pasta, seafood and gelato). The show venue even had a counter serving fresh tender coconut water and models strutted down the runway to the rhythms of the tarantella. Giorgio Armani presented a line of slouchy bloomers, sheer cover-ups and short suits, featuring painterly prints and tassels—just what we need for those soirées under the stars. The accessories followed suit; the flatforms at Prada and Chloé would make for stylish accoutrements on a holiday. For their spring/summer 2017 collection, Delhi-based designer duo Hemant and Nandita elevated holiday basics like swimsuits, shorts, crop tops and sarong-esque skirts using Victorian ruffles and vibrant print play. Nishka Lulla set out to reinvent the pantsuit, working with softer fabrics and delicate embellishments to transform it into a resort essential. Lulla says, “I used lightweight, everyday materials like cotton and tulle in relaxed comfy silhouettes, with frills and flounces thrown in for good measure.” Aparna Badlani, curator and co-owner of multi-designer boutique Atosa, Mumbai, has long recognised the potential of well-made resortwear. “At a point when destination weddings are such a huge phenomenon, the category is finally getting its due,” she says. If there’s one image that captures the exquisite charm of travel, it’s got to be that of actor and socialite Talitha Getty hanging out on the terrace of her Marrakech home, immortalised by photographer Patrick Lichfield in the late ’60s.  It even inspired Yves Saint Laurent to design a line of kaftans that he called Une Passion Marocaine. Designer and TV personality Nicole Richie, who has a perpetual vacation vibe about her, best embodies this spirit today. Her style reminiscent of LA’s boho-luxe aesthetic from the ’60s and the ’70s. Whether it’s through pictures of Taylor’s Swift’s glamorous squad chilling together on a yacht or Olivia Palermo and beau Johannes Huebl’s romantic romp in Greece, travel continues to fire our imagination and inform fashion in the most powerful ways.  Much like with eveningwear, building a bankable resortwear wardrobe takes work. “Start with the basics and build from there. Think kaftans, palazzos, shorts, day dresses and strappy sandals,” says Badlani. According to Lulla, the trick is to invest in lightweight, versatile separates that can be paired with other items from your wardrobe. “Take, for instance, bustiers that you can wear on the beach or with high-waisted bottoms for a night out,” she says. It’s always a good idea to mix luxe pieces with exotic finds from local boutiques and markets to create a look that is uniquely yours. Abaya is an outer garment worn by Muslim women. It also called burqa in certain countries. This garment is a long robe or cloak, which covers the body except for head, feet, and hands. The traditional abayas are black in colour. But now, these abayas have now got a fashion makeover.    The women, who are style savvy women and love to boast the tradition and trend can try the updated versions. We got in touch with LimeRoad's fashion stylist, Rina S Walia to talk about the new styles:   1. Denim love The long denim abaya is the best for the all-denim look. Try a black one with colourful pleats at the bottom. Complete the look with a pair of pumps and a black sling bag.     3. Pretty pastels Pastel shades have become the talk of the town. Try a beautiful pastel pink abaya as the go-to attire for days when you want to look effortlessly stylish.    4. Cape Craze Capes are totally ruling the ramps this season. Don't lag! As designers get nostalgic for the flamboyant ’80s, sequins go gangsta and shiny vinyl finds its way back into our closet. This season sparkle comes imbued with a street sensibility as the more-is-more mantra from our favourite decade clashes with athleisure’s fluid dynamism. Cue the season’s sharpest plissé skirts teamed with a pair of equally luxe sneakers. Designers drummed up a host of options that make an easy transition from the cubicle to the dance floor. We’re looking to Michael Kors’ slashed sequinned mini dresses and Phoebe Philo’s egg-shaped lurex pullovers at Céline for inspiration. “I like bare legs in winter; I like night for day. I like Alexa Chung mixing with Nan Kempner. It’s about the interesting mix,” said Kors in an interview post his show. At Kenzo, Humberto Leon and Carol Lim sent out a line of vinyl dresses and skirts, foil-print trousers and oversized metallic jackets. Isabel Marant flirted with vinyl too in retro styles, adding animal prints and plaid to the mix. “It really goes back to when I would sneak out, aged 15, to punk clubs like Le Palace and Les Bains Douches,” said the Parisian designer. Between Marc Jacobs’ subversive separates at NYFW and Rajesh Pratap Singh’s gilded army closer home, the message is loud and clear—street glamour is here to stay. Designer Sanchita Ajjampur’s futuristic mash of foil, mesh and paillettes, and Gaurav Jai Gupta’s street-style spin on metallic handlooms, further confirm the mood of the times. It’s evident that fashion is making no bones about its Ziggy Stardust-meets-Beyoncé philosophy, and the pop culture influencers are lapping it up. Historically, the first image that comes to mind in this category is that of  ’60s fashion icon and rocker Keith Richards’s then girlfriend Anita Pallenberg who took to the Cannes red carpet in a lurex jumper. Leave it to the Kardashian-Jenner clan to reinvent Pallenberg’s louche luxe uniform as they elevate street style basics like sweatshirts, lace-up boots and trackpants. Kendall Jenner even brought back the chainmail dress from the ’90s. Closer home Alia Bhatt is having a go with unexpected pairings like a camo shirt and a plissé skirt, offering us a fresh take on the trend.      Which brings us to the question of how to do it right. Archana Walavalkar, celebrity stylist and co-founder Stylecracker, says that styling is everything here. “It’s important to blend the look seamlessly, not letting the shiny piece acquire hero status at any point.” It’s a good idea to stock up on basics like hologram sweatshirts, sequinned numbered tees, slip dresses with a glamorous sheen, and metallic denims. If you’re shine-shy, begin with a statement accessory. Let the gleaming heels from Demna Gvasalia’s debut at Balenciaga or Fendi’s festive-edition gold totes give you some ideas. “Go casual with jeans and a tee teamed with embellished sandals. This is easier to pull off if you don’t quite dare to go all guns blazing,” says Ajjampur. Fine jewellery is also following suit by putting a casual spin to sparkle. Case in point: Nirav Modi’s Embrace range of diamond bangles, which stretch like a dream, offer a snug fit and are best worn with denims and a boyfriend shirt. The writing’s on the wall: Whatever your glittery vice may be, it’s time to wear it on your sleeve.   Wendell Rodricks is a man credited with many firsts. At a time when Indian fashion was all about opulence and grandeur, he introduced the idea of minimalism. He was one of the few Indian designers to bring eco-friendly textiles to the forefront and also pioneered resortwear in India. To commemorate his contributions to the fashion industry, Rodricks was awarded the Padma Shri title in 2014. While contemporaries are predictably passing on their legacies and labels to family members, the designer has entrusted it into the hands of young prodigy Schulen Fernandes. And he did it in his inimitable style, bang in the middle of the runway at his label's fall/winter showing at the 2016 Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW). In a fun, free-wheeling chat, Rodricks and Fernandes tell us about what's in store for the legendary label.Wendell, after holding the reins for 28 years, you've decided to hand them over to Schulen. Schulen, how did he break it to you and what was your reaction?Wendell Rodricks: I always wanted the label to go to somebody I trusted. Schulen came to me straight from college and she has been with me for four years. She had already started taking a lot of creative decisions for the label. For instance, last season we did the Indica Emporia presentation at LFW with vintage Indian garments. It was completely her vision and work from start to end. I wanted to slowly take the backseat with this label so that I could make time for my other passions. I felt the time was just right for her to take the label and fly with it.Schulen Fernandes: It obviously didn't happen out of the blue. The handover was always on the cards and it took two years of work laying the foundation. However, when the actual moment arrived, it was hard to believe. How are your roles divided in the new scheme of things?WR: I’d like to think of myself as a benevolent dictator (laughs). On a serious note, Schulen has complete freedom to realise her creative vision at the label now and I am happy to have her take over.SF: Wendell will obviously be the mentor. My work will now involve everything from conceptualising collections to actually bringing it to life. I am also excited about the business end of it and we have a competent team to help us on that front.Schulen, tell us a little bit about your debut collection, Trapezoid, for the Wendell Rodricks label presented at LFW. And, Wendell, what did you think of it?SF: I have always loved architecture and geometry. The trapezoid form has been used in architecture from ancient times and it is so versatile. We decided to explore it in fashion with this collection. We used a mix of structured shapes and fluid fabrics working with paper silks, chanderis and a lot of eco-friendly materials. WR: I was really surprised when Schulen came up with the idea. It is a form that I've seen in Inca and Aztec architecture and in our temple gopurams. The Indian woman's body which is narrow at the shoulders and wide at the hips also follows the trapezoid form. This was particularly relevant because for the first time we introduced a size chart specific to the Indian woman at LFW this season. I felt really proud watching the show. The biggest compliment to me and to Schulen was when people told us it (the collection) looked like Wendell Rodricks. When a new creative leader takes charge at a fashion house, change is afoot—what can we expect from the label?WR: I've always focussed on high-end fashion and have never been able to cater to the mid-range. I hope Schulen will be able to expand the reach of this label to more people the way my colleague Anita Dongre has done very successfully. I also want her to take risks with the label and be more experimental.SF: We will definitely retain the minimalistic language and eco-friendly DNA of the label as we move forward. I would like to introduce newer, younger silhouettes and experiment heavily with materials. What lies ahead for both of you? Wendell, do you miss being behind the wheel? Schulen, are you at all daunted?WR: I don’t miss being behind the wheel at all. I can finally dedicate time to things that I’ve been waiting to do. The work on the museum is underway (Rodricks is turning his Goa home into a space dedicated to Goan costumes). The dogs are taking it well but my three cats are giving me grief about the move! I would like to write a lot more. My next book Poskem is about Goa. I hope I’ll be able to turn it into a movie like Chetan Bhagat (laughs). I’d like to teach a lot more too.SF: I am excited about what lies ahead and loving every minute of my new job. Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Tasselled earrings work exceptionally well with this outfit. Back to the basicsHow can we not mention the quintessential ethnic work-fashion piece? A kurta is not only comfortable to wear but looks oh-so-chic, especially if there is a design element that adds to the look. The asymmetric style gives it an edgy look. If the neckline is low, then team it up with a chunky choker and mid-sized studs in the ear. If the neckline is high, leave the neck jewellery-less and wear chunky earrings. Add some bangles and finger rings and you're set.Makeup: Rosy glow makeup would look perfect with this. Round hoops at your ears and chunky bangles will complete the look.Makeup: To compliment this look we would suggest mauve accents as a preferred makeup looks. Mauve is one of those perfect shades for transitioning from warm weather to cooler temperatures because it feels more dramatic than summery shades. You can endorse a simple sari look, clubbed with natural makeup and light jewelry to mark the occasion. This Diwali fashion trend  will help you keep light and would make your celebration free of fuss. And whoever said, less is more, are obviously right. Try and find out! If you're comfortable in salwar-kameer or sari or a pant-suit or shorts, you should totally rock it with all your confidence, and fashion and trends would follow! 2. Which dress code fits for the Diwali festival? Ideally, people generally prefer wearing traditional outfits like saris, lehengas and salwar-kameer. There are several other varieties of ethnic outfits from regional areas that can be totally your pick this Diwali. If you're celebrating the festival at home, you can go for something that gives you comfort and mobility as well as style. However, if you're spending this festive time outside the home, you can try new trends and styles like ethnic pants, dhoti salwar, among others. Our advice would be to blend comfort and fashion to have a great time. 3. Is it ok to wear a black color dress on Diwali? Several people in Indian people believe that black should not be picked up to wear on Diwali day. Independently, you can decide to wear the color that you want. But, the festive feeling is all about joy and celebration with your loved ones. It's best if you take advice from a family member to avoid hurting any sentiments on this auspicious day. Take a moment and reminisce about the days when we would send out anxious messages to our gang asking them about their outfits. What they were donning for the night? What if our outfits matched? The horror! These momentous precautions have a taken a back seat with changing times.  Matching outfits with your friend is no more a faux pas. Instead, it has become a raging and super fun trend that is here to stay! Twinning as a trend first emerged in South Korea’s K-pop culture. While coordinating your outfits completely is not an anomaly entirely, it can overpower the essence of your real personality and make you look, umm, a little too alike. But hey! We’ve got you covered. Have a look at these simple tips and tricks to ace the twinning game. Go ahead and make that winning statement with your fashion twin! One colour palette, multiple outfitsThis is a great way to flaunt the twin-win look without being too discernible. No worries even if you and bestie have different taste when it comes to styling your clothes. The main idea is to predominantly stay within the same colour palette and explore varied outfits. Think Gigi Hadid’s and Kendal Jenner’s iconic twin ensembles Match your fabricsHere’s an easy breezy example to help you get a better idea about this tip.  You can wear a chic eyelet white cotton dress with and your twin can throw on a white top having a similar eyelet detail. Dressing in tandem with your friend in this way leaves a lot of room for experimentation.  Top to bottom! Bottom to top!Interchanging the colours of your outfit with your BFF can be really fun. Fancy sporting a cute baby pink skirt with a pastel blue top? Your BFF, on the other hand, can rock a baby pink top with a pastel blue skirt. Think out of the boxWhat’s the first thing that comes to your mind when you think about twinning? Matching your garbs, right? While this is the most popular choice, there are some other subtle ways in which you can strut your way into the twin parade. How about getting matching phone covers? You are your fashion twin will be carrying around your phone pretty much everywhere. Bring out those accessories There are a myriad of ways in which you can elevate your twinning game without synchronizing your outfits from head to toe. Add a pair of matching oxidized tribal jhumkas to your ensemble for that subtle yet classy twinning look.  So there you have it! Your very own handy guide which will aid you in conquering this super-fun trend. Lastly, we would just want to remind you that twinning is not about replicating each other’s clothes. Don’t strive to look identical! It is one thing to twin your outfit with a person and another to look like their clone. Maintaining your identity is of crucial importance. Reflect on of your personal sense of style. Ensure that your individual personality shines through your matching outfit. A lot is shouldered by the details therein. The aim is not to look like identical twins. You want to alike but different. You can wear the same shirt but pair it up with different bottoms. Wear dresses with a similar length but different prints. Yes, twinning can be that effortless. She had a Cinderella moment, where the ‘fairy godfather’ flicked his wand, and the black and blue gown by Tommy Hilfiger lit up in blue! This was made possible with technology; the structure inside the dress was made up of metallic plates, LED lights, batteries and wire. At the same event, musician Janelle Monáe wore an exaggerated Christian Siriano balloon-hipped dress that had a motorised blinking eye on one breast! This too was an amalgamation of fashion and technology at its chicest! Katy Perry was one of the foremost though and had worn a LED dress at the Met Gala and during her tour in 2014. It’s not just the celebs that get to wear such high-tech ensembles, even daily wear is getting its fair share of technological advancement. Wrist-worn smart watches or bands have become common in recent years. But, according to a research carried out by UK-based Juniper Research, the trend is shifting to ‘connected clothing’, which is forecasted by them to become $1 billion industry in 2020! Here are some of such cool garments that you can choose from.Jacket phone: What if you could pick up calls, control music volume, and get directions by just taping or brushing the sleeves? Levi and Google have collaborated for a jacket that does just that! Digital yogi: If you’re learning yoga, and want to refine your poses and get them right, these yoga pants are just for you! Brand Nadi X has come up with the pants that sense when your yoga pose needs refining and uses haptic feedback to create small vibrations on the body part you need to adjust.Swimming in sun: We’re always worried about just how much sunscreen to apply when on the beach, wearing swimwear. Brand Neviano has come up with stylish swimsuits that have a water-proof a UV sensor that detects if the UV rays are high and if you need more sunscreen to be applied! Research is also being done on how else to incorporate technology into fashion in order to make our life easier. At Deakin University’s Institute for Frontier Materials, they’re looking into developing fibres that can store energy. They’re hoping to make garments that can be used to charge phones and other small devices. Imagine slipping your discharged phone into your pocket, and it comes out charged! Well, with more and more of our lives getting touched by technology, is this tech-forward fashion really a surprise? You’ll be shedding those heavy jackets and coats and finally be able to show off the latest trends in fashion as you step out. Here’s looking at the trends this season that will have you turn heads. While the previous year was all sorts of the frivolous extravaganza, this year is more about practical functionality with a generous dollop of extra. Animal printsAnimal prints started making the rounds of runways sometime early last year and in filtered into our closets in full force by the end of the year. The predatory prints from the ’80s had made a massive comeback but with the much-needed makeover! The well-known prints are so much chic and oh so covetable now. What was once considered a bold statement for the wild-hearted is now being sported at ease by the shy too. Cheetah, leopard, snake, zebra, you name it and the print is available at your go-to an e-commerce site. Styling an animal print is a little tricky as you do not want to look like you belong to the circus! Steer clear of heavy fabrics like wools and velvets and opt for smooth and silky outfits such as silks and cotton. Start with a skinny leopard printed bodysuit and boyfriend jeans with boots and work your way up to a snakeskin evening gown with strappy black heels and minimalistic jewellery and you’re all set.  Utility dressingRemember days you were looked down upon for leaving your house in oversized sweats and cargo pants? Well, it turns out that you can proudly flaunt your baggy cargo pants and sneaks this year, all thanks to the utility dressing rage! Welcome to 2019 where function meets fashion in the form of unpolished practicality. It is nothing but practical, laid back and super comfortable clothing. 2019 has functionality written all over it. Imagine practical oversized clothing in muted tones. Combat trousers, chic overalls, trench coats, baggy sweats, sneakers are taking the fashion world with a storm and we aren’t complaining one bit. The key to nailing the perfect utility look is to style the pieces. If you haven’t experimented yet, start with styling functional clothing with tailored pieces. Start with layering an army jacket over a solid black jumpsuit or playsuit with black boots and move ahead. Also, you can jazz up your khaki trench coat with a red lip and a silk scarf for the perfect date look or can sport those ‘ugly’ trainers with a sleep skirt suit at work and be practical, comfortable and oh so chic at the same time. Win-win!  Cycling shortsCycling shorts are nothing new; in fact, Princess Diana regularly sported them with crew necks long ago. Fast forward to 2019, and they are easily the biggest trend of the year. They were unmissable on the runaways and have been marking territory in online and offline stores in abundance. And not, not just in the regular black spandex garment we’ve grown up with but jazzed up in pretty colours and prints and embroidery. It goes without saying that the humble piece of sportswear has graduated the fashion ladder by heaps and how. The garment that was once worn for physical activities is now being sported under blazers to the boardroom. And oh, it is Kim Kardashian approved too! Women all across the globe have taken a fancy for these bodycon shorts and are pairing it off with anything and everything. From boardrooms to date nights to soirees, these shorts are hard to miss. You too could dip your toes in the water by the pairing of a solid coloured one with a loose oversized tee for your regular coffee runs and upgrade by sporting metallic ones underneath blingy long blazers. It isn’t clear on if the trend is here to stay or not, but that doesn’t stop it from being everywhere at the moment! Oversized2019 revolves around the word oversized! From oversized unstructured jackets and t-shirts to oversized huge sunnies and hats, there’s no stopping really! (Yep, that means we would have to put away our skinny sunglasses from last season!) While last season was more sleek and minimal in terms of accessories, this season is all about exaggeration in terms of hats, belts, bags, etc. The tote bag has gotten a makeover and has blown out really big! Loud hair bands- studded, leather, satin etc too seem to have maximized. Sunglasses are big and bold with added adornments. Chunky jewellery in a more natural form rather than being polished would be a hit this year. Belts too are broad and oversized. 80’s fashionThe thumb rule of fashion is that each trend resurfaces after a few years. There are some that we can’t stand and some we welcome with open arms, like the 80’s fashion. The retro fashion has gotten a redo and we can’t wait to see it on the streets. Imagine belted high waist denim and power suits in neon (remember Priyanka Chopra?) and fringed mullets and big hair. Puffy sleeves, ruffles and shoulder pads are more fashionable than you thought. Although the style is more refined and structured than what it was before. Shoulder pads blazers mean business and are definitely not going anywhere for a long time. Ruffles trims tops and dress continue selling like hot cakes. Statement sleeves too are in the running. Bipasha Basu Singh GroverIn Falguni Mehta.					 It’s time for all of us to make a resolution to not fall prey to body figure stereotyping and make it all about self-love. Not trying to hide behind frumpy clothes that do you no justice is one way to do that. Finding out and understanding your body type is something to be thankful for, however making it a stereotype is not. So all the apple body-shaped woman, pear body-shaped and also the full-sized hourglass body-shaped ladies, stop being used to the embarrassing yourself, rather start embracing yourself! With numerous brands breaking the beauty taboo with real-body campaigns and policies we celebrate every woman with perfection. If you are curvy, it is important to dress according to your size. Say goodbye to every oversized clothes and slide into the outfits with the right fit that will hide your problem areas and highlight the right angles of your frame. Styling from top to bottom can bring a vast change in your look. Have a look at some great style tips for real girls who felt too voluptuous to wear certain items, and we're here to blow those myths right out of the water. LINES AND SHAPES You need your first impression to be fab-worthy, and it is all about your lines and shapes that draw the eye. One great trick is to wear monochrome ensembles. This makes the viewer’s eye move up to down, or vice versa, forming one uninterrupted line, which makes you look tall and slim. If you’re looking to enhance those curves, then opt for a bodycon dress in the right fabric like jersey. You can also wear ensembles that have lines narrowing at the waist and spreading away at the bust and the hips. The lines can be in the form of a print, stitches, pleats, etc. A dress with a plunging V-neck and a cinched waist which then flairs out below, also gives the illusion of an hourglass figure.  THE RULE OF THE HEM Knowing where hems or borders should be on your body can help you lengthen the frame. A knee-length skirt, for example, should sit just right under the knee, never around the biggest part of the calf.  The hem of the jeans should be at the ankle, or (even better) an inch or two below. If you are not of average height, buy your clothes, specifically the bottoms from a retailer that gives you perfect length options. Well, hems can be tricky sometimes but the best thing is to not to have a clue about it and find a tailor with a good eye, trust them and learn as you go.  SAY 'NO' TO OVERSIZED CLOTHES Just beanpoles look great in larger than the average dress size! Don’t add volume to your body by wearing oversized dresses. Instead, pick the clothes that are body-skimming (not too tight) and show your curvy side. Say no to a giant t-shirt, but a maxi or kaftans that skim the curves and have some belt at the waist is cool. If you want an easy profile, or if you got your favourite graphic on a tee or tunic then pair it with tighter trousers or jeans and make it to your advantage. MIND THE SHOES It’s always a head-to-toe thing and what you put on your feet that matters. Pointy tips and low heels can make you look slim, whether you are pairing it with a skirt or a pair of pants. Try to find a shoe with a vamp the ends at the top of your toes, other than halfway around. Shoe styles with low vamps include ballet flats and pumps. High-vamp shoes include Mary Janes and loafers. WHAT NOW, ACCESSORIES? Long chains, not chokers are good to go, especially if you got classic apple shape and short neck. Your focus should be on creating long, unbroken lines along your body. No mood of jewellery? Grab a long scarf helps for the same effect. Layering your jewellery is another way of drawing the eye vertically. From choker to long chains, layer with a couple of them together. Even when wearing bangles and bracelets, stack them up.  VOTE FOR LAYERS Contrary to stereotypes, layering doesn’t necessarily add volume. Instead, it sometimes gives your body a definition. Wearing a tank top with a pretty cardigan instead of one-piece dress or T-shirt can help to underline your shape.  Ensure though that you don’t layer with bulky garments.  EMBRACE YOUR HIGH WAIST High-waisted pants are your companion. They help tuck in folds and fat and minimize muffin tops since they end at the slimmest part of the waist. Ensure they're long, finishing at the lower leg or underneath, following the rule of the hemline.  Dress to make yourself feel good, and you will make heads turn!  Text: Akruti Khandkar 													Step into summers with a fresh hair style to set the tone of the season right. Only issue: You’ve worn them a number of times last season and they just don’t feel that special anymore. How you wish your boots had some colour or a fringe or even a shiny buckle. Sigh! Fret not. With some easy fix tricks, you can upgrade your boots to the latest fashion trends of this season and always stay in style! Buckle up!What you need: Belts, scissors, hot glue.How to make: Cut your belt measured according to the roundness of your boot at the calf. Use hot glue to attach your belt onto your boot. Hold it in place and let it dry. Cut off any unwanted extra belt length and buckle it around your boot. Add extra notches if required. You can repeat the same procedure using more belts with different colours or textures and you have your very own cowgirl boots! Cool cutsWhat you need: Ruler, penknife, chalk.How to make: Draw or trace the design of your choice onto your boot using chalk. Size your grid according to your liking. Use the pen knife to cut out the parts you wish to keep hollow. Once done, wipe off the chalk marks with a damp cloth and you cut out boots are ready. This DIY is easier to work with semi-thick leather that won’t lose shape or tear after cutting. Dazzling tipsWhat you need: Paintbrush, gold/silver pearl shine paint, a thick masking tape, fixative sprayHow to make: Add masking tape a few centimetres away from the tip of the boot. Press firmly. Paint using the gold or silver paint making sure the paint doesn’t go under the tape. Paint smooth and even coats to get a smooth surface. Allow it to dry for a couple of hours and remove the tape. Wipe off any stray dried up paint. Spray on the fixative spray and let it dry for 24 hours. And voila! Lace all dayWhat you need: Lace, pins (if required) and fabric glue.How to make: Cut strips of lace that is long enough to go around your boot. Arrange your pattern and pin it so it holds your desired shape. Using tiny amounts of glue, attach it to your boot. Let it dry completely. You can even add a few beaded chains and feathers for a complete boho look. Retro kicksWhat you need: Masking tape, matte finish paint, brush, scissors.How to make: Cut pieces of the masking tape and stick them onto your boot in any desired shape. You can make a star shape or go abstract and stick the tape onto your boot in any way you like. Once this is done, paint over the design you've created using any matte finish paint of your choice. Let it dry and peel the tape off slowly to reveal your design. Continue making more designs or simply stick the tape in equidistant parallel lines to create stripes for a sporty look.Text: Yvonne Jacob 													The glamour industry revolves around fashion cycles and trends that dominated once, have returned to claim their spot again. After changing three flights and taking a three-hour bus ride, we landed in Montepuez—the second largest city in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique. The day had been a whirlwind, as we hopped on and off different vehicles. The moment we landed in Mozambique, however, a burst of fresh, clean air welcomed us. The quaint city is home to Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM), which is a Mozambican company developing operations at the ruby deposits in the city, and covers approximately 33,600 hectares. A leading supplier of responsibly-sourced coloured gemstones across the globe, MRM is owned by UK-based natural resource company Gemfields (75 per cent), and Mozambican company Mwiriti (25 per cent). We spent two days in the heart of the most recently discovered ruby deposit in the world, and unearthed more than just these precious crimson stones. 													The journey beginsOver 500 million years in the making, ruby, or ratnaraj (meaning king of the gemstones in ancient Sanskrit), is an extremely rare stone, cherished by royalty, social A-listers, and collectors alike. We went to see one of the mine pits on the first day, where rubies are deposited as alluvial or colluvial material over a weathered bedrock.Rubies were first discovered in Montepuez in 2009, following which, Gemfields and Mwiriti signed an agreement in 2011 to officiate the mining process. MRM uses a multidisciplinary approach for mining—geological (rubies that are typically associated with certain rocks or minerals), geophysical (airborne survey—magnetic and radiometric), and geochemical (determining chemical signatures of hidden mineral deposits). The sheer size of the mine pit was staggering, and it brought forth the concern of what happens to it once it has been exhausted.Mining with a conscienceMRM is committed to mining in a way that has the least environmental impact. Jack Cunningham, Sustainability, Policy and Risk Director at Gemfields, explains, “Before we mine an area, we collect seeds of the indigenous plants and trees from the top soil and create a seed bank. We then grow the seeds in a nursery for replanting as we complete mining.” Along with encouraging biodiversity, old pits are back-filled and rehabilitated, and no harmful chemicals are used during the mining process. “Machine oil is carefully managed and stored, machines and vehicles are maintained by our in-house teams, and all spills are cleaned up and the contaminated soil is bioremediated,” says Cunningham.The road to development was not an easy one, and initially, the company faced resistance from the inhabitants. Cunningham recalls, “There was uncertainty from the local community about what the benefits would be and how quickly they would receive those. An influx of thousands of illegal miners also caused social problems at a time when we weren’t yet in a position to help the community. Since 2014, however, we have had a dedicated team on the ground that carries out community engagement, and addresses their needs and grievances, and the relationship with them has vastly improved.” MRM has provided employment to 1,110 people, both directly and via contractors, 95 per cent of whom are Mozambican nationals. The mining company has also helped nine farming associations (two of which are dedicated to empowering women and in total represent 290 partner farmers), and taught them new techniques that have increased yields. Looking at the community as a whole, the company has invested in infrastructure for four primary schools (three of which are new), providing education to 1,000 primary school-aged children. “Schooling is the responsibility of the state, however our infrastructure atleast helps the government with a costly aspect of public education. Once established, we hand over the schools to the government for their onward management as a national asset,” elucidates Cunningham. The establishment of two mobile health clinics serves thousands of people across six villages. Isac Rafael, Director of the Namanhumbir Health Center, Mozambique, stated, “With these mobile clinics, it’s possible to care for patients in the most remote areas without sanitary units. This also gives easy access to pregnant women, children, and the elderly, who don’t have to travel long distances.”The final stepWe spent the last leg of our journey in the wash plant and sorting house, where the raw stones are processed and graded according to their colour, size, and clarity. We witnessed how a team of highly skilled sorters picked rubies from the rubble, in a secure environment. Their hands worked like machines as they separated the precious stones in silent harmony. The final pieces are then auctioned off by Gemfields and till June 2017, a total of eight ruby auctions have generated a revenue of US$280 million.We entered the city with a bunch of preconceived notions, and after spending two days in the shoes of a miner, left with hope for the Montepuez community. That’s what you get in this city of Mozambique, along with beautiful never-ending blue skies, and a warm community that believes in co-existence. FASHIONHigh glossNothing screams power more than high shine fabrics worn appropriately. While last season was all about plastics in apparel, this season is all about high gloss on any and every fabric texture such as leather, satin etc. Right from long wrap-around coats to pants to even see-through dresses, high shine is marking its territory everywhere. But beware if worn out of proportion or styled incorrectly, the trend sure can fall back easily. The best way to start would be with a high shine statement belt on a solid outfit and move upwards to high gloss trimmings on outfits and then take the plunge! “I feel high gloss fabrics can somehow add sheer sexiness to the look. I personally love wearing statement gloss t-shirt dresses and black or nude shoes,” says lifestyle blogger Naina Ahluwalia. Plaid and simpleThe key to play with plaid is to not go overboard with it and style it with colourful bright accessories to brighten up the look. “If you ask me about plaid, I can only and only think of the term classic yet trendy. Plaid can be played around with prints and colours but it's not a trend, I would call it an evergreen print that everyone needs to have in their closet. Of course, every year something or the other trendy using plaid comes up and those make good additions to the closet,” shares lifestyle blogger Aleena Macker. You can try your hand at plaid button-down skirts or bright plaid co-ordinates or even plaid mules, there’s no stopping this season. Add a dollop of feminine to plaid through glam jewellery, bold lips or bling bags and watch your style quotient go through the roof!Fringe benefits The best part about the fringe trend is its versatility. Not only can you incorporate these sassy strings into your wardrobe but you can also sport it through any medium i.e. through an accessory or clothing piece or even footwear. “You have a variety of different options when it comes to fringes. You can play around with beads or metallic ropes or even denim, the list just goes on and on,” says fashion blogger Puja Wani, “A well-fitted tee with fringes on denim looks really chic for the day and pair a contemporary sari with a fringed noodle strap crop makes heads turn at a social soirée!” ACCESSORIESSkinny sunglassesWe are totally crushing big time on skinny sunglasses to go along with our skinny tall soy lattes. Trust us when we say that a pair of these can totally escalate your look within seconds. What started with a few sightings on Instagram influencers has only gone up on the fashion ladder with everybody adapting to the style. One thing is for sure, the 90’s skinny game is here to stay for a while and you could try experimenting with the same. While the black skinnies sure do seem like a classic, there are a lot of varieties to choose from. Imagine bags with tiny fur trims and pearls and fabric patches with logos or numbers. The size of these goodies ranges from tiny shoulder bags to handbags to even totes! A great bag can make or break the look and these embellished bags undeniably enliven the look in a jiffy. With Chanel kicking off the trend early this year and going crazy with plastic covered everything, most designers followed suit.
