EMPIRE STATE OF MINDEmpire waistlineThe first and most recognisable waistline there is the empire waistline also popularly referred to as the empire silhouette, empire line or just empire style. The basic structure of this waist pattern is categorised by the tightly fitted bodice that ends just below the bust to deliver the whole high-waisted look. The obsession with the high-waisted line began during the 18th century and was brought to fame by the empress of the first French Empire, Napoleon Bonaparte’s wife, Empress Josephine de Beauharnais; which is where the whole regal reference is sourced from. If a style was good enough for an empress, you can be sure it’s good enough for you as well. The entire style is part of the neoclassical style that was obsessed with imitating and replicating or rather reviving the style that could be seen in the ancient Greek and Roman which portrayed women wearing long gowns clinched under the bust.Perhaps it's old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the style a wonderfully romantic appeal. The flowy and really luxurious feel it imparts makes your inner Greek goddess preen with appreciation, accompanied with the fact that it’s incredibly comfy with zero constriction is an advantage that has very women sighing in absolute relief. Its old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the empire waistline style a wonderfully romantic appeal.Match-maker: The empire waist is designed in such a way that it sits above a woman's natural waistline and generally accentuates the bust which is why it is ideally always accompanied with deep scoop necklines or sweetheart and V-necklines.   This style is perfect for those with pear-shaped bodies i.e. having a slim upper body and a more voluptuous lower body. As such if you don’t want to draw attention to your hips then empire waistline is the way to go. The waist tends to emphasise the narrowest part of the body and camouflaging the wider lower body. It’s also great for short people because the raised waistline creates the appearance of extra height. Now, for the don’ts - avoid the billowy, voluminous fabrics. Pleats and gathers are another no-nos.It is best to stick to with A-line structures or sheath that help to highlight your body’s best features instead of hiding it under too much fabric. When wearing an empire waist top, the best choice of bottom wear is either skinny or straight legged pants. Pairing it up with voluminous wide-legged tend it delivers a rather frumpy, disproportionate look. Empire waist dresses are ideal for pregnant women as its flowy and comfortable. DROP DOWNDrop waistAfter the waistline was pulled up to new heights, the winds of change eventually made their way through the world of fashion and according to the laws of the universal: what goes up must come down. So after the waistline enjoyed the lofty highs, during the roaring 20s, it dropped down to become the distinctive dropped waist style. Around the time when women were finally breaking free from a vile instrument of torture also known as the corset, they decided to adopt more masculine silhouettes. It was believed to be seen as female liberation from traditionally-accepted shapes. A dropped waist sits below the actual natural waistline of a woman and is characterised by the line across the hips instead of the waist thereby providing the illusion of a longer torso. The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival. During then the look took on a sportier feel rather than the elegantly sleek feminine look of the 20’s. Designers have experimented around with it for years and while the basic construct was never tampered with, there were several add-ons like belts, pleated and ruffled skirts to give it a little extra something every time.The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival.Match-maker: Dropped waisted looks aren’t quite as popular today as they were before but they haven’t faded into obscurity completely because the whole ‘shapeless’ look is on the prowl and is extremely favoured. The waist makes quite a statement and, if you know just how to wear and accessorise it, it can turn you into an über fashionista who knows how to work any style like a boss. Short drop-waisted look looks fantastic on women with the tall slender willowy figures and narrow hips. With the addition of a ruffled skirt for a flouncy free-flowing look or an A-line skirt for a sleeker formal look, it could swing either way. It would be prudent for women who have a heavier lower half to stay away from the ruffles as it would be super counterproductive and make the lower body look even wider.For those with long legs and a short torso, drop-waisted dress - with moderate heels - works well. And for those with a long torso and short legs, drop waists with high heels will help to balance out the long torso and deliver a balanced, symmetrical look. BASQUE IN ITBasque waistlineWhat could you have in common with a woman who lived during the American Civil War? Nothing much; except maybe your dress’s waistline. The Basque waistline, which is also referred to as the antebellum waistline is a waistline that emerged when the hourglass figure was the shape every woman was vying for. This waistline served to flatter the equally proportioned body of an hourglass shape and has merits for other body types as well.A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures. The style forms a noticeable ‘V’ on the front of the body coming 2-3 inches below the normal waistline. If the pronounced V-shape is too sharp for one’s taste and then the style can also be modified to a softer U-shape. It is a generally flattering style that provides a slimmer and longer torso due to its low ‘V’ and reduces the width of the hips and waist. Though the idea is to love your body no matter what, wanting to take off a couple for inches every now and then using illusionary means is perfectly acceptable. The style originally began as French-fitted bodice or jacket that eventually become part of the dress rather than a separate piece altogether. A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures.Matchmaker: A Basque waistline is flattering for many body shapes; the low V-shaped line lengthens the torso and creates a wonderfully slim silhouette. However, due to the shape of the waistline, the style tends to draw distinct attention to the lower tummy region and if you aren’t comfortable with that then it's best to avoid this style. Pear-shaped bodies or square shaped bodies should not go for this kind of waistline as it would not be able to appropriately accentuate and flatter those kinds of body types. Hourglass and other body types would be able to carry it off perfectly as it helps to balance out the hips and waist due to the elongation illusion the waist creates.   LOSE THE SYMMETRYAsymmetric waistlineThings that are straight and simple are thoroughly uninteresting after a while. In order to shake things up, the fashion industry developed an obsession with everything that was off-centre and unbalanced. And that is because things like that tend to be more interesting. There is more depth, character and visual appeal. From hemlines with varying lengths to slanted necklines, there is something about asymmetrical patterns in an attire that just make the whole look more sophisticated and bold while breaking free from the rigid symmetry.Though an asymmetrical waistline is not as radical as some of the other things in the same school of thought, it is an interesting style to incorporate. An asymmetrical waistline is a style that sits diagonally across the natural waistline. It originates from a point in the natural waistline and then extends down in a slant to the opposite end. In other words, it is just a slanted waistline across your body, high on one side and low on the other.Asymmetrical waistline creates a slimming effect for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies.Match-maker: Asymmetrical waistline is a type of waistline that will create a slimming effect. Thus, it is great for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. WAIST NOT, WANT NOTPrincess seamThe absence of something is often beneficial as well. Though there exist several types of waistlines to go with every kind of body, there is a particular style that does not need a visible waistline. A style that is much beloved and which is about as timeless as the name itself - the princess seam style. It is a style that will probably never go out of style and is an epitome of soft feminity.A princess seam or line is characterised by the long seams that start from below the arm, or under the shoulder and curves delicately over the bust and down the body to give a prominent long look that that associated with A-line dresses. The seam can be stitched into blouses or dresses to have the desired structure and shape. Due to the way it is designed, the style does not need a waistline since it runs along panels down the body. The princess seam was associated with Charles Frederick Worth, a prominent English fashion designer of the 19th and 20th century who is also acknowledged by many as the ‘Father of Haute Couture’. The style was of course created for Princess Alexandra of Denmark, the wife of King Edward VII. Due to its fitted and figure-hugging design, it was believed to be the first ‘bodycon’ (who are we to deny that fact?).The princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.Match-maker: The princess seam works remarkably well for those with hourglass figures, the long, shapely seams that gather in at the waist and flare out again at the hips. However, the princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.  It’s a wardrobe staple for every lady, kind of like a good pair of shoes or an LBD. Or better yet an LBD with princess seams is a very acceptable option as well.  Either way, knowing what looks good on your unique body is the first step to being fashionably perfect every day but the personal interpretations and add-ons are what make the outfit your identity.  Text: Crystal SymssImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock					Cover storyMonochrome jackets look both trendy and sophisticated. Co-founded by Jayesh Sachdev, it was a venture to bring his art to many through fashion and décor. What he didn’t know was that all their products will be sold out within the first week. Their quirky – as their name rightly suggests – designs are well appreciated and have had many takers even amongst the celebs like Deepika Padukone, Ranveer Singh, Priyanka Chopra, Alia Bhatt, Parineeti Chopra, Amitabh and Abhishek Bachchan, Kangana Ranaut and Kajol. The brand defines itself as a fashion and lifestyle label that exudes wearable eccentricity. “That, in addition to rich colour, graphic art and playful sophistication define our essence,” Sachdev mentions in the brand information, “We are synonymous with all things fun, offbeat and quirky. Our exuberant approach to the everyday encourages personal style with a dash of incandescent charm. We call it life in technicolor.” An artist by passion, a designer by choice and a creative entrepreneur by vocation, Sachdev talks about the brand, his journey and making people a walking gallery. It shouldn’t have been such a surprise though. Sachdev is an artist, designer and entrepreneur. He graduated with a Degree in Visual Communication at Lasalle College of the Arts, Singapore and holds the national record for having painted India’s largest concept artwork. Alongside running the Quirk Box, he continues to practice as an artist, exhibiting through New York to Bombay. He has won many awards including British Council Young Arts Entrepreneurs India 2008, Tiger Translate India Arts Awards and Crow Bar Asia Advertising Awards and he is also a credited TEDx speaker. Apart from his art, he is an avid photographer and loves to play tennis. Quirk Box also, is an award-winning label, alongside its founder. It won the Best Urban Wear Label – India award at Grazia Young India Fashion Awards in 2015. They have showcased their collection at the Lakme Fashion Week since 2013. In previous interviews, the artist-designer who is inspired by Sabyasachi and Manish Arora told the story behind Quirk Box, “There is an oddity and sense of innovation that is a virtue of Quirk Box. This oddity, this quirkiness, and this implicit need to be original and fun put together are what we like to call the Quirk Box. We’re here to be different and carve a niche of our own in this ever-growing industry. The strategy is to only provide fresh, quirky and unimaginable designs to our customers and reach out to prospects that haven’t yet been exposed to quirky fashion and lifestyle.” Living up to its story and its name, each collection by this brand has been unique and out-of-the-box. Not one to follow trends, but to set them, he has kept true to the essence of the brand with each collection, having come up with new and interesting prints every time. “Our USP is our strong understanding of design and fashion and our inherent traits of wanting to create something original each time,” he explains, “We are not aping trends, even though our works have a very strong ‘pop art’ essence, we are neither imitating designs, nor finding inspiration from Bollywood/Hollywood or popular culture, we are constantly striving to create innovative art that spells individuality.” Sachdev and his brand are all about expressing their art through various mediums, and thus was the Quirk Box Design Studio born. “I am primarily a visual artist,” tells the man who believes that ‘design is art with a function and business is applying that design into context’, “I have no formal understanding of fashion. My art and illustration aesthetic are what makes Quirk Box distinguished. The art that is made for Quirk Box is put into fashion, but fashion is only one such medium onto which my art can be applied to. We can design your space, your business identity, textile prints, wedding cards… the scope is diverse and limitless.” Through this independent design studio, the design style that is inherently Quirk Box can be hired as a service and not just as a product. We have a tête-à-tête with Sachdev talking of the milestones he’s reached in his journey till now, his inspirations and aspirations. Can you tell in brief about your journey to date?It's been a decade that I've been an artist; so it’s clearly been a long and exciting one. I started out as a Jr. Art Director at an agency in Singapore, after graduating from an art school. I eventually moved back to India to start Emblem, my design studio. That didn’t initially kick off the way I'd have imagined and I occupied myself painting. Before I knew it, I'd become a full-time artist. I founded Emblem Tee, and the Emblem Art Gallery and later Quirk Box. I like to believe I'm a creative entrepreneur as much as an artist. Along the way I picked up a few accolades and awards, it's been a frustrating, enriching and a learning journey, and I'm probably not even close to halfway where I'd like to be. Were art and design something you wanted to pursue from the start?I wanted to write. I wanted to play tennis and football. When I didn’t end up pursuing those as career options, I had a strong idea that I would be inclined towards a Visual Arts career. What inspires you to create?There is something magical and whimsical about creation. You have freedom. I enjoy this freedom of being a creator.  What inspired you to start Quirk Box?As an artist, you tend to have a limited audience. Often affluent or far too niche and restricted. This meant all my creative ideas and visions would manage to reach a small audience. I hoped that a lot more people could firstly, witness my art and secondly, afford it. Quirk Box was started to be a functional art label. Instead of buying my art on a canvas, you could now buy it as a garment. When you wear Quirk box, you are a walking gallery of my imagination. You started with an online store, and haven’t gone for the traditional retail format. Was that a conscious decision? Do you plan to have your own store in the future?The idea was always the penetration of the market. If you've lived in one place too long, you become a frog in a pond. You have to go out there and tell your story to everyone. I didn’t want to be tied to a physical space. I needed my art to be everywhere. And online allows me to reach 200 countries as opposed to one specific location that a brick and mortar are about.Since the start, you have come up with out-of-the-box designs. How has the response been?We turned seven in April. It's been wonderful. We've dressed commoners and celebrities alike. Won the awards that mattered and got the features that matter. We've sold from Pune to Peru. I have much to be grateful for. How’s the Quirk Box journey been till date? Can you tell us in brief about the milestones in this journey?When we started out seven years ago, we started out wanting to create something exciting. We had unrealistic ambitions, we wanted to reach the entire country, but a part of me believed I was being delusional to expect it. A week into our launch we were sold out and we realised we had created something larger than we knew. It has been a learning curve. Meeting incredibly talented people, incredible experiences, winning relevant awards, dressing fashion goddesses, it opened new windows of opportunities and experiences, from the fashion weeks to dressing A-listers. It's been a long tough exciting ride.Where do you get your inspiration from when you come up with new collections?Inspiration is everywhere. We find inspiration from our experiences and surroundings. There is no preset for this. Every day is a new experience and ideas are ever evolving. The fabrics you choose, the prints, the colours… Why do you choose what you do?I make art that I chose to make. We do not restrict ourselves with the art. The freedom of creating is why we started this. This is not trending determined. The fabrics that are chosen based on the season, cotton would work in warmer weathers, crepe and silks in the festive season. Since we print a multitude of colour, we also need to pick fabrics that allow us to print the kind of art we make. We also try to keep our prices in-check so the fabrics determine the same. Can you tell us about your latest collection?Our summer collection Chikanobu was inspired by the 18th-century Woodcut Artworks of the Japanese Artist Toyohara. I love all things Japanese, and Japanese art was something I've always been intrigued by. My wife Priyanka who is now the Chief Illustrator at Quirk Box was truly inspired by the idea of recreating his works in a contemporary context. The artworks of Emperor Meiji, the Japanese Cranes, Waves and Geisha's all features as artworks in the series of our Summer Resort wear. We used Crepe this season. It is light in weight and the blend we use is easy on sweat, heat and wash care.Who is your inspiration? I am inspired by my travel experiences. Food, small, the unknown that is exciting brings with it new stories to tell. Stories that we tell through art and fashion. Your most and least favourite parts of designing?Every day at work is a challenge; a new challenge. The amalgamation of art and business is something I am excited by. I thrive on this. Having to solve internal conflicts of tailor/labour is a rather annoying part of the profession though.What in your opinion is your biggest achievement so far?That I am able to sustain art in a country that has no value for it, is my biggest achievement. Quirk Box was one of the first of its kind with the designs that you came up with. These days there are many who do similar or “inspired” designs. Your take on plagiarism in the industry.Everything is an inspiration, and everything is a copy… some more than others. I see a tree and I draw it. I copy from nature. Some see the drawing of my tree and copy it. Unfortunately, due to the weak intellectual property laws and ambiguities, this won’t change anytime soon. In the meanwhile, we have to believe that imitation is the best form of flattery.Being an artiste and a designer, how do you balance the two facets?They are integrated. One fuels a passion, one fuels the bills. Can you tell us a little about Quirk Box Design?Quirk Box is an independent boutique art-based design studio. It offers crafted solutions for all your design needs.  With over 10 years of experience in the design space, including branding, graphics and fashion, the studio offers the same philosophy and principle of its original art and design and strong aesthetic essence, that is no longer limited to its in-house label, but to anyone that would like to hire its service. having worked with fashion, art, graphic design, branding, advertising, space design, the brand now offers you a design language you need, keeping intact the graphic art and playful sophistication that defines our essence. Can you tell us a little about your next collection?Our next is our most ambitious collection yet. Given the detail of the work, we are still working against the clock to release it in time for August. But hopefully, it will see the light of day soon.What do you envision the future holding for you?I wish I could foretell the future. But I can only hope. Hope to create good work, hope that it continues to be appreciated. Hope that I can sustain a lifestyle that allows me to travel extensively.What is your advice to the upcoming designers and fashion entrepreneurs?They don't need my advice. They need self-belief, courage and perseverance.					Sleeves are an element of fashion that has undergone some drastic upgrades, variations and evolutions in the last century. So whether you want to channel the Elizabethan age of over-the-top opulence or free-spirited bohemian vibes, there is a sleeve for every kind of whim and fancy. Like everything in the fashion industry, there is a time when some styles rise above the rest to become the look and talk of the season and the sleeves making waves (literally) this season are a mix of delightful throwbacks and modern sophisticated elegance. Bell of the ballBell sleeve is a super cute and fun style that is making a comeback to the fashion scene. The bell sleeves have been much beloved for their flowy design that allows easy movement and for their uber-graceful feminine appearance. In its previous lives, bell sleeves started their journey out by simply being a flared sleeve that was a part of the Japanese Heian period. A long dramatic flared sleeve was a classic feature and style norm back in the day. It then migrated across the world into the European medieval era and was predominately a style that was seen in the outfits of members of the church clergy. And it was around that time that the sleeve slowly and steadily developed its signature bell structure.The elite class of the Elizabethan era adored the bell sleeves. And as 'less is more' was not a phrase that the stylists of the Elizabethan era particularly believed in at the time, they decided to make it more extravagant (because, why not?) By adding on various embellishments like frills, lace and pleats . After which, the sleeves safely made their way into the modern world wherein the bell shape became more distinct and was synonymous with gentle femininity.The bell sleeves have been around for a long time and are likely to be around for a good bit more too considering the comebacks it makes every few years, seamlessly incorporating itself into the latest fashion trends. Though the bell structure is highly appreciated in the form of sleeves, its other variant 'the bell bottoms' weren't so lucky. But the world of fashion is a strange and unpredictable place. You never know what might pop up again.Why, though? Why has this simple little style managed to stick around for so long? Well, it because bell sleeves are enormously versatile. They have comfortably made themselves a perfectly fashionable asset in every area. From chic work wear to flirty casual and elegant evening wear, bell sleeves can be brought to every area of ââinterest. (Multipurpose utility? Yes, please). It is also wearable in a range of different fabrics as well as wool, lace and silk.How to style: Bell sleeves are great for any kind of occasion. And they come in several different variations, the fitted sleeve with bell flare starting only at the wrist or at the elbow. This is great for people wanting a combination of two styles; full-fitted sleeve and bell sleeve. When it comes to styling it for a classy, ââhigh fashion workwear ensemble, bell sleeves that tie at the elbow add that dash of sleek with a mild dose of flounce. Paired with some tailored pants make an effortless fashionable work-wear look that will help get rid of those Monday blues. Sheer silk blouses sporting bell sleeves are perfect for decadent evening wear and is super comfortable. Cap-tain of styleIf there was ever a voting poll to decide which is the 'all-time favorite sleeve' then cap sleeves would probably win hands down. Cap sleeves give us a feel of soft femininity, throwing it back to those long dreamy gowns with adorable cap sleeves that Keira Knightley wore to the ball in Pride and Prejudice (Who wouldn't want to pretend to be in that situation?). It is a representation of simple, uncomplicated design that is made for everyone. Their modest design is probably why they have been a part of bridal gowns and bridesmaids dress for a long time. The first record of cap sleeves being included into wedding attire has been traced back to the roaring 1920s and then made their way into everyday party wear fashion as well (flapper dresses anyone?).After that, the beloved cap sleeves cruised their way into the 30s, 40s and 50s. Clearly, fashion couldn't let them go and for good reason. It was made widely popular and sealed its place as timeless style when the biggest celebrities showcased their little cap sleeves of the most important day of their lives: their wedding. Scores of celebrities and royalty have sported cap-sleeved wedding gowns and strengthened its reputation as a favored design. When Jackie Kennedy Onassis wed John Kennedy in 1953 in her beautiful cap-sleeved gown, the style's popularity shot through the roof. Mega style icon Audrey Hepburn wore a cap-sleeve wedding dress in her movie 'Funny Face' in 1957 and that made it official, the cap sleeves were here to stay.The most recent ambassador for the beloved cap sleeve is the ever popular sister of the Duchess of Cambridge herself, Pippa Middleton. The fashion world will probably never forget the day she stepped out in that immaculate form-fitting cap-sleeved white gown on the day of the royal wedding. The wedding was not the only historic thing that happened that day. Pippa, with endless grace and panache, brought the caps back into the fashion scene. And it did not end there. When it was Pippa's turn to tie the knot, she dazzled the world again with another cap-sleeved beauty. Cap-sleeved elegance at its finest ladies!How to style: Though it is extremely favored in the wedding scene, bell sleeves are also quite flexible and can be showcased in everyday fashion as well. Along with it being a part of the usual suspects of western wear ie dresses and tops, you can even bring this style a little closer to home. Embellished high-necked sari blouses with cap-sleeves are exceptionally gorgeous and are a great way to amp up your traditional wear. Bishop sleeveBishop sleeves are sleeves that are quite similar to a bell sleeve, however, they have one defining feature. The full-length sleeves have a familiar flare that flows from the shoulder but it ends with a wide cuff that is gathered and cinched at the wrist. The style emulates a luxurious vintage feel. And it should rightfully because this style has been around for a long time. Though the sleeves are similar to the shape to the sleeves worn by bishops of the church- hence the name - but traces of the flouncy sleeves go even further back in time to the sixth-century Byzantine era (Kudos to them for probably being the oldest sleeve style ever). Though they were not all that prevalent during that time, bishop sleeves become a lot more common during the 1800s.Bishop sleeves got major traction back in the mid-60s during the time when the free-spirited hippie culture was making a statement in society. The relaxed flowing look it created coincided perfectly with the hippie style and they were all for it. Further on, in the 70s and 80s, the sleeves were made of lycra and polyesters to maintain the soft bouncy look that was its biggest selling point. Bishop sleeves created a flattering, balanced silhouette that made a person's shoulders look smaller in comparison. The cuff, historically, is a wide button cuff but over the years, it went through many reconstructions. Elasticized cuffs, embellished cuffs and cuffs with decorative trimmings were all a part of the advancements the bishop sleeves underwent to meet the ever-changing fashion demands.The distinctive shape of the bishop sleeve also attributes it to be known as balloon sleeves. They are also believed to be similar to peasant sleeves due to the fact that they both gather around the wrist. However, the difference is that peasant sleeves ideally tend to puff out at the shoulders, while bishop sleeves just flow smoothly from the shoulder down the arm for a nice draped effect. Peasant sleeves also do not possess a wide cuff but rather have a simple elastic band.How to style: Bishop sleeves are very distinctive and make quite a statement with their classically vintage look. Hence, they are great for formal blouses. Paired with a fitted high-waisted pant to emphasize the sleeves and create a stunning silhouette that just all of the soft sophistication; in other words, high fashion boss lady. For a look that's more casual Fridays, pair it with jeans instead. Draped bishop sleeves add a perfect little dramatic flair to a short loose dress with some strappy wedges or flats and you've basically got you're boho-chic on. Or a fitted dress that flatters your natural curves along with flowing sleeves is perfect for desk to dinner days. Keeping up with the kimono sleeveJapan's foremost export into the world of fashion is the traditional kimono and most popularly the kimono sleeve has carved its place into the fashion scene for the smooth elegant effect that it gave. Traditionally, the type of kimono a person wore would be a marker that officially denoted their social standing, rank and occupation. Well, clothes tend to have that effect even now in a rather unofficial, unspoken way. Nevertheless, the sleeve style eventually made its way across to the western world towards the end of the 1940s.Traditional Japanese wide kimono sleeves are varied in lengths. The sleeves of the kimono's that were used in theatrical performances tending to almost 3 feet long and would drag across the floor for spectacularly dramatic effect. Imagine walking into a party with 3 foot long sleeves (instant show stopper). Unfortunately, that wouldn't be the most practical thing to wear in the real world, so the sleeves were cut down to size to suit more normal measurements. Ideally, kimono sleeves have a deep armhole and the sleeve does not have a definite shoulder seam or armhole seam, which is its peculiarity. The main body of the garment and the sleeve are created from the same continuous piece of material, it, therefore, is also known as a 'grown-on' sleeve.How to style: Kimono sleeves are the trend this season and are perfect for wrap dresses, cinched-in waist secured with a sash that completely the whole traditional kimono look as a whole. Kimono sleeves are also great for sheer or silk blouses that go well with pants or pencil skirts. Shrugs with long kimono sleeves are an excellent way of adding a chic layer to casual jeans and tank top outfit. Cape wonder sleeveCape sleeves and capes are on the list of trending items this season. It's a cool look that speaks of elevated style and if you know just how to wear it and accessorize it, it can be a striking feature in your fashion diaries. Cape sleeves are can be traced back to the past with the introduction of the cloak. Capes were basically an outer garment that draped over the wearer and covered the shoulders, arms and was fastened at the neck. They were super popular back in medieval Europe (Try not to think of long Dracula-esque cape). After their heyday back in the dark ages, capes are back in the modern age to make a style statement unlike any other with designers offering new spins and innovations on trend to make classy and impart a sense of regality because every girl deserves to be a queen .Cape sleeves are most popularly seen on jackets - as the cape is essentially made for outerwear - that has been upgraded with bold new patterns, interesting new fabrics and showcased in varying lengths for every kind of occasion. The sleeves can either in be flared if made with softer fabrics or can be straight and sleek for a more defined structure.How to style: Cape sleeves are great on blazers and because the fabric is stiffer, the silhouette you acquire is impeccably sleek and very flattering; perfect for when you evolve from boss lady to modern queen! It is ideal for smart elegant formal wear or can be used to dress up a basic and top ensemble for a night out. Long flared, looser cape sleeves work well on dresses for an ultra-majestic look or on light pastel colored tops for those casual brunch days. Pick out any one of this season's trendiest sleeves and work it like a boss. Text: Crystal Symss Images: Yogen Shah Like history, fashion sure has a way of resurrecting back. Well, this year, fashionistas have re-adopted trends from the 90’s and we aren’t complaining one bit. One look around the fashion circle, and you’d be able to spot them! “This season is all about picking up trends from the 90’s decade and styling them with your own personal twist,” believes Azmeen Madhani Molo, fashion expert, Blush boutique. Stylist Chaitali Banavalikar-Kulkarni informs, “90s were a total game changer since people became more experimental about their style, rather than focusing on what a particular group of people are wearing.” These are our top picks for the season, have a look on how to style and slay these looks!					Of staple stringsThis quite modest piece of string worn across the neck dates back to 2500 BC! From denoting prostitution to denoting lesbianism, the choker has travelled quite practically everywhere. The choker, now sitting proudly in jewellery cases gained its due attention in the 1900’s because of Queen Alexandra of England when she flaunted one to hide a small scar. It further garnered attention when people started wearing plastic chokers in 1990’s. From Gwyneth Paltrow flashing one at the 1999 Academy Awards to Paris Hilton and Rihanna, every fashion diva has surrendered to the choker game. Back home, Zeenat Aman was one of the first celebrities to rock a choker. Of course, these days the humble choker has enjoyed popularity as celebrities such as Sonam Kapoor, Priyanka Chopra, etc. exhibit various types of choker including diamonds, lace, velvet, beads, leather, shoelace (Yep, even a shoelace can be worn as a choker!) Not only is it super stylish, it is also easy on the pocket and comes with a guarantee of making you seem like an Insta- goddess! Chokers are literally the easiest way to make you seem like you belong to the ‘you can’t sit with us’ tribe. The 90s saw the ‘it’ crowd styling their plastic cord with denim shorts and crops.Style guide: Chokers are something that could be worn throughout the day and beyond.  The strand science is pretty easy to grasp. (No Einstein IQ required here!). The only deciding factor to keep in mind to wear one is the neckline of the outfit that you would be wearing it with. Now, you could wear a dainty ribbon cord for a super casual day out in denim and a tee or could go glam displaying an extravagant bold crystal version with an off-shoulder gown. You could also parade around in multi-layered chokers by pairing them with low neckline outfits. “Chokers are in but can get common these days. Mix it up with a layer of other neck pieces of various lengths to give it a new and different look,” shares designer Neha Sharma. Moving on to traditional outfits, nothing like an Indian-ised version of a choker to pair with a lehenga for your oh-so-important mehendi function. Put together a statement piece of a pearl droplet choker with a sheer black sari and be prepared to make heads turn at the soiree! Return of the coy cropA moment of applause for Madeline Vionnet for if it wasn’t her, we really wouldn’t have been offered the cropped fashion. In 1932, Madeline Vionnet designed an evening gown with strategically cut openings at the waist. The design was accepted by the masses and how! By the 1940’s, women’s magazine had further enhanced the trend by exposing degrees of midriff. Teen magazines of late 1940’s and 1950’s too weren’t far behind and happily participated in the movement by flaunting midriff barring suits and tops. Although it was restricted to swimwear initially, since the trend was so widely accepted, it was only natural for it to have an upgrade and move into women’s wear.This was only the beginning for the coy crop top. Crop tops further moved ahead to become “the look” of the 1980’s. The midriff-baring piece of clothing found a fan in Madonna, who wore it in a lot of her albums. She even made it a part of her signature look. It further garnered tons of exposure on silver screen and was part of many iconic films such as Dirty Dancing and Flash Dance. Crop tops conquered the pop culture and became a major part of it all throughout the 90’s. The low rise jeans paired with belly shirts became a classic duo especially in the sector of music and television. Britney Spears too was seen parading around in the same quite often. While they were initially worn during daily workouts with leggings, the crop top progressed to being worn with denim for a casual look.Style guide: Fortunately, styling a crop top isn’t all that demanding as it is quite a versatile piece and each one of us can find a variant to work around with.  Cropped fashion isn’t restricted to the 20 something’s or to the women with washboard abs.  The beauty of it is that it can blend into your business wardrobe as efficiently as it can belong to your vacation travel suitcase. If you aren’t comfortable with taking a leap forward by sporting a short crop, you could always work your way up by taking a shirt or top and giving it a DIY crop makeover by tying it! Full sleeved short tops paired with full skirts are another way of toning down the flash. You could also pair one with a high-waisted pant or knife pleated palazzo and add a blazer to rock that conference at 3 pm at the workplace. “Who’s not a fan of crop tops? It pairs well with high-waisted bottoms. Throw on a shrug to avoid showing off too much (if you want to tone down the look),” shares Sharma. Matching separates like a crop and a skirt with heels and a colour pop sling could have you looking like a million bucks – that too, without having to spend it. Doesn’t it look like it’s time for you to head down to the store and invest in some crop tops now? From functional to fashionableGiven fashion’s fixation on everything mini this year, it was only a matter of time that this completely charming backpack came back marching into our lives with drum rolls. If you are a 90’s kid, you probably remember owning at least one of these bags that was then imprinted with your favourite cartoon character and taking it for a day out at the annual picnic or at the local dance class sessions. What once proudly sat proudly on our study tables is back yet again only looking fresher than ever. The backpack (the bigger version) came into existence in the 1920’s solely as a functional carrier. It was only much later when designers realized that they could transform it from being just functional to being more fashionable and mint money!  The mini backpack gained massive popularity when it materialized on screen in Amy Heckerling’s Clueless in 1995 slung over the shoulder of the fictional Cher and there was no looking back after that. Alicia Silverstone donned one with her plaid miniskirts and knee socks and carried it so well that it became a must-have accessory for everybody.While it did not have a lot of variants back then, today you have a number of varieties to choose from. Ranging from leather goodies to satin to even denim, the mini backpack does not disappoint. This super fun and chic miniature not only can be worn as a backpack but also serves well as a handbag (all you have to do is hold it by its handle on the top!) so yes, you can enjoy the best of two worlds effortlessly. Style guide: Heading for a movie? Take along a mini backpack in a bright shade that stands out, whilst going super casual in denim and a V-neck. You could probably never imagine cocktails and mini backpacks in the same sentence but yes, you could invest in a fancier leather mini backpack handbag and take it for a night out with the girlfriends. It looks good and keeps your hands free to hold your drink easily. While satin backpacks could be taken while shopping, you could resort to the denim ones for game night at the arcade or while cheating on the diet at the pizza parlour. “Not only could you carry them with western outfits but you could even pair a bling-y mini with a sari to a kitty party!” points out Molo. There really is no stopping this fun-sized bag this season, we really advise you to go grab one of these and join the tribe! Also, you’re welcome!  Denim dramaMost of us are positively familiar with how denim came into existence; it worked its way up from being worn solely by labourers to being warmly accepted by the masses. High-waisted denim is a different thing altogether. It was invented in 1940 when brand Levis produced clothing keeping in mind the women working on land and in factories. The particular style allowed them to retain their modesty as they had to bend down to work. In the 60s, Marilyn Monroe donned one with a belt and shirt tucked right in and starred in the movie called The Misfits. You probably don’t need us telling you how well the look was accepted and followed. Most of us still wear it the Monroe way even today. Banavalikar-Kulkarni makes note, “In the 90s, high-waisted jeans were worn with crop tops and that’s come as-is as a trend now. You can just pull over an open shirt for daily wear.”The brand Guess made denim all the more popular with its campaigns starring Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell, Drew Barrymore, and the late Anna Nicole Smith. High-waisted denim is being offered in a lot of different washes and styles which is why most everybody succumbed to the trend. Full speed to 2018 and a quick peep to today’s fashion scenario and you would notice how so many people are embracing the high-waisted trend. Style guide: You really cannot go wrong with this piece of clothing. Not only does it make you look curvier, it also makes you look slimmer, curvy and tall. Easy to wear, and low-maintenance is what makes them a must-have. “Denims emphasize the curves so well; they look graceful,” informs Molo. Wearing a dark wash denim with a white V-neck and some hoops makes you look oh-so-sassy and effortless; throw in some tan handbag and nude blocks and you are ready to kill! Pair it off with a bling bralette and you’ve got your Saturday night OTTN ready! Try heading to the workplace in a pair with a satin floral shirt with these denims and be ready to nail the Friday dressing OOTD!  Majorly monochromeThis is a classic that has seen many versions through the years. Not only did this trend get plenty of space in the Chanel collection of yore but it was also a big time hit with its current design head, Karl Lagerfeld and featured regularly in his collections. The designer liked the winning blend so much that he wears the combination himself. The 60’s went gaga over anything and everything edgy. The black and white optical illusions were a hit. Women went on to adopt the black and white, simple yet stunning pieces and felt that it came equipped with power. Back then, polka dotted dresses paired with hats sold like hot cakes (and polka dots' trend is back again!). Down the eras, designers including Victoria Beckham, Carolina Herrerra were smitten by the monochrome bug too. The 90s saw this trend with a twist. It was not just about the black-and-whites, which themselves were in vogue, but monochrome also caught attention in its coloured version. Ensembles in varying tones of the same colour became a rage. And this trend in monochrome is back this season, with its own twist. “Monochrome in the 90s was more of bright colours, but these days, people have turned to pastels,” informs Banavalikar-Kulkarni.Style guide: “Styling monochrome is quite simple, a little tricky but mostly the end result is nothing short of remarkable,” shares Azmeen. Monochrome does require a thought before but looks really chic and classy once styled in the correct manner. Let’s brave the 2018 summer by keeping it simple in a white shirt and black jeggings and statement accessories like a bold neckpiece or earrings and some chunky bracelets. Black body con dresses worn with white capes make you look like nothing short of a fashion diva. Steer clear of prints and keep it simple as prints could break the look. Bright colours, along with trending pastels, work well for summers; why not wear a monochrome ensemble with a bright and pastel shade in the same colour like pink, blue or green?Text: Ravina SachdevImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock																		This season, up your shoe game by choosing the trendiest footwear in town. You need to make a solid first impression on a blind date. What do you do? a) You head to the mall with a clear idea of what your ensemble will be, with backups in case you don’t find what you’re looking for.b) You look through your closet, pick out clothes that will work, but shop for new accessories that will up the glam. c) You put together a look using your favourites from your closet. The idea of a date is to get to know the real you, right?  2. Which of these phrases best describes your wardrobe?a) Organised and filled with sensible separatesb) Timeless and covering a wide range of stylesc) Eclectic and full of colour 3. How do you usually shop for new clothes or accessories? a) You make a list of things you need and adhere to it strictlyb) You head out with an open mind and buy a few things that you really likec) You buy EVERYTHING you see on impulse! 4. How much time would you say you spend getting ready?a) You’re always the one that’s ready first. You don’t need much time if you know what you’re doing. b) It depends on the occasion. If you find someone wearing the same outfit as you, how do you react?a) You get annoyed and want to make sure that you’re pulling off the look better than them.b) You’re not a fan of the idea, so you spend the day avoiding being seen next to them.c) You’re #Twinning! This calls for a selfie! Mostly As  Type A Personality: Type As are ambitious and proactive. You love planning ahead and go over and above what is expected of you. The fact that you put so much time and effort into everything you do means that you’re fiercely competitive, and sometimes invite unnecessarily stressful situations. You’ve probably been called a control freak before, and you know the title is well deserved. You pride yourself in your ability to be organised, on time and efficient. Mostly Bs  Somewhere in between: You are all about adapting to circumstances. Falling on neutral ground between competitive and laidback, you are well-adjusted and change your approach based on what is called for. You are capable of being both a fearless leader and a willing team player. When you commit to something, you go all in, but you also know when it’s time to take a step back and detach yourself from a situation.  Mostly Cs  Type B Personality: You’re relaxed and believe in going with the flow. You are the kind of person to stop to smell the roses, and are known to enjoy the little things. People often mistake your laidback nature for inefficiency, but you know you can get things done without stressing yourself out. You’re not so much about the results as you are about the process, which is why you are good at tasks that require creativity and innovation. The final day of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 gave an indication of what’s going to impact your sartorial choices in spring and summer. Take a look. RufflesSpring catwalks around the world are cascading with ruffles and the Capital wasn’t an exception. While Rina Dhaka included the frilly detail in her saris, kurtas and dresses at the finale, Ashish N Soni juxtaposed them on clean and classic silhouettes to make his ready-to-wear line look young, fun and sensuous. Flash dance shoulderThis is an evolution of the off shoulder trend. Designer Sulakshana Monga adapted the peekaboo treatment for her clothes, flash dance or the ‘accidental’ shoulder show that reveals a little flesh without showing too much was a predominant trend. Monga used Half-on, half-off tops and dresses with single ruffled shoulders exposing only a slice of skin. If you wear this, keep the rest of the outfit simple and let your shoulder do the talking. Sheer fabricSheer fabrics such as chiffon, tulle, mesh, organza and chanderi have been summer staples for long and they made an impactful appearance on the runway at the Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018. From hemlines, tops with sheer insets, skirts and dresses at Monga’s to sheer in Indian wear--embellished sheer lehengas and blouses and saris at the Suneet Varma’s show--the trend was ubiquitous. Traditional embroideryIndian culture and craftsmanship were both profusely showcased on the ramp via traditional motifs and intricate embroideries. From thread embroidery at Pankaj and Nidhi, Krishna Mehta and Charu Parashar to intricate zardozi embroidery seen at Suneet Varma’s show, this ethnic element is here to stay though the silhouettes may vary from western contemporary to Indian. Day four of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 saw an abundance of clashing prints, all-white ensembles, dramatic hemlines and statement sleeves. Here’s a round up of the trends that is sure to get your attention: Shades of whiteMany shades of white were spotted on the runway. They offered a stark contrast to the multitude of prints and colours. From Madhu Jain, Kavita Bhartia to Abhi Singh and Ekta Jaipuria and Ruchira Kandhari paired white with white in their collections. If you’re not big on white-on-white, add a few loose fitted casual styles from Payal Jain, frilly and flirty skirts from Kavita Bhartia or a few traditional cotton kurtas from Madhu Jain to your wardrobe and mix and match it with other colours. Shirts under spaghetti strapsStylistas Kim Kardashian and Kendall and Kylie Jenner have been doing this for a while now and designers Dhruv Kapoor and Abhi Singh seemed to have got the drift. Models sashayed down the ramp wearing risqué spaghetti dresses and tank tops over shirts in different sizes and shapes. So ladies, it’s time to bring out your slinky dresses. Print on printThe runway saw an abundance of clashing patterns and prints, proving that this trend for the brave will be big in the upcoming season. While Shivan and Narresh had matching top and bottom sets with prints boasting of forest sights, Dhruv Kapoor matched ditsy florals with vintage prints. Exaggerated sleevesThis is one of the biggest trends for spring summer. And there are so many different types of statement sleeves to suit different types of arms. From billowy bell shaped, ultra long and oversized to ruffled, cinched at the wrist to exaggerated cuffs, there’s enough to last you more than one season. Asymmetrical hemlinesEverything isn’t straight and narrow for summers, designers played with geometry and courted the asymmetrical hemlines in myriad ways. Anju Modi brought the mullet back in fashion—her kurtas had hemlines that were short at the front and long in the back. Meanwhile, Kavita Bhartia, Dhruv Kapoor and Bhanuni by Jyoti experimented with the handkerchief hemline. As the growing popularity of cruise shows indicates, between Instagram-worthy beach escapes, destination weddings and glamping, resort fashion has indeed come a long way. Whether you’re reclining on sun loungers or cruising over gorgeous landscapes in a hot air balloon, there’s no excuse to look sloppy anymore, especially when you travel. While the island state of mind is just that—a state of mind—the allure of a glorious coverup, a feather-light kaftan or one of those hand-woven, basket totes is real, palpable and, suddenly, everywhere.  Spring/summer 2017 runways are proof that resortwear can go well beyond throw-on-and-go pieces. Take Miu Miu’s retro Italy-inspired collection, which comprise a line of ruched bikinis, patterned robe-style dresses and teensy twinsets, accompanied by embossed pool slides and appliqued swim caps. Miuccia Prada understands the value of a chic escape. “It’s a celebration of summer and its pleasures,” she mused during the post-show interview. Dolce & Gabbana also sought inspiration from the Italian tropics for its covered sundresses, bralets and miniskirts in fun prints (think pasta, seafood and gelato). The show venue even had a counter serving fresh tender coconut water and models strutted down the runway to the rhythms of the tarantella. Giorgio Armani presented a line of slouchy bloomers, sheer cover-ups and short suits, featuring painterly prints and tassels—just what we need for those soirées under the stars. The accessories followed suit; the flatforms at Prada and Chloé would make for stylish accoutrements on a holiday. For their spring/summer 2017 collection, Delhi-based designer duo Hemant and Nandita elevated holiday basics like swimsuits, shorts, crop tops and sarong-esque skirts using Victorian ruffles and vibrant print play. Nishka Lulla set out to reinvent the pantsuit, working with softer fabrics and delicate embellishments to transform it into a resort essential. Lulla says, “I used lightweight, everyday materials like cotton and tulle in relaxed comfy silhouettes, with frills and flounces thrown in for good measure.” Aparna Badlani, curator and co-owner of multi-designer boutique Atosa, Mumbai, has long recognised the potential of well-made resortwear. “At a point when destination weddings are such a huge phenomenon, the category is finally getting its due,” she says. If there’s one image that captures the exquisite charm of travel, it’s got to be that of actor and socialite Talitha Getty hanging out on the terrace of her Marrakech home, immortalised by photographer Patrick Lichfield in the late ’60s.  It even inspired Yves Saint Laurent to design a line of kaftans that he called Une Passion Marocaine. Designer and TV personality Nicole Richie, who has a perpetual vacation vibe about her, best embodies this spirit today. Her style reminiscent of LA’s boho-luxe aesthetic from the ’60s and the ’70s. Whether it’s through pictures of Taylor’s Swift’s glamorous squad chilling together on a yacht or Olivia Palermo and beau Johannes Huebl’s romantic romp in Greece, travel continues to fire our imagination and inform fashion in the most powerful ways.  Much like with eveningwear, building a bankable resortwear wardrobe takes work. “Start with the basics and build from there. Think kaftans, palazzos, shorts, day dresses and strappy sandals,” says Badlani. According to Lulla, the trick is to invest in lightweight, versatile separates that can be paired with other items from your wardrobe. “Take, for instance, bustiers that you can wear on the beach or with high-waisted bottoms for a night out,” she says. It’s always a good idea to mix luxe pieces with exotic finds from local boutiques and markets to create a look that is uniquely yours. As designers get nostalgic for the flamboyant ’80s, sequins go gangsta and shiny vinyl finds its way back into our closet. This season sparkle comes imbued with a street sensibility as the more-is-more mantra from our favourite decade clashes with athleisure’s fluid dynamism. Cue the season’s sharpest plissé skirts teamed with a pair of equally luxe sneakers. Designers drummed up a host of options that make an easy transition from the cubicle to the dance floor. We’re looking to Michael Kors’ slashed sequinned mini dresses and Phoebe Philo’s egg-shaped lurex pullovers at Céline for inspiration. “I like bare legs in winter; I like night for day. I like Alexa Chung mixing with Nan Kempner. It’s about the interesting mix,” said Kors in an interview post his show. At Kenzo, Humberto Leon and Carol Lim sent out a line of vinyl dresses and skirts, foil-print trousers and oversized metallic jackets. Isabel Marant flirted with vinyl too in retro styles, adding animal prints and plaid to the mix. “It really goes back to when I would sneak out, aged 15, to punk clubs like Le Palace and Les Bains Douches,” said the Parisian designer. Between Marc Jacobs’ subversive separates at NYFW and Rajesh Pratap Singh’s gilded army closer home, the message is loud and clear—street glamour is here to stay. Designer Sanchita Ajjampur’s futuristic mash of foil, mesh and paillettes, and Gaurav Jai Gupta’s street-style spin on metallic handlooms, further confirm the mood of the times. It’s evident that fashion is making no bones about its Ziggy Stardust-meets-Beyoncé philosophy, and the pop culture influencers are lapping it up. Historically, the first image that comes to mind in this category is that of  ’60s fashion icon and rocker Keith Richards’s then girlfriend Anita Pallenberg who took to the Cannes red carpet in a lurex jumper. Leave it to the Kardashian-Jenner clan to reinvent Pallenberg’s louche luxe uniform as they elevate street style basics like sweatshirts, lace-up boots and trackpants. Kendall Jenner even brought back the chainmail dress from the ’90s. Closer home Alia Bhatt is having a go with unexpected pairings like a camo shirt and a plissé skirt, offering us a fresh take on the trend.      Which brings us to the question of how to do it right. Archana Walavalkar, celebrity stylist and co-founder Stylecracker, says that styling is everything here. “It’s important to blend the look seamlessly, not letting the shiny piece acquire hero status at any point.” It’s a good idea to stock up on basics like hologram sweatshirts, sequinned numbered tees, slip dresses with a glamorous sheen, and metallic denims. If you’re shine-shy, begin with a statement accessory. Let the gleaming heels from Demna Gvasalia’s debut at Balenciaga or Fendi’s festive-edition gold totes give you some ideas. “Go casual with jeans and a tee teamed with embellished sandals. This is easier to pull off if you don’t quite dare to go all guns blazing,” says Ajjampur. Fine jewellery is also following suit by putting a casual spin to sparkle. Case in point: Nirav Modi’s Embrace range of diamond bangles, which stretch like a dream, offer a snug fit and are best worn with denims and a boyfriend shirt. The writing’s on the wall: Whatever your glittery vice may be, it’s time to wear it on your sleeve.   Wendell Rodricks is a man credited with many firsts. At a time when Indian fashion was all about opulence and grandeur, he introduced the idea of minimalism. He was one of the few Indian designers to bring eco-friendly textiles to the forefront and also pioneered resortwear in India. To commemorate his contributions to the fashion industry, Rodricks was awarded the Padma Shri title in 2014. While contemporaries are predictably passing on their legacies and labels to family members, the designer has entrusted it into the hands of young prodigy Schulen Fernandes. And he did it in his inimitable style, bang in the middle of the runway at his label's fall/winter showing at the 2016 Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW). In a fun, free-wheeling chat, Rodricks and Fernandes tell us about what's in store for the legendary label.Wendell, after holding the reins for 28 years, you've decided to hand them over to Schulen. Schulen, how did he break it to you and what was your reaction?Wendell Rodricks: I always wanted the label to go to somebody I trusted. Schulen came to me straight from college and she has been with me for four years. She had already started taking a lot of creative decisions for the label. For instance, last season we did the Indica Emporia presentation at LFW with vintage Indian garments. It was completely her vision and work from start to end. I wanted to slowly take the backseat with this label so that I could make time for my other passions. I felt the time was just right for her to take the label and fly with it.Schulen Fernandes: It obviously didn't happen out of the blue. The handover was always on the cards and it took two years of work laying the foundation. However, when the actual moment arrived, it was hard to believe. How are your roles divided in the new scheme of things?WR: I’d like to think of myself as a benevolent dictator (laughs). On a serious note, Schulen has complete freedom to realise her creative vision at the label now and I am happy to have her take over.SF: Wendell will obviously be the mentor. My work will now involve everything from conceptualising collections to actually bringing it to life. I am also excited about the business end of it and we have a competent team to help us on that front.Schulen, tell us a little bit about your debut collection, Trapezoid, for the Wendell Rodricks label presented at LFW. And, Wendell, what did you think of it?SF: I have always loved architecture and geometry. The trapezoid form has been used in architecture from ancient times and it is so versatile. We decided to explore it in fashion with this collection. We used a mix of structured shapes and fluid fabrics working with paper silks, chanderis and a lot of eco-friendly materials. WR: I was really surprised when Schulen came up with the idea. It is a form that I've seen in Inca and Aztec architecture and in our temple gopurams. The Indian woman's body which is narrow at the shoulders and wide at the hips also follows the trapezoid form. This was particularly relevant because for the first time we introduced a size chart specific to the Indian woman at LFW this season. I felt really proud watching the show. The biggest compliment to me and to Schulen was when people told us it (the collection) looked like Wendell Rodricks. When a new creative leader takes charge at a fashion house, change is afoot—what can we expect from the label?WR: I've always focussed on high-end fashion and have never been able to cater to the mid-range. I hope Schulen will be able to expand the reach of this label to more people the way my colleague Anita Dongre has done very successfully. I also want her to take risks with the label and be more experimental.SF: We will definitely retain the minimalistic language and eco-friendly DNA of the label as we move forward. I would like to introduce newer, younger silhouettes and experiment heavily with materials. What lies ahead for both of you? Wendell, do you miss being behind the wheel? Schulen, are you at all daunted?WR: I don’t miss being behind the wheel at all. I can finally dedicate time to things that I’ve been waiting to do. The work on the museum is underway (Rodricks is turning his Goa home into a space dedicated to Goan costumes). The dogs are taking it well but my three cats are giving me grief about the move! I would like to write a lot more. My next book Poskem is about Goa. I hope I’ll be able to turn it into a movie like Chetan Bhagat (laughs). I’d like to teach a lot more too.SF: I am excited about what lies ahead and loving every minute of my new job. A kurta is not only comfortable to wear but looks oh-so-chic, especially if there is a design element that adds to the look. The asymmetric style gives it an edgy look. If the neckline is low, then team it up with a chunky choker and mid-sized studs in the ear. If the neckline is high, leave the neck jewellery-less and wear chunky earrings. Add some bangles and finger rings and you're set.Makeup: Rosy glow makeup would look perfect with this. Round hoops at your ears and chunky bangles will complete the look.Makeup: To compliment this look we would suggest mauve accents as a preferred makeup looks. You can endorse a simple sari look, clubbed with natural makeup and light jewelry to mark the occasion. This Diwali fashion trend  will help you keep light and would make your celebration free of fuss. And whoever said, less is more, are obviously right. Try and find out! This Diwali, show off some printed perfection Printed Maxi dresses are everybody's top favorite outfit, no matter the occasion. Come Diwali, try and pick some printed maxi dresses that match the festive appeal and accentuate your fashion game . You can go for an ethnic range, which is available in most brands or prefers something simplistic. Take cues from your favorite celebs and up your festive style game in printed maxi dresses .Tips: Don't go overboard by mixing too many different prints. However, if you're mixing patterns, don't blend more than two types of prints in your look. Go ethnic, this Diwali, with the veritable vestsWhether you are a lover of all things simple or adore a jazzed-up look, an ethnic vest, popularly known as Koti, can be the perfect pick this Diwali season. Pair it with your Anarkali, long kurta or a simple top, your festive fashion appeal would be unmatchable in this spunky Diwali fashion trend . Team it up with right accessories, and voila!Tip: Pay extra attention to the right fit. Vest, if not of the perfect fit, can break your look. This Diwali has a sequined affairThere can never be enough of sequins love possible in this world. A little bit of glitter can add the oomph to your look, making you the dazzling diva of every party. Sequins have been in vogue for quite some time. This Diwali, try on a sequined range of outfits at the glittering festivities . From sequined saris to skirts and even kurta, there's nothing that can't handle the sequin shine with elan. What would be your pick?Tips:  You look can be made much better if you add some bold colors to compliment sequins. With sequined outfits, chunky or clunky jewellery or excess accessories should be avoided. Ethnic pants are in vogue this DiwaliGone are the days when bottom wears cam with a limited range of varieties. This Diwali put your fashionable foot forward in ethnic pants. From intricately embroidered range to brocade and zari patterns, ethnic pants are all the rage this season. Pair them up with your fave kurta or crop top, the choice is all yours.Tips: Right fit is the right tip for ethnic pants fashion . Make sure the length of your kurta doesn't kill the charm of your pants. Crop top and lehenga - the perfect trend to pick this DiwaliEndorsed by all your fave celebs, crop top and lehenga combination tops our list of traditional yet spunky Diwali wear . With the accentuated oomph of the crop top and desi touch of the lehenga , this look is a sure-shot heart winner. Go plain or glittery, or printed or embroidered, there are more than one ways to rock this Diwali fashion trend. What would you choose?Tips:  Keep heavy jewellery at bay, if trying this fashion trend. It's best if you choose a simpler neckline for your crop top if you plan to wear jewelry , especially the heavy ones. Bring in comfort and fashion in dhoti salwarsDhoti salwar is a perfect blend of comfort, style and chic statement. Pair them up with a bold tank top or traditional kurtas, their appeal is undeniable. Bring on the desi Diwali swag in brocade This Diwali, move over the usual desi prints and try something quintessentially traditional. Brocades have been the crown jewel of the Indian textile landscape. Go for a brocade print sari or try this Diwali fashion trend in skirts or salwar-kameez. Sari with jacket are all the rage, this DiwaliWhat can be a better way to sport a sari with a fun jacket, this Diwali! This fashion fad has been making waves for its boss-lady vibes. What to wear for Diwali Diwali is the time to celebrate with your family. It is also about celebrating our colorful traditions and vibrant culture. However, what you choose to wear should stem out from your idea of âÂÂâÂÂcomfort. If you're comfortable in salwar-kameer or sari or a pant-suit or shorts, you should totally rock it with all your confidence, and fashion and trends would follow! 2. Which dress code fits for the Diwali festival? Ideally, people generally prefer wearing traditional outfits like saris, lehengas and salwar-kameer. There are several other varieties of ethnic outfits from regional areas that can be totally your pick this Diwali. If you're celebrating the festival at home, you can go for something that gives you comfort and mobility as well as style. However, if you're spending this festive time outside the home, you can try new trends and styles like ethnic pants, dhoti salwar, among others. Our advice would be to blend comfort and fashion to have a great time. 3. Is it ok to wear a black color dress on Diwali? Several people in Indian people believe that black should not be picked up to wear on Diwali day. Independently, you can decide to wear the color that you want. But, the festive feeling is all about joy and celebration with your loved ones. It's best if you take advice from a family member to avoid hurting any sentiments on this auspicious day. Take a moment and reminisce about the days when we would send out anxious messages to our gang asking them about their outfits. What they were donning for the night? What if our outfits matched? The horror! These momentous precautions have a taken a back seat with changing times.  Matching outfits with your friend is no more a faux pas. Instead, it has become a raging and super fun trend that is here to stay! Twinning as a trend first emerged in South Korea’s K-pop culture. While coordinating your outfits completely is not an anomaly entirely, it can overpower the essence of your real personality and make you look, umm, a little too alike. But hey! We’ve got you covered. Have a look at these simple tips and tricks to ace the twinning game. Go ahead and make that winning statement with your fashion twin! One colour palette, multiple outfitsThis is a great way to flaunt the twin-win look without being too discernible. No worries even if you and bestie have different taste when it comes to styling your clothes. The main idea is to predominantly stay within the same colour palette and explore varied outfits. Think Gigi Hadid’s and Kendal Jenner’s iconic twin ensembles Match your fabricsHere’s an easy breezy example to help you get a better idea about this tip.  You can wear a chic eyelet white cotton dress with and your twin can throw on a white top having a similar eyelet detail. Dressing in tandem with your friend in this way leaves a lot of room for experimentation.  Top to bottom! Bottom to top!Interchanging the colours of your outfit with your BFF can be really fun. Fancy sporting a cute baby pink skirt with a pastel blue top? Your BFF, on the other hand, can rock a baby pink top with a pastel blue skirt. Think out of the boxWhat’s the first thing that comes to your mind when you think about twinning? Matching your garbs, right? While this is the most popular choice, there are some other subtle ways in which you can strut your way into the twin parade. How about getting matching phone covers? You are your fashion twin will be carrying around your phone pretty much everywhere. Bring out those accessories There are a myriad of ways in which you can elevate your twinning game without synchronizing your outfits from head to toe. Add a pair of matching oxidized tribal jhumkas to your ensemble for that subtle yet classy twinning look.  So there you have it! Your very own handy guide which will aid you in conquering this super-fun trend. Lastly, we would just want to remind you that twinning is not about replicating each other’s clothes. Don’t strive to look identical! It is one thing to twin your outfit with a person and another to look like their clone. Maintaining your identity is of crucial importance. Reflect on of your personal sense of style. Ensure that your individual personality shines through your matching outfit. A lot is shouldered by the details therein. The aim is not to look like identical twins. You want to alike but different. You can wear the same shirt but pair it up with different bottoms. Wear dresses with a similar length but different prints. Yes, twinning can be that effortless. She had a Cinderella moment, where the ‘fairy godfather’ flicked his wand, and the black and blue gown by Tommy Hilfiger lit up in blue! This was made possible with technology; the structure inside the dress was made up of metallic plates, LED lights, batteries and wire. At the same event, musician Janelle Monáe wore an exaggerated Christian Siriano balloon-hipped dress that had a motorised blinking eye on one breast! This too was an amalgamation of fashion and technology at its chicest! Katy Perry was one of the foremost though and had worn a LED dress at the Met Gala and during her tour in 2014. It’s not just the celebs that get to wear such high-tech ensembles, even daily wear is getting its fair share of technological advancement. Wrist-worn smart watches or bands have become common in recent years. But, according to a research carried out by UK-based Juniper Research, the trend is shifting to ‘connected clothing’, which is forecasted by them to become $1 billion industry in 2020! Here are some of such cool garments that you can choose from.Jacket phone: What if you could pick up calls, control music volume, and get directions by just taping or brushing the sleeves? Levi and Google have collaborated for a jacket that does just that! Digital yogi: If you’re learning yoga, and want to refine your poses and get them right, these yoga pants are just for you! Brand Nadi X has come up with the pants that sense when your yoga pose needs refining and uses haptic feedback to create small vibrations on the body part you need to adjust.Swimming in sun: We’re always worried about just how much sunscreen to apply when on the beach, wearing swimwear. Brand Neviano has come up with stylish swimsuits that have a water-proof a UV sensor that detects if the UV rays are high and if you need more sunscreen to be applied! Research is also being done on how else to incorporate technology into fashion in order to make our life easier. At Deakin University’s Institute for Frontier Materials, they’re looking into developing fibres that can store energy. They’re hoping to make garments that can be used to charge phones and other small devices. Imagine slipping your discharged phone into your pocket, and it comes out charged! Well, with more and more of our lives getting touched by technology, is this tech-forward fashion really a surprise?
