Feminine is in!Go on, give it a go!					Winter is finally over, and we’re happy about the sunny days to be here again. You’ll be shedding those heavy jackets and coats and finally be able to show off the latest trends in fashion as you step out. Here’s looking at the trends this season that will have you turn heads. While the previous year was all sorts of the frivolous extravaganza, this year is more about practical functionality with a generous dollop of extra. Animal printsAnimal prints started making the rounds of runways sometime early last year and in filtered into our closets in full force by the end of the year. The predatory prints from the ’80s had made a massive comeback but with the much-needed makeover! The well-known prints are so much chic and oh so covetable now. What was once considered a bold statement for the wild-hearted is now being sported at ease by the shy too. Cheetah, leopard, snake, zebra, you name it and the print is available at your go-to an e-commerce site. Styling an animal print is a little tricky as you do not want to look like you belong to the circus! Steer clear of heavy fabrics like wools and velvets and opt for smooth and silky outfits such as silks and cotton. Start with a skinny leopard printed bodysuit and boyfriend jeans with boots and work your way up to a snakeskin evening gown with strappy black heels and minimalistic jewellery and you’re all set.  Utility dressingRemember days you were looked down upon for leaving your house in oversized sweats and cargo pants? Well, it turns out that you can proudly flaunt your baggy cargo pants and sneaks this year, all thanks to the utility dressing rage! Welcome to 2019 where function meets fashion in the form of unpolished practicality. It is nothing but practical, laid back and super comfortable clothing. 2019 has functionality written all over it. Imagine practical oversized clothing in muted tones. Combat trousers, chic overalls, trench coats, baggy sweats, sneakers are taking the fashion world with a storm and we aren’t complaining one bit. The key to nailing the perfect utility look is to style the pieces. If you haven’t experimented yet, start with styling functional clothing with tailored pieces. Start with layering an army jacket over a solid black jumpsuit or playsuit with black boots and move ahead. Also, you can jazz up your khaki trench coat with a red lip and a silk scarf for the perfect date look or can sport those ‘ugly’ trainers with a sleep skirt suit at work and be practical, comfortable and oh so chic at the same time. Win-win!  Cycling shortsCycling shorts are nothing new; in fact, Princess Diana regularly sported them with crew necks long ago. Fast forward to 2019, and they are easily the biggest trend of the year. They were unmissable on the runaways and have been marking territory in online and offline stores in abundance. And not, not just in the regular black spandex garment we’ve grown up with but jazzed up in pretty colours and prints and embroidery. It goes without saying that the humble piece of sportswear has graduated the fashion ladder by heaps and how. The garment that was once worn for physical activities is now being sported under blazers to the boardroom. And oh, it is Kim Kardashian approved too! Women all across the globe have taken a fancy for these bodycon shorts and are pairing it off with anything and everything. From boardrooms to date nights to soirees, these shorts are hard to miss. You too could dip your toes in the water by the pairing of a solid coloured one with a loose oversized tee for your regular coffee runs and upgrade by sporting metallic ones underneath blingy long blazers. It isn’t clear on if the trend is here to stay or not, but that doesn’t stop it from being everywhere at the moment! Oversized2019 revolves around the word oversized! From oversized unstructured jackets and t-shirts to oversized huge sunnies and hats, there’s no stopping really! (Yep, that means we would have to put away our skinny sunglasses from last season!) While last season was more sleek and minimal in terms of accessories, this season is all about exaggeration in terms of hats, belts, bags, etc. The tote bag has gotten a makeover and has blown out really big! Loud hair bands- studded, leather, satin etc too seem to have maximized. Sunglasses are big and bold with added adornments. Chunky jewellery in a more natural form rather than being polished would be a hit this year. Belts too are broad and oversized. 80’s fashionThe thumb rule of fashion is that each trend resurfaces after a few years. There are some that we can’t stand and some we welcome with open arms, like the 80’s fashion. The retro fashion has gotten a redo and we can’t wait to see it on the streets. Imagine belted high waist denim and power suits in neon (remember Priyanka Chopra?) and fringed mullets and big hair. Puffy sleeves, ruffles and shoulder pads are more fashionable than you thought. Although the style is more refined and structured than what it was before. Shoulder pads blazers mean business and are definitely not going anywhere for a long time. Ruffles trims tops and dress continue selling like hot cakes. Statement sleeves too are in the running. Expect to see a lot more of the 80’s fashion this year! Text by Ravina SachdevImages by Yogen Shah Some of the colour trends of the year, ruling the ramps and streets alike, are fiesta (red-orange), jester red, turmeric, living coral, pink peacock, pepper stem (yellow-green) and Aspen gold. While hues like Aspen gold and pink peacock became celebs’ favourite in no time, others too are making their way in style. Gone are the days when eyeglasses were considered unfashionable and boring. Today, there’s no smarter accessory to add to your look. They give a polished appearance that’s both sexy and strong. In fact, the trend is winning so many hearts that not only are they being donned with prescription lenses but also as no-power lenses, purely to make a fashion statement. All for the artsy effect! As we know, 2019 is about going bold and individualistic in your fashion choices. So, go for a fat frame, pick a sleek one in an oversized variant, or take the classic way. Catch on this spectacle rage with these celeb-inspired looks:OVERSIZED glasses clearly lead the list It’s never too modern for the RETRO-ROUND frames Ooomph up with an AVIATOR Sassy and sleek SEMI-RIMLESS framesBack to the BASICS 													Minimalist and sassy, the most appealing jewellery trend of the year spells all things quaint. While statement necklaces and chunky earrings are very much in play, they are limited to adorning occasional events. For an everyday appearance, more and more people are looking for accessories that are glamorous but subtle, and enhances the outfit instead of overpowering it. There’s more to it... The season is witnessing a thrust of natural and wild energy, and animal motifs are being donned everywhere from drop earrings to dainty rings. “Animal motifs like butterfly, peacock, fish etc. have always been an evergreen trend. They depict the beauty of nature and the vibrant shades of one’s personality. The beautiful colours of a butterfly, for instance, depicts particularly well in drop earrings and pendants. If you are buying fashion jewellery, match it right with your outfit to get an effortless quirky look with animal motifs.” Tells Pradnya Mhaske, the Head of Jewellery Design and Merchandising at CaratLane. While statement necklaces and chunky earrings are very much in play, they are limited to adorning occasional events. For an everyday appearance, more and more people are looking for accessories that are glamorous but subtle, and enhances the outfit instead of overpowering it. There’s more to it... The season is witnessing a thrust of natural and wild energy, and animal motifs are being donned everywhere from drop earrings to dainty rings. “Animal motifs like butterfly, peacock, fish etc. have always been an evergreen trend. They depict the beauty of nature and the vibrant shades of one’s personality. The beautiful colours of a butterfly, for instance, depicts particularly well in drop earrings and pendants. If you are buying fashion jewellery, match it right with your outfit to get an effortless quirky look with animal motifs.” Tells Pradnya Mhaske, the Head of Jewellery Design and Merchandising at CaratLane. Bipasha Basu Singh GroverIn Falguni Mehta.					 It’s time for all of us to make a resolution to not fall prey to body figure stereotyping and make it all about self-love. Not trying to hide behind frumpy clothes that do you no justice is one way to do that. Finding out and understanding your body type is something to be thankful for, however making it a stereotype is not. So all the apple body-shaped woman, pear body-shaped and also the full-sized hourglass body-shaped ladies, stop being used to the embarrassing yourself, rather start embracing yourself! With numerous brands breaking the beauty taboo with real-body campaigns and policies we celebrate every woman with perfection. If you are curvy, it is important to dress according to your size. Say goodbye to every oversized clothes and slide into the outfits with the right fit that will hide your problem areas and highlight the right angles of your frame. Styling from top to bottom can bring a vast change in your look. Have a look at some great style tips for real girls who felt too voluptuous to wear certain items, and we're here to blow those myths right out of the water. LINES AND SHAPES You need your first impression to be fab-worthy, and it is all about your lines and shapes that draw the eye. One great trick is to wear monochrome ensembles. This makes the viewer’s eye move up to down, or vice versa, forming one uninterrupted line, which makes you look tall and slim. If you’re looking to enhance those curves, then opt for a bodycon dress in the right fabric like jersey. You can also wear ensembles that have lines narrowing at the waist and spreading away at the bust and the hips. The lines can be in the form of a print, stitches, pleats, etc. A dress with a plunging V-neck and a cinched waist which then flairs out below, also gives the illusion of an hourglass figure.  THE RULE OF THE HEM Knowing where hems or borders should be on your body can help you lengthen the frame. A knee-length skirt, for example, should sit just right under the knee, never around the biggest part of the calf.  The hem of the jeans should be at the ankle, or (even better) an inch or two below. If you are not of average height, buy your clothes, specifically the bottoms from a retailer that gives you perfect length options. Well, hems can be tricky sometimes but the best thing is to not to have a clue about it and find a tailor with a good eye, trust them and learn as you go.  SAY 'NO' TO OVERSIZED CLOTHES Just beanpoles look great in larger than the average dress size! Don’t add volume to your body by wearing oversized dresses. Instead, pick the clothes that are body-skimming (not too tight) and show your curvy side. Say no to a giant t-shirt, but a maxi or kaftans that skim the curves and have some belt at the waist is cool. If you want an easy profile, or if you got your favourite graphic on a tee or tunic then pair it with tighter trousers or jeans and make it to your advantage. MIND THE SHOES It’s always a head-to-toe thing and what you put on your feet that matters. Pointy tips and low heels can make you look slim, whether you are pairing it with a skirt or a pair of pants. Try to find a shoe with a vamp the ends at the top of your toes, other than halfway around. Shoe styles with low vamps include ballet flats and pumps. High-vamp shoes include Mary Janes and loafers. WHAT NOW, ACCESSORIES? Long chains, not chokers are good to go, especially if you got classic apple shape and short neck. Your focus should be on creating long, unbroken lines along your body. No mood of jewellery? Grab a long scarf helps for the same effect. Layering your jewellery is another way of drawing the eye vertically. From choker to long chains, layer with a couple of them together. Even when wearing bangles and bracelets, stack them up.  VOTE FOR LAYERS Contrary to stereotypes, layering doesn’t necessarily add volume. Instead, it sometimes gives your body a definition. Wearing a tank top with a pretty cardigan instead of one-piece dress or T-shirt can help to underline your shape.  Ensure though that you don’t layer with bulky garments.  EMBRACE YOUR HIGH WAIST High-waisted pants are your companion. They help tuck in folds and fat and minimize muffin tops since they end at the slimmest part of the waist. Ensure they're long, finishing at the lower leg or underneath, following the rule of the hemline.  Dress to make yourself feel good, and you will make heads turn!  Text: Akruti Khandkar 													You might have had a love-hate relationship with chokers, but they became fashionable 500 years ago and are still raging among fashion enthusiasts in their evolved forms. Below are few glimpses of the fashion week to upgrade your MO: GucciAfter all-black everything, it’s head-to-toe red that will be talked about.  VersaceHave a quilted leather jacket in your wardrobe? Team it with a neutral turtleneck underneath to appear ramp-ready. Also, animal print is everywhere, unveil your wild side with it. United Colors of BenettonTake cues from UCB on how to rock the rainbow trend.					PastelsA perfect choice for an OOTD, these sweet-looking hues can be paired with almost anything in your wardrobe. From Minnie Mouse in 1928 to Dior’s best-selling New Look piece in 1954, polka dot print has taken everyone aback with its feminine and romantic appeal. Its fan base ranges from Hollywood actor Emma Stone to Bollywood beauties Sonam Kapoor Ahuja and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Be it on clothes or accessories, this print ups any look to its epitome. Swara BhaskerIn a Mango dress.					 Winters see you bring out those old boots and show them the light of the day. Only issue: You’ve worn them a number of times last season and they just don’t feel that special anymore. How you wish your boots had some colour or a fringe or even a shiny buckle. Sigh! Fret not. With some easy fix tricks, you can upgrade your boots to the latest fashion trends of this season and always stay in style! Buckle up!What you need: Belts, scissors, hot glue.How to make: Cut your belt measured according to the roundness of your boot at the calf. Use hot glue to attach your belt onto your boot. Hold it in place and let it dry. Cut off any unwanted extra belt length and buckle it around your boot. Add extra notches if required. You can repeat the same procedure using more belts with different colours or textures and you have your very own cowgirl boots! Cool cutsWhat you need: Ruler, penknife, chalk.How to make: Draw or trace the design of your choice onto your boot using chalk. Size your grid according to your liking. Use the pen knife to cut out the parts you wish to keep hollow. Once done, wipe off the chalk marks with a damp cloth and you cut out boots are ready. This DIY is easier to work with semi-thick leather that won’t lose shape or tear after cutting. Dazzling tipsWhat you need: Paintbrush, gold/silver pearl shine paint, a thick masking tape, fixative sprayHow to make: Add masking tape a few centimetres away from the tip of the boot. Press firmly. Paint using the gold or silver paint making sure the paint doesn’t go under the tape. Paint smooth and even coats to get a smooth surface. Allow it to dry for a couple of hours and remove the tape. Wipe off any stray dried up paint. Spray on the fixative spray and let it dry for 24 hours. And voila! Lace all dayWhat you need: Lace, pins (if required) and fabric glue.How to make: Cut strips of lace that is long enough to go around your boot. Arrange your pattern and pin it so it holds your desired shape. Using tiny amounts of glue, attach it to your boot. Let it dry completely. You can even add a few beaded chains and feathers for a complete boho look. Retro kicksWhat you need: Masking tape, matte finish paint, brush, scissors.How to make: Cut pieces of the masking tape and stick them onto your boot in any desired shape. You can make a star shape or go abstract and stick the tape onto your boot in any way you like. Once this is done, paint over the design you've created using any matte finish paint of your choice. Let it dry and peel the tape off slowly to reveal your design. Continue making more designs or simply stick the tape in equidistant parallel lines to create stripes for a sporty look.Text: Yvonne Jacob 													From Minnie Mouse in 1928 to Dior’s best-selling New Look piece in 1954, polka dot print has taken everyone aback with its feminine and romantic appeal. After changing three flights and taking a three-hour bus ride, we landed in Montepuez—the second largest city in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique. The day had been a whirlwind, as we hopped on and off different vehicles. The moment we landed in Mozambique, however, a burst of fresh, clean air welcomed us. The quaint city is home to Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM), which is a Mozambican company developing operations at the ruby deposits in the city, and covers approximately 33,600 hectares. A leading supplier of responsibly-sourced coloured gemstones across the globe, MRM is owned by UK-based natural resource company Gemfields (75 per cent), and Mozambican company Mwiriti (25 per cent). We spent two days in the heart of the most recently discovered ruby deposit in the world, and unearthed more than just these precious crimson stones. 													The journey beginsOver 500 million years in the making, ruby, or ratnaraj (meaning king of the gemstones in ancient Sanskrit), is an extremely rare stone, cherished by royalty, social A-listers, and collectors alike. We went to see one of the mine pits on the first day, where rubies are deposited as alluvial or colluvial material over a weathered bedrock.Rubies were first discovered in Montepuez in 2009, following which, Gemfields and Mwiriti signed an agreement in 2011 to officiate the mining process. MRM uses a multidisciplinary approach for mining—geological (rubies that are typically associated with certain rocks or minerals), geophysical (airborne survey—magnetic and radiometric), and geochemical (determining chemical signatures of hidden mineral deposits). The sheer size of the mine pit was staggering, and it brought forth the concern of what happens to it once it has been exhausted.Mining with a conscienceMRM is committed to mining in a way that has the least environmental impact. Jack Cunningham, Sustainability, Policy and Risk Director at Gemfields, explains, “Before we mine an area, we collect seeds of the indigenous plants and trees from the top soil and create a seed bank. We then grow the seeds in a nursery for replanting as we complete mining.” Along with encouraging biodiversity, old pits are back-filled and rehabilitated, and no harmful chemicals are used during the mining process. “Machine oil is carefully managed and stored, machines and vehicles are maintained by our in-house teams, and all spills are cleaned up and the contaminated soil is bioremediated,” says Cunningham.The road to development was not an easy one, and initially, the company faced resistance from the inhabitants. Cunningham recalls, “There was uncertainty from the local community about what the benefits would be and how quickly they would receive those. An influx of thousands of illegal miners also caused social problems at a time when we weren’t yet in a position to help the community. Since 2014, however, we have had a dedicated team on the ground that carries out community engagement, and addresses their needs and grievances, and the relationship with them has vastly improved.” MRM has provided employment to 1,110 people, both directly and via contractors, 95 per cent of whom are Mozambican nationals. The mining company has also helped nine farming associations (two of which are dedicated to empowering women and in total represent 290 partner farmers), and taught them new techniques that have increased yields. Looking at the community as a whole, the company has invested in infrastructure for four primary schools (three of which are new), providing education to 1,000 primary school-aged children. “Schooling is the responsibility of the state, however our infrastructure atleast helps the government with a costly aspect of public education. Once established, we hand over the schools to the government for their onward management as a national asset,” elucidates Cunningham. The establishment of two mobile health clinics serves thousands of people across six villages. Isac Rafael, Director of the Namanhumbir Health Center, Mozambique, stated, “With these mobile clinics, it’s possible to care for patients in the most remote areas without sanitary units. This also gives easy access to pregnant women, children, and the elderly, who don’t have to travel long distances.”The final stepWe spent the last leg of our journey in the wash plant and sorting house, where the raw stones are processed and graded according to their colour, size, and clarity. We witnessed how a team of highly skilled sorters picked rubies from the rubble, in a secure environment. Their hands worked like machines as they separated the precious stones in silent harmony. The final pieces are then auctioned off by Gemfields and till June 2017, a total of eight ruby auctions have generated a revenue of US$280 million.We entered the city with a bunch of preconceived notions, and after spending two days in the shoes of a miner, left with hope for the Montepuez community. That’s what you get in this city of Mozambique, along with beautiful never-ending blue skies, and a warm community that believes in co-existence.					After changing three flights and taking a three-hour bus ride, we landed in Montepuez—the second largest city in the province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique. The day had been a whirlwind, as we hopped on and off different vehicles. The moment we landed in Mozambique, however, a burst of fresh, clean air welcomed us. The quaint city is home to Montepuez Ruby Mining (MRM), which is a Mozambican company developing operations at the ruby deposits in the city, and covers approximately 33,600 hectares. A leading supplier of responsibly-sourced coloured gemstones across the globe, MRM is owned by UK-based natural resource company Gemfields (75 per cent), and Mozambican company Mwiriti (25 per cent). We spent two days in the heart of the most recently discovered ruby deposit in the world, and unearthed more than just these precious crimson stones. 													The journey beginsOver 500 million years in the making, ruby, or ratnaraj (meaning king of the gemstones in ancient Sanskrit), is an extremely rare stone, cherished by royalty, social A-listers, and collectors alike. We went to see one of the mine pits on the first day, where rubies are deposited as alluvial or colluvial material over a weathered bedrock.Rubies were first discovered in Montepuez in 2009, following which, Gemfields and Mwiriti signed an agreement in 2011 to officiate the mining process. MRM uses a multidisciplinary approach for mining—geological (rubies that are typically associated with certain rocks or minerals), geophysical (airborne survey—magnetic and radiometric), and geochemical (determining chemical signatures of hidden mineral deposits). The sheer size of the mine pit was staggering, and it brought forth the concern of what happens to it once it has been exhausted.Mining with a conscienceMRM is committed to mining in a way that has the least environmental impact. Jack Cunningham, Sustainability, Policy and Risk Director at Gemfields, explains, “Before we mine an area, we collect seeds of the indigenous plants and trees from the top soil and create a seed bank. We then grow the seeds in a nursery for replanting as we complete mining.” Along with encouraging biodiversity, old pits are back-filled and rehabilitated, and no harmful chemicals are used during the mining process. “Machine oil is carefully managed and stored, machines and vehicles are maintained by our in-house teams, and all spills are cleaned up and the contaminated soil is bioremediated,” says Cunningham.The road to development was not an easy one, and initially, the company faced resistance from the inhabitants. Cunningham recalls, “There was uncertainty from the local community about what the benefits would be and how quickly they would receive those. An influx of thousands of illegal miners also caused social problems at a time when we weren’t yet in a position to help the community. Since 2014, however, we have had a dedicated team on the ground that carries out community engagement, and addresses their needs and grievances, and the relationship with them has vastly improved.” MRM has provided employment to 1,110 people, both directly and via contractors, 95 per cent of whom are Mozambican nationals. The mining company has also helped nine farming associations (two of which are dedicated to empowering women and in total represent 290 partner farmers), and taught them new techniques that have increased yields. Looking at the community as a whole, the company has invested in infrastructure for four primary schools (three of which are new), providing education to 1,000 primary school-aged children. “Schooling is the responsibility of the state, however our infrastructure atleast helps the government with a costly aspect of public education. Once established, we hand over the schools to the government for their onward management as a national asset,” elucidates Cunningham. The establishment of two mobile health clinics serves thousands of people across six villages. Isac Rafael, Director of the Namanhumbir Health Center, Mozambique, stated, “With these mobile clinics, it’s possible to care for patients in the most remote areas without sanitary units. This also gives easy access to pregnant women, children, and the elderly, who don’t have to travel long distances.”The final stepWe spent the last leg of our journey in the wash plant and sorting house, where the raw stones are processed and graded according to their colour, size, and clarity. We witnessed how a team of highly skilled sorters picked rubies from the rubble, in a secure environment. Their hands worked like machines as they separated the precious stones in silent harmony. The final pieces are then auctioned off by Gemfields and till June 2017, a total of eight ruby auctions have generated a revenue of US$280 million.We entered the city with a bunch of preconceived notions, and after spending two days in the shoes of a miner, left with hope for the Montepuez community. That’s what you get in this city of Mozambique, along with beautiful never-ending blue skies, and a warm community that believes in co-existence. Diwali is a time for gifting - and buying something for ourself and our home. What to buy? Femina puts together its favourite picks in fashion, beauty, accessories, décor and more.					FASHIONHigh glossNothing screams power more than high shine fabrics worn appropriately. While last season was all about plastics in apparel, this season is all about high gloss on any and every fabric texture such as leather, satin etc. Right from long wrap-around coats to pants to even see-through dresses, high shine is marking its territory everywhere. But beware if worn out of proportion or styled incorrectly, the trend sure can fall back easily. The best way to start would be with a high shine statement belt on a solid outfit and move upwards to high gloss trimmings on outfits and then take the plunge! “I feel high gloss fabrics can somehow add sheer sexiness to the look. I personally love wearing statement gloss t-shirt dresses and black or nude shoes,” says lifestyle blogger Naina Ahluwalia. Plaid and simpleThe key to play with plaid is to not go overboard with it and style it with colourful bright accessories to brighten up the look. “If you ask me about plaid, I can only and only think of the term classic yet trendy. Plaid can be played around with prints and colours but it's not a trend, I would call it an evergreen print that everyone needs to have in their closet. Of course, every year something or the other trendy using plaid comes up and those make good additions to the closet,” shares lifestyle blogger Aleena Macker. You can try your hand at plaid button-down skirts or bright plaid co-ordinates or even plaid mules, there’s no stopping this season. Add a dollop of feminine to plaid through glam jewellery, bold lips or bling bags and watch your style quotient go through the roof!Fringe benefits The best part about the fringe trend is its versatility. Not only can you incorporate these sassy strings into your wardrobe but you can also sport it through any medium i.e. through an accessory or clothing piece or even footwear. “You have a variety of different options when it comes to fringes. You can play around with beads or metallic ropes or even denim, the list just goes on and on,” says fashion blogger Puja Wani, “A well-fitted tee with fringes on denim looks really chic for the day and pair a contemporary sari with a fringed noodle strap crop makes heads turn at a social soirée!” ACCESSORIESSkinny sunglassesWe are totally crushing big time on skinny sunglasses to go along with our skinny tall soy lattes. Trust us when we say that a pair of these can totally escalate your look within seconds. What started with a few sightings on Instagram influencers has only gone up on the fashion ladder with everybody adapting to the style. One thing is for sure, the 90’s skinny game is here to stay for a while and you could try experimenting with the same. While the black skinnies sure do seem like a classic, there are a lot of varieties to choose from. You could go crazy and pick a pair of colour tinted glasses to go with super ripped black denim and a black crop or could try white rimmed statement sunglasses over an all-white outfit for the local Sunday brunch!Bag that styleThe trend started with designer labels such as Gucci and Prada displaying embellished bags on runways and it has only been widely appreciated and accepted by the masses. Imagine bags with tiny fur trims and pearls and fabric patches with logos or numbers. The size of these goodies ranges from tiny shoulder bags to handbags to even totes! A great bag can make or break the look and these embellished bags undeniably enliven the look in a jiffy. Macker says, “For bags or any kind of accessories including shoes, I absolutely love embellishments. It gives so much more character to pieces and if you can customize the embellishments there is just nothing like having your own unique piece. I have to say the Gucci has set the bar high with their embellished bags.” Try carrying a denim shoulder bag with faux pearls and diamonds on a classic white blouse and blue denim to the lazy Saturday lunch with the girls or a box bag with adornments for the cocktail soiree the week after and be indebted to us forever!Dance in trans(parent)!While we were throwing our everyday essentials in a plastic see-through bags last season, this season is all about transparent footwear (now we can openly flaunt our pedicures!). Clear PVC sandals are selling like hot cakes and by the looks of it, this trend is definitely here to stay. With Chanel kicking off the trend early this year and going crazy with plastic covered everything, most designers followed suit. If you think wearing see-through shoes is bizarre, you could participate by wearing a combination of plastic, leather peep toes or sandals with plastic straps, or footwear with plastic heels. You could most certainly wear PVC boots on a bodycon lacy dress if you’re ready to bear it all! Fashion blogger Madhavi Dey says, “PVC shoes are a major life saver. I love wearing these statement pieces see through ankle boots on an all-black ensemble as it just adds the right touch of edge to the outfit.” BEAUTYGive a clean(se) chitWe have finally come to the realization that cleansing oils aren’t the bad heroes we made them out to be. In fact, they are seen to be the most liked product currently. Cleansing is the most effective way of getting dirt free, crystal clear and soft skin in a jiffy and cleansing oils seem to deliver all that and much more efficiently. Experts confirm that while cleansers do strip your skin of natural oils, cleansing oil does not clog your pore. Beauty blogger Stacey Castenha says, “I’ve started using a cleansing oil and it only does wonders to my skin. Not only does it cleans my face really nice but also leaves it glowing and super soft. This is one product that is never exiting my vanity.” Looks like it’s time to put this oil down on the list of things to buy this season!Enhancing beautyThe trend that started sometime early this year has only grown. Face serums are a game changer and people are only starting to realize. Whether your skin is acne-prone or dehydrated or dull, there is a magic potion available for every skin type and for every skin related problem. Majority of us Indian women suffer from dehydrated skin and the answer to that is moisture-based hydration face serum. “People always thought that face serums are a strict no as they make the skin too oily or clog the pores but 2018 has been a game changer. People are understanding their skin like never before and adding these serums to their daily beauty regime,” informs Catenha. Time for a much-needed skincare shopping run! Inclusive beautyA little while back, Rihanna upped her game big time after releasing her foundation line with FENTY Beauty. The foundation that came in a variety of 40 different shades (yes, 40 different shades and we aren’t even joking about it!) made our lives so much simpler. People all over the world went crazy as they no longer had to mix a few different shades in order to create the one suitable for their skin. This started a movement that every skin tone is unique and deserves to be celebrated. It was only logical that soon other beauty brands followed suit and started going beyond the customary 10-15 shade range. “Today, it’s all about customization. Right from outfit to beauty to even food, everybody wants something exclusive designed just for them. The inclusive beauty trend is definitely here to stay and is only going to get bigger and bigger with each season,” says Wani. DÉCORGeometric accentsAs Pantone predicted geometric accents have certainly proved to be the hottest trend of the year in decor. What started as modest triangles and circles on tiny vases and tableware here and there has only blown up and manifested itself on objects everywhere. The octagons and hexagons are repeatedly making bold appearances on items such as home furnishing, tiles, wallpapers, fabrics, etc. among others. Interior decorator Heena Sabhnani shares, “A lot of my clients have been taken aback with what the change they saw in their home by incorporating geometric patterns. It instantly brightens up a dull and boring home and adds just the right touch of modern.” Geometric prints are an easy way to up your décor game and give your home the much needed modern touch that it so needed. You too can join on the bandwagon by getting a bright and colourful wallpaper on the bar wall or you can start by dipping one toe at a time and get geometric wall hangings by the dinning or a subtle rug to start with. Frills and trimsWe are as surprised as you are; as for most of us, fringe belongs in the closet. Well, clearly not anymore as the trend has gotten a major upgrade. This season, the style is moving out of our wardrobes and on our décor and we aren’t complaining one bit. Fringe doesn’t necessarily have to mean overdressed. Lightly fringed hems on lamps or a statement fringe trimmed chandelier add the right touch of flirty modern chic. Everything boring is fun again! Fringes are seen making indiscreet roaring appearances on sofa chairs, statement mirrors wall hangings and other zillion things. Again, you could opt for a fringed sofa set for a modern Gatsby look or start with a tiny fringe trim lamp on the nightstand and thank us later!Lush livingVelvet for the longest time has been synonymous to luxury and opulence and the quickest and easiest way to transform your house and give it a luxurious touch is by upgrading your plain Jane furniture with plush velvet pieces. Earlier, velvet was a fabric that was easy to stain, required a lot of looking after, was really difficult to maintain and was available in limited colours. However, all that has changed and today you can get a variety of different shades and options and you’d be surprised at how low maintenance the fabric is and it really doesn’t require much looking after it. You could start experimenting by getting a plush turquoise throw on or cushions and notice the change or go all out and invest in larger pieces like a purple velvet statement couch with chairs and let it rule your space. Velvet just instantly jazzes up the place like nothing else and adds in a generous dollop of chic royalty. Velvet curtains and upholstery too have entered the market and are slowly crawling into our homes. You could begin with black or dark mauve velvet drapes and move to loud bright hues. The key point to remember is not go overboard as velvet on its own self is a statement fabric so minimalism is the keyword to keep in mind while engaging with velvet. Well, it’s time to go ahead and get your velvet on.Text: Ravina Sachdev					Diwali is a time for gifting - and buying something for ourself and our home. What to buy? Plaid and simpleThe key to play with plaid is to not go overboard with it and style it with colourful bright accessories to brighten up the look. “If you ask me about plaid, I can only and only think of the term classic yet trendy. Plaid can be played around with prints and colours but it's not a trend, I would call it an evergreen print that everyone needs to have in their closet. Of course, every year something or the other trendy using plaid comes up and those make good additions to the closet,” shares lifestyle blogger Aleena Macker. You can try your hand at plaid button-down skirts or bright plaid co-ordinates or even plaid mules, there’s no stopping this season. Add a dollop of feminine to plaid through glam jewellery, bold lips or bling bags and watch your style quotient go through the roof!Fringe benefits The best part about the fringe trend is its versatility. Not only can you incorporate these sassy strings into your wardrobe but you can also sport it through any medium i.e. through an accessory or clothing piece or even footwear. “You have a variety of different options when it comes to fringes. You can play around with beads or metallic ropes or even denim, the list just goes on and on,” says fashion blogger Puja Wani, “A well-fitted tee with fringes on denim looks really chic for the day and pair a contemporary sari with a fringed noodle strap crop makes heads turn at a social soirée!” ACCESSORIESSkinny sunglassesWe are totally crushing big time on skinny sunglasses to go along with our skinny tall soy lattes. Trust us when we say that a pair of these can totally escalate your look within seconds. What started with a few sightings on Instagram influencers has only gone up on the fashion ladder with everybody adapting to the style. One thing is for sure, the 90’s skinny game is here to stay for a while and you could try experimenting with the same. While the black skinnies sure do seem like a classic, there are a lot of varieties to choose from. You could go crazy and pick a pair of colour tinted glasses to go with super ripped black denim and a black crop or could try white rimmed statement sunglasses over an all-white outfit for the local Sunday brunch!Bag that styleThe trend started with designer labels such as Gucci and Prada displaying embellished bags on runways and it has only been widely appreciated and accepted by the masses. Imagine bags with tiny fur trims and pearls and fabric patches with logos or numbers. The size of these goodies ranges from tiny shoulder bags to handbags to even totes! A great bag can make or break the look and these embellished bags undeniably enliven the look in a jiffy. Macker says, “For bags or any kind of accessories including shoes, I absolutely love embellishments. It gives so much more character to pieces and if you can customize the embellishments there is just nothing like having your own unique piece. I have to say the Gucci has set the bar high with their embellished bags.” Try carrying a denim shoulder bag with faux pearls and diamonds on a classic white blouse and blue denim to the lazy Saturday lunch with the girls or a box bag with adornments for the cocktail soiree the week after and be indebted to us forever!Dance in trans(parent)!While we were throwing our everyday essentials in a plastic see-through bags last season, this season is all about transparent footwear (now we can openly flaunt our pedicures!). Clear PVC sandals are selling like hot cakes and by the looks of it, this trend is definitely here to stay. With Chanel kicking off the trend early this year and going crazy with plastic covered everything, most designers followed suit. If you think wearing see-through shoes is bizarre, you could participate by wearing a combination of plastic, leather peep toes or sandals with plastic straps, or footwear with plastic heels. You could most certainly wear PVC boots on a bodycon lacy dress if you’re ready to bear it all! Fashion blogger Madhavi Dey says, “PVC shoes are a major life saver. I love wearing these statement pieces see through ankle boots on an all-black ensemble as it just adds the right touch of edge to the outfit.” BEAUTYGive a clean(se) chitWe have finally come to the realization that cleansing oils aren’t the bad heroes we made them out to be. In fact, they are seen to be the most liked product currently. Cleansing is the most effective way of getting dirt free, crystal clear and soft skin in a jiffy and cleansing oils seem to deliver all that and much more efficiently. Experts confirm that while cleansers do strip your skin of natural oils, cleansing oil does not clog your pore. Beauty blogger Stacey Castenha says, “I’ve started using a cleansing oil and it only does wonders to my skin. Not only does it cleans my face really nice but also leaves it glowing and super soft. This is one product that is never exiting my vanity.” Looks like it’s time to put this oil down on the list of things to buy this season!Enhancing beautyThe trend that started sometime early this year has only grown. Face serums are a game changer and people are only starting to realize. Whether your skin is acne-prone or dehydrated or dull, there is a magic potion available for every skin type and for every skin related problem. Majority of us Indian women suffer from dehydrated skin and the answer to that is moisture-based hydration face serum. “People always thought that face serums are a strict no as they make the skin too oily or clog the pores but 2018 has been a game changer. People are understanding their skin like never before and adding these serums to their daily beauty regime,” informs Catenha. Time for a much-needed skincare shopping run! Inclusive beautyA little while back, Rihanna upped her game big time after releasing her foundation line with FENTY Beauty. The foundation that came in a variety of 40 different shades (yes, 40 different shades and we aren’t even joking about it!) made our lives so much simpler. People all over the world went crazy as they no longer had to mix a few different shades in order to create the one suitable for their skin. This started a movement that every skin tone is unique and deserves to be celebrated. It was only logical that soon other beauty brands followed suit and started going beyond the customary 10-15 shade range. “Today, it’s all about customization. Right from outfit to beauty to even food, everybody wants something exclusive designed just for them. The inclusive beauty trend is definitely here to stay and is only going to get bigger and bigger with each season,” says Wani. DÉCORGeometric accentsAs Pantone predicted geometric accents have certainly proved to be the hottest trend of the year in decor. What started as modest triangles and circles on tiny vases and tableware here and there has only blown up and manifested itself on objects everywhere. The octagons and hexagons are repeatedly making bold appearances on items such as home furnishing, tiles, wallpapers, fabrics, etc. among others. Interior decorator Heena Sabhnani shares, “A lot of my clients have been taken aback with what the change they saw in their home by incorporating geometric patterns. It instantly brightens up a dull and boring home and adds just the right touch of modern.” Geometric prints are an easy way to up your décor game and give your home the much needed modern touch that it so needed. You too can join on the bandwagon by getting a bright and colourful wallpaper on the bar wall or you can start by dipping one toe at a time and get geometric wall hangings by the dinning or a subtle rug to start with. Frills and trimsWe are as surprised as you are; as for most of us, fringe belongs in the closet. Well, clearly not anymore as the trend has gotten a major upgrade. This season, the style is moving out of our wardrobes and on our décor and we aren’t complaining one bit. Fringe doesn’t necessarily have to mean overdressed. Lightly fringed hems on lamps or a statement fringe trimmed chandelier add the right touch of flirty modern chic. Everything boring is fun again! Fringes are seen making indiscreet roaring appearances on sofa chairs, statement mirrors wall hangings and other zillion things. Again, you could opt for a fringed sofa set for a modern Gatsby look or start with a tiny fringe trim lamp on the nightstand and thank us later!Lush livingVelvet for the longest time has been synonymous to luxury and opulence and the quickest and easiest way to transform your house and give it a luxurious touch is by upgrading your plain Jane furniture with plush velvet pieces. Earlier, velvet was a fabric that was easy to stain, required a lot of looking after, was really difficult to maintain and was available in limited colours. However, all that has changed and today you can get a variety of different shades and options and you’d be surprised at how low maintenance the fabric is and it really doesn’t require much looking after it. You could start experimenting by getting a plush turquoise throw on or cushions and notice the change or go all out and invest in larger pieces like a purple velvet statement couch with chairs and let it rule your space. Velvet just instantly jazzes up the place like nothing else and adds in a generous dollop of chic royalty. Velvet curtains and upholstery too have entered the market and are slowly crawling into our homes. You could begin with black or dark mauve velvet drapes and move to loud bright hues. The key point to remember is not go overboard as velvet on its own self is a statement fabric so minimalism is the keyword to keep in mind while engaging with velvet. EMPIRE STATE OF MINDEmpire waistlineThe first and most recognisable waistline there is the empire waistline also popularly referred to as the empire silhouette, empire line or just empire style. The basic structure of this waist pattern is categorised by the tightly fitted bodice that ends just below the bust to deliver the whole high-waisted look. The obsession with the high-waisted line began during the 18th century and was brought to fame by the empress of the first French Empire, Napoleon Bonaparte’s wife, Empress Josephine de Beauharnais; which is where the whole regal reference is sourced from. If a style was good enough for an empress, you can be sure it’s good enough for you as well. The entire style is part of the neoclassical style that was obsessed with imitating and replicating or rather reviving the style that could be seen in the ancient Greek and Roman which portrayed women wearing long gowns clinched under the bust.Perhaps it's old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the style a wonderfully romantic appeal. The flowy and really luxurious feel it imparts makes your inner Greek goddess preen with appreciation, accompanied with the fact that it’s incredibly comfy with zero constriction is an advantage that has very women sighing in absolute relief. Its old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the empire waistline style a wonderfully romantic appeal.Match-maker: The empire waist is designed in such a way that it sits above a woman's natural waistline and generally accentuates the bust which is why it is ideally always accompanied with deep scoop necklines or sweetheart and V-necklines.   This style is perfect for those with pear-shaped bodies i.e. having a slim upper body and a more voluptuous lower body. As such if you don’t want to draw attention to your hips then empire waistline is the way to go. The waist tends to emphasise the narrowest part of the body and camouflaging the wider lower body. It’s also great for short people because the raised waistline creates the appearance of extra height. Now, for the don’ts - avoid the billowy, voluminous fabrics. Pleats and gathers are another no-nos.It is best to stick to with A-line structures or sheath that help to highlight your body’s best features instead of hiding it under too much fabric. When wearing an empire waist top, the best choice of bottom wear is either skinny or straight legged pants. Pairing it up with voluminous wide-legged tend it delivers a rather frumpy, disproportionate look. Empire waist dresses are ideal for pregnant women as its flowy and comfortable. DROP DOWNDrop waistAfter the waistline was pulled up to new heights, the winds of change eventually made their way through the world of fashion and according to the laws of the universal: what goes up must come down. So after the waistline enjoyed the lofty highs, during the roaring 20s, it dropped down to become the distinctive dropped waist style. Around the time when women were finally breaking free from a vile instrument of torture also known as the corset, they decided to adopt more masculine silhouettes. It was believed to be seen as female liberation from traditionally-accepted shapes. A dropped waist sits below the actual natural waistline of a woman and is characterised by the line across the hips instead of the waist thereby providing the illusion of a longer torso. The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival. During then the look took on a sportier feel rather than the elegantly sleek feminine look of the 20’s. Designers have experimented around with it for years and while the basic construct was never tampered with, there were several add-ons like belts, pleated and ruffled skirts to give it a little extra something every time.The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival.Match-maker: Dropped waisted looks aren’t quite as popular today as they were before but they haven’t faded into obscurity completely because the whole ‘shapeless’ look is on the prowl and is extremely favoured. The waist makes quite a statement and, if you know just how to wear and accessorise it, it can turn you into an über fashionista who knows how to work any style like a boss. Short drop-waisted look looks fantastic on women with the tall slender willowy figures and narrow hips. With the addition of a ruffled skirt for a flouncy free-flowing look or an A-line skirt for a sleeker formal look, it could swing either way. It would be prudent for women who have a heavier lower half to stay away from the ruffles as it would be super counterproductive and make the lower body look even wider.For those with long legs and a short torso, drop-waisted dress - with moderate heels - works well. And for those with a long torso and short legs, drop waists with high heels will help to balance out the long torso and deliver a balanced, symmetrical look. BASQUE IN ITBasque waistlineWhat could you have in common with a woman who lived during the American Civil War? Nothing much; except maybe your dress’s waistline. The Basque waistline, which is also referred to as the antebellum waistline is a waistline that emerged when the hourglass figure was the shape every woman was vying for. This waistline served to flatter the equally proportioned body of an hourglass shape and has merits for other body types as well.A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures. The style forms a noticeable ‘V’ on the front of the body coming 2-3 inches below the normal waistline. If the pronounced V-shape is too sharp for one’s taste and then the style can also be modified to a softer U-shape. It is a generally flattering style that provides a slimmer and longer torso due to its low ‘V’ and reduces the width of the hips and waist. Though the idea is to love your body no matter what, wanting to take off a couple for inches every now and then using illusionary means is perfectly acceptable. The style originally began as French-fitted bodice or jacket that eventually become part of the dress rather than a separate piece altogether. A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures.Matchmaker: A Basque waistline is flattering for many body shapes; the low V-shaped line lengthens the torso and creates a wonderfully slim silhouette. However, due to the shape of the waistline, the style tends to draw distinct attention to the lower tummy region and if you aren’t comfortable with that then it's best to avoid this style. Pear-shaped bodies or square shaped bodies should not go for this kind of waistline as it would not be able to appropriately accentuate and flatter those kinds of body types. Hourglass and other body types would be able to carry it off perfectly as it helps to balance out the hips and waist due to the elongation illusion the waist creates.   LOSE THE SYMMETRYAsymmetric waistlineThings that are straight and simple are thoroughly uninteresting after a while. In order to shake things up, the fashion industry developed an obsession with everything that was off-centre and unbalanced. And that is because things like that tend to be more interesting. There is more depth, character and visual appeal. From hemlines with varying lengths to slanted necklines, there is something about asymmetrical patterns in an attire that just make the whole look more sophisticated and bold while breaking free from the rigid symmetry.Though an asymmetrical waistline is not as radical as some of the other things in the same school of thought, it is an interesting style to incorporate. An asymmetrical waistline is a style that sits diagonally across the natural waistline. It originates from a point in the natural waistline and then extends down in a slant to the opposite end. In other words, it is just a slanted waistline across your body, high on one side and low on the other.Asymmetrical waistline creates a slimming effect for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies.Match-maker: Asymmetrical waistline is a type of waistline that will create a slimming effect. Thus, it is great for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. WAIST NOT, WANT NOTPrincess seamThe absence of something is often beneficial as well. Though there exist several types of waistlines to go with every kind of body, there is a particular style that does not need a visible waistline. A style that is much beloved and which is about as timeless as the name itself - the princess seam style. It is a style that will probably never go out of style and is an epitome of soft feminity.A princess seam or line is characterised by the long seams that start from below the arm, or under the shoulder and curves delicately over the bust and down the body to give a prominent long look that that associated with A-line dresses. The seam can be stitched into blouses or dresses to have the desired structure and shape. Due to the way it is designed, the style does not need a waistline since it runs along panels down the body. The princess seam was associated with Charles Frederick Worth, a prominent English fashion designer of the 19th and 20th century who is also acknowledged by many as the ‘Father of Haute Couture’. The style was of course created for Princess Alexandra of Denmark, the wife of King Edward VII. Due to its fitted and figure-hugging design, it was believed to be the first ‘bodycon’ (who are we to deny that fact?).The princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.Match-maker: The princess seam works remarkably well for those with hourglass figures, the long, shapely seams that gather in at the waist and flare out again at the hips. However, the princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.  It’s a wardrobe staple for every lady, kind of like a good pair of shoes or an LBD. Or better yet an LBD with princess seams is a very acceptable option as well.  Either way, knowing what looks good on your unique body is the first step to being fashionably perfect every day but the personal interpretations and add-ons are what make the outfit your identity.  Text: Crystal SymssImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock					One thing that is never up for compromise is to look one's best at all times. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. WAIST NOT, WANT NOTPrincess seamThe absence of something is often beneficial as well. Though there exist several types of waistlines to go with every kind of body, there is a particular style that does not need a visible waistline. A style that is much beloved and which is about as timeless as the name itself - the princess seam style. It is a style that will probably never go out of style and is an epitome of soft feminity.A princess seam or line is characterised by the long seams that start from below the arm, or under the shoulder and curves delicately over the bust and down the body to give a prominent long look that that associated with A-line dresses. The seam can be stitched into blouses or dresses to have the desired structure and shape. Due to the way it is designed, the style does not need a waistline since it runs along panels down the body. The princess seam was associated with Charles Frederick Worth, a prominent English fashion designer of the 19th and 20th century who is also acknowledged by many as the ‘Father of Haute Couture’. The style was of course created for Princess Alexandra of Denmark, the wife of King Edward VII. Due to its fitted and figure-hugging design, it was believed to be the first ‘bodycon’ (who are we to deny that fact?).The princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.Match-maker: The princess seam works remarkably well for those with hourglass figures, the long, shapely seams that gather in at the waist and flare out again at the hips. However, the princess seam works well with any body type as the seams help to slenderize your frame.  It’s a wardrobe staple for every lady, kind of like a good pair of shoes or an LBD. Or better yet an LBD with princess seams is a very acceptable option as well.  Either way, knowing what looks good on your unique body is the first step to being fashionably perfect every day but the personal interpretations and add-ons are what make the outfit your identity.  Text: Crystal SymssImages: Yogen Shah and Shutterstock					One thing that is never up for compromise is to look one's best at all times. To do so is vastly simple and it turns out that we were fussing over the wrong waistline this entire time! All you need is the knowledge about the many waistlines available out there, and know the perfect one for you. The dress with the right waistline will give you a flattering silhouette that will highlight all the right areas and hide the ones you don’t want to show! In order to achieve the perfectly flattering silhouette that you’ve always dreamed of, picking an outfit with the right waistline that matches your body shape is all there is to it (cheers all around). So no slumpy, sloppy ill-fitting attire and wardrobe malfunctions because we are here to deliver to you the fashion tips to match the right body shape to the right waistline. It’s the kind of matchmaking we are here to help with! So read on, and get ready for some shopping for the coming season. You will look on point always, and ensure you make heads turn.  EMPIRE STATE OF MINDEmpire waistlineThe first and most recognisable waistline there is the empire waistline also popularly referred to as the empire silhouette, empire line or just empire style. The basic structure of this waist pattern is categorised by the tightly fitted bodice that ends just below the bust to deliver the whole high-waisted look. The obsession with the high-waisted line began during the 18th century and was brought to fame by the empress of the first French Empire, Napoleon Bonaparte’s wife, Empress Josephine de Beauharnais; which is where the whole regal reference is sourced from. If a style was good enough for an empress, you can be sure it’s good enough for you as well. The entire style is part of the neoclassical style that was obsessed with imitating and replicating or rather reviving the style that could be seen in the ancient Greek and Roman which portrayed women wearing long gowns clinched under the bust.Perhaps it's old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the style a wonderfully romantic appeal. The flowy and really luxurious feel it imparts makes your inner Greek goddess preen with appreciation, accompanied with the fact that it’s incredibly comfy with zero constriction is an advantage that has very women sighing in absolute relief. Its old-time origins and traces in the 18th century that give the empire waistline style a wonderfully romantic appeal.Match-maker: The empire waist is designed in such a way that it sits above a woman's natural waistline and generally accentuates the bust which is why it is ideally always accompanied with deep scoop necklines or sweetheart and V-necklines.   This style is perfect for those with pear-shaped bodies i.e. having a slim upper body and a more voluptuous lower body. As such if you don’t want to draw attention to your hips then empire waistline is the way to go. The waist tends to emphasise the narrowest part of the body and camouflaging the wider lower body. It’s also great for short people because the raised waistline creates the appearance of extra height. Now, for the don’ts - avoid the billowy, voluminous fabrics. Pleats and gathers are another no-nos.It is best to stick to with A-line structures or sheath that help to highlight your body’s best features instead of hiding it under too much fabric. When wearing an empire waist top, the best choice of bottom wear is either skinny or straight legged pants. Pairing it up with voluminous wide-legged tend it delivers a rather frumpy, disproportionate look. Empire waist dresses are ideal for pregnant women as its flowy and comfortable. DROP DOWNDrop waistAfter the waistline was pulled up to new heights, the winds of change eventually made their way through the world of fashion and according to the laws of the universal: what goes up must come down. So after the waistline enjoyed the lofty highs, during the roaring 20s, it dropped down to become the distinctive dropped waist style. Around the time when women were finally breaking free from a vile instrument of torture also known as the corset, they decided to adopt more masculine silhouettes. It was believed to be seen as female liberation from traditionally-accepted shapes. A dropped waist sits below the actual natural waistline of a woman and is characterised by the line across the hips instead of the waist thereby providing the illusion of a longer torso. The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival. During then the look took on a sportier feel rather than the elegantly sleek feminine look of the 20’s. Designers have experimented around with it for years and while the basic construct was never tampered with, there were several add-ons like belts, pleated and ruffled skirts to give it a little extra something every time.The drop waist though popular with the 20’s flapper dresses are more commonly remembered in their 60’s revival.Match-maker: Dropped waisted looks aren’t quite as popular today as they were before but they haven’t faded into obscurity completely because the whole ‘shapeless’ look is on the prowl and is extremely favoured. The waist makes quite a statement and, if you know just how to wear and accessorise it, it can turn you into an über fashionista who knows how to work any style like a boss. Short drop-waisted look looks fantastic on women with the tall slender willowy figures and narrow hips. With the addition of a ruffled skirt for a flouncy free-flowing look or an A-line skirt for a sleeker formal look, it could swing either way. It would be prudent for women who have a heavier lower half to stay away from the ruffles as it would be super counterproductive and make the lower body look even wider.For those with long legs and a short torso, drop-waisted dress - with moderate heels - works well. And for those with a long torso and short legs, drop waists with high heels will help to balance out the long torso and deliver a balanced, symmetrical look. BASQUE IN ITBasque waistlineWhat could you have in common with a woman who lived during the American Civil War? Nothing much; except maybe your dress’s waistline. The Basque waistline, which is also referred to as the antebellum waistline is a waistline that emerged when the hourglass figure was the shape every woman was vying for. This waistline served to flatter the equally proportioned body of an hourglass shape and has merits for other body types as well.A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures. The style forms a noticeable ‘V’ on the front of the body coming 2-3 inches below the normal waistline. If the pronounced V-shape is too sharp for one’s taste and then the style can also be modified to a softer U-shape. It is a generally flattering style that provides a slimmer and longer torso due to its low ‘V’ and reduces the width of the hips and waist. Though the idea is to love your body no matter what, wanting to take off a couple for inches every now and then using illusionary means is perfectly acceptable. The style originally began as French-fitted bodice or jacket that eventually become part of the dress rather than a separate piece altogether. A Basque waistline is flattering V-shaped waistline that is ideally beneficial for curvaceous figures.Matchmaker: A Basque waistline is flattering for many body shapes; the low V-shaped line lengthens the torso and creates a wonderfully slim silhouette. However, due to the shape of the waistline, the style tends to draw distinct attention to the lower tummy region and if you aren’t comfortable with that then it's best to avoid this style. Pear-shaped bodies or square shaped bodies should not go for this kind of waistline as it would not be able to appropriately accentuate and flatter those kinds of body types. Hourglass and other body types would be able to carry it off perfectly as it helps to balance out the hips and waist due to the elongation illusion the waist creates.   LOSE THE SYMMETRYAsymmetric waistlineThings that are straight and simple are thoroughly uninteresting after a while. In order to shake things up, the fashion industry developed an obsession with everything that was off-centre and unbalanced. And that is because things like that tend to be more interesting. There is more depth, character and visual appeal. From hemlines with varying lengths to slanted necklines, there is something about asymmetrical patterns in an attire that just make the whole look more sophisticated and bold while breaking free from the rigid symmetry.Though an asymmetrical waistline is not as radical as some of the other things in the same school of thought, it is an interesting style to incorporate. An asymmetrical waistline is a style that sits diagonally across the natural waistline. It originates from a point in the natural waistline and then extends down in a slant to the opposite end. In other words, it is just a slanted waistline across your body, high on one side and low on the other.Asymmetrical waistline creates a slimming effect for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies.Match-maker: Asymmetrical waistline is a type of waistline that will create a slimming effect. Thus, it is great for those full figured or thick-waisted ladies. On the other hand, those on the shorter side should stay away from this waistline as the long waist will make the rest of the body appear shorter. However, if you have short height, you should not opt for this waistline style as this will just make you appear shorter. This year is all about pastel colours, from runways to the fashion streets. Be it shades of almond or subtle hues of cream and pink, this one fashion trend is here to stay for a long time. Find out five different ways you can style these ice cream colours right: Wear a pastel coloured sweater over a simple white T-shirt or top. Pair it with distressed jeans and casual shoes. Add a shoulder bag to the outfit.  Style a striped monochrome top with a pair of black skinny jeans and don a pastel coloured shrug over it. Wear comfortable loafers and a sling bag to complete the look. Pair a tie-up striped top with a pastel mini skirt along with a handbag. Add flats for a casual look.  Wear a printed dress with beige heels ideal for a party look. Also, add a plain pastel coloured bag to offset the prints. Style a printed pastel top with a printed bright skirt for a daring yet fun look. Complete the outfit with a pair of stylish sandals.					Factors like comfort and the rise of casual wear like kurti-palazzo duo has led to fusion wear being one of the most followed trends this season. Today’s women want to combine contemporary styles with a hint of vintage charm. Thus, it becomes all the more important for you to pair the two separates right. Here we tell you five different ways you can style Indo-western outfits: Style a high-low kurti with boyfriend or casual jeans. Add a saddle bag and a pair of oxford shoes to complete the look. Jacket style kurti with a pair of palazzos is appropriate for both college and work. Wear it with loafers or slip-ons. Wear a printed kurta with a pair of printed palazzos for a bold and beautiful fashion statement. Complete the outfit with white sneakers to offset the prints. Don a shirt-style kurta with a pair of well-fitted trousers and add casual shoes to the look. Pair a kurti dress with trousers which is ideal for a casual day out with friends. Carry a tote bag to complete the look effortlessly.					The big news—lilac is set for a major comeback. This year is all about pastel colours, from runways to the fashion streets. We can’t exactly pinpoint the time when outlandish became fashionable, but it should be around the time when designers like Virgil Abloh and Demna Gvasalia burst onto the scene (of course, Alessandro Michele being the flagbearer). In the past few months, we have witnessed crocs get a couture update, and sunglasses go ridiculously tiny. But what has the caught the fancy of It-girls around the world and even our B-Town club is the ugly sneaker. Inspired from the trainers once seen in your dad’s footwear closet in the ’90s, these oversized sneakers are the epitome of cool today. How to identify them—well look for chunky shapes, stacked sole and (most probably) a fashion-forward celeb rocking these with their on-point style. Here’s proof. Off-shoulder style has lived and thrived amongst us since the 1800s–the era of art, architecture, romance and fashion in the form of elaborate dresses. Having a feminine appeal and an ability to blend with different silhouettes has made it every woman’s wardrobe essential. From red carpet gowns to a girl’s go-to date clothing, off-shoulder has found its way everywhere and in everything. Even the Indian bridal wear designers are not spared and are often seen experimenting with the trend. The best thing about it? You need not worry about going to the gym and getting perfectly-toned shoulders— just hop in one of the exposed shoulder dresses and you are ready to go. B-town fashionistas like Kangana Ranaut, Alia Bhatt and Anushka Sharma are often seen in these fresh, sporty looks. The trend has been embraced by major high-fashion brands and has been spotted on the runways for a few seasons now. There are three things you definitely need to flaunt this look—a comfortable outfit, a cool pair of sneakers and a major dose of attitude. Let’s see five different ways of sporting athleisure: Pair a printed short sleeve T-shirt with track pants for a casual day out with friends. You can complete the look by wearing white sneakers for women or sport shoes.   A plain T-shirt paired with printed track pants is an ideal combination for a lazy college day. Complete the look with either white sneakers or sport shoes. Pair a casual tank top with training tights to look gym-ready. Add boots to your outfit instead of sneakers and you are good to hit the club at night.  					There is nothing off about this trend, paradoxical to its name. Believed to be invented in 1873 by Jacob Devis and Levi Strauss, denim has come a long way since its inception. Today, it has forayed into footwear, accessories, furniture and even vehicles as seat covers. From the most eminent designers in the fashion fraternity to celebrities and even influencers, denim has spared no one and is everyone’s go-to clothing item. We tell you five ways you can style denim this season and look stunningly fashionable:What comes to your mind when you think of comfort and style together? A stylish pair of casual jeans indeed! Considered a wardrobe must-have, a pair of casual jeans could be styled with a simple, embellished T-shirt. To make the outfit look swish and smart, add-on a pair of white sneakers or flats.  When our favourite skinny jeans become a big no-no in the monsoon season, bootcut jeans come to our rescue. Pair them with a printed, chiffon shirt to keep your look easy-breezy. Complete this look by wearing crocs or slip-ons.  Wearing denim-on-denim is one fashion combination that can never go wrong. Style a well-fitted denim shirt with a slightly lighter shade of denim culottes and you’re ready to take on the world. Complete the look with floater sandals.   A-line skirts are in vogue! And what’s better than having them in denim. Don an off-shoulder, striped top over an A-line denim skirt to look perfect for a casual day out with friends. Pair the outfit with monsoon boots to complete the look. What is the perfect colour-combination you ask for women's fashion? White and denim hands down! Wear a printed white T-shirt, on skinny white jeans and pair them with a denim jacket. The entire ensemble exudes chicness. Complete the look with white sneakers.					Isn’t this statement the absolute truth? With the recent incident at Cannes 2018, where American actor Kristen Stewart was seen removing her heels on the red carpet as a protest against the film festival’s dress code—all female guests should wear heels–the message was crystal clear: No more telling us what to wear! With well-being as the topmost priority, women have consciously replaced the gut-wrenching experience of wearing stilettos with congenial foot candies, sneakers! According to a report by NPD’s group retail tracking service, sales of heels dropped by 12 per cent in the year 2017, while the sneakers market witnessed a boom of 37 per cent. Experts claim that other than factors like comfort and health concerns among women, one rationale seen for the decrease in the sales of heels is casualisation of every occasion. Let’s find out how Bollywood celebs are rocking the trend. One of the leading actors in Bollywood, Alia Bhatt flaunts her Madison pants and Adidas sneakers at the airport. Her off-white handbag, paired with the coolest pair of black shades, completes the athleisure look.  In her Alcoolique trench, Shopbop white crop top and Deme by Gabriella pants, Shraddha Kapoor slays this look in all its glory. The Zara shoes worn by the actor complete the outfit effortlessly.  When it comes to style, Malaika Arora can never go wrong. Here she styles an airport look by wearing a Narendra Kumar outfit.  Actor Mahira Khan looks exemplary in this perfectly styled outfit. Her flawless ensemble paired with YSL shoes oozes modishness and excellence.  When it comes to new trends, the Bollywood fashionista can never be left behind. Kareena Kapoor Khan looks simple yet stylish in this airport look. She wears an off-white shirt with a pair of well-fitted denims. The sporty sneakers complete the outfit with utmost ease.  Sophie Choudry surely knows how to pull off an all-denim attire. The Gucci shoes effortlessly complement her Topshop outfit and Claudie Pierlot jacket. The arm candy by Jimmy Choo and the Fendi glares complete the look.					The one piece of clothing that can make any outfit look well-styled instantly is denim.
