We demystify the main types so you can pull them off like the women of Bollywood.GinghamGingham is one of the most common variants you can wear. It’s a basic, evenly-sized checkered pattern with no more than two colours. While it’s most commonly used on shirts, you could also pair matching separates like this bandeau-skirt combo on Alia Bhatt.Play with the size of the print for different results, like this mini-check jacket on Bhumi Pednekar.Windowpane checksWindowpane checks are exactly what they sound like – thin, spaced out checks that form a graph-like pattern. Since they’re subtle, they work great when you’re wearing print-on-print, like this checked blouse and striped sari on Jacqueline Fernandez.Vidya Balan sports the thicker variant of the windowpane check in this Kanjeevaram sari.Bend the rules and wear dotted checks instead of stripes like this cropped top on Tamannaah Bhatia.TartanTraditionally used for Scottish kilts, tartan is formed with unequally-sized checks, in two or more colours. Sonakshi Sinha wears a tartan slip dress over a plain white tee for a casual ensemble.This gathered-waist tartan skirt on Sonam Kapoor pays tribute to the original Scot kiln.If you’re looking for something more feminine, this tartan off-shoulder dress on Huma Qureshi is a good place to start. 													If you didn’t know what a coat dress (aka trench dress) was earlier, Priyanka Chopra’s 2017 Met Gala look surely taught you a thing or two. The Ralph Lauren dress (and the train attached to it) that entered our collective conscience last year might be too avant-garde to pull off on an occasion that doesn’t involve a red carpet, but that’s no reason for you to shy away from trying the trend that all of B-Town seems to now be obsessed with. Here’s all the coat dress inspiration you’ll need.Minimal and monochrome were the two keywords for Aditi Rao Hydari in this white Zara coat worn with black booties.													Shilpa Shetty Kundra looks like royalty in this red, fit-and-flare trench dress by Madison.													Match your lipstick with your printed coatdress like Kajol Devgan.													Millennial pink can step aside to make way for hot pink. – Kajal Aggarwal in Plakinger.													For the risqué at heart, play a little peek-a-boo with your lingerie like Rhea Chakraborty.													We’re not quite over the mustard colour trend, and clearly Genelia Deshmukh in Twelve AM:PM agrees.													Flaunt those legs like Parul Gulati in a maroon coat dress by Zara.													A variant of the coat dress is the blazer dress, like this ruffle-detail number by Nishka Lulla on Rakul Preet Singh													Sonakshi Sinha mixes it up with a solid, longline wrap coat over an embellished top, by Nikita Mhaisalkar.													Add some colour with a belt or skirt underneath, or both, like Surveen Chawla in Madison (jacket) and Cover Story (skirt). The fashion world never seems to run out of ways to make shoulder-show uber chic. From cold to off to one, there are tons of ways to flaunt your shoulders and look fab while you’re at it. One-shoulder outfits in particular are a simple detail that can transform your ordinary look to a truly red carpet-worthy ensemble. Here is some inspiration from Bollywood’s finest on how you can pull off the trend. Kriti Sanon shows you how it is done in a black red-carpet ensemble. Anushka Sharma sticks to her classic style in a Falguni & Shane Peacock outfit. The Kapoor sisters give us major twinning goals in their monochrome outfits. Esha Gupta looks sharp in a Monsoori gown. Mandira Bedi flaunts her chiseled clavicle in a Swapnil Shinde outfit. Aditi Rao Hydari does modern androgyny in a deconstructed shirt and flared trousers. Bhumi Pednekar in Nikhil Thampi. “The Fossil Q Gen 3 does everything a smartwatch should while looking as gorgeous as it does,” says actor Shruti Haasan, who loves everything about this smartwatch. According to Shruti, this watch is just like her and goes well with her glamorous and free-spirited personality. The actor identifies with Fossil Q Gen 3 for its simple yet tech-savvy features like activity and sleep trackers, touchscreen display, Bluetooth support and notification alerts for mails, messages, social media, etc. Like her, the watch is simple yet chic.The best part, however, is that this smartwatch is custom-made for women and is available in rose-gold colour, which is a hot favourite. From the strap to the dial, Fossil has paid attention to make it look trendy and elegant. Irresistible features like music control, battery life of up to 24 hours, LED flashlight and water-resistant make it a must-have for every woman. What more, this smartwatch is compatible with Android 4.3+ and iOS 9+ devices, and is recommended by Shruti herself. Here’s what she has to say about Fossil Q Gen3 smartwatch.  Q&A with Shruti HaasanOn Fossil: There’s a sense of belonging you feel with certain brands since it defines you and fits you perfectly. That’s the feeling I get when I think of Fossil. It resonates with my style—a little bit of love and a whole lot of vintage. On Fossil Q Gen 3: I love geeking out on tech advancements! The Gen 3 does everything a smartwatch should while looking as gorgeous as it does. I’m hardly ever without my phone, and I’m usually in a tizzy when I can’t find it. The watch has been a lifesaver in such situations. I’ve also checked emails, notifications, sent tiny and quick messages, used my phone’s music app, and controlled phone calls. It’s pretty much my mini phone. I’ve almost abused the selfie feature. I’m constantly taking pictures of my friends, family and self. There’s a lot more I’ve to learn about the watch, but for now, this is what I generally use it for. On smartwatch options for women: I was thrilled to find out that there were real options for women’s watches and not just smaller dials and pink straps. We have been given real choices and not looked upon as an afterthought. I’ve always loved rose gold-coloured jewellery and watches, so it’s just that much better for me! There’s just so much more to explore when it comes to the world of Fossil women’s smartwatches. Why Shruti recommends this watch to others: I love how the watch seems to play with the user, just as much as the user plays with the watch. That’s what makes it so unique. So, yes, definitely recommending this to everyone I know. I think it also would make an ideal first-time watch. The user interface is simple and the variety of straps and dial settings are immense. One word that defines Fossil Q Gen 3: 'Me' That’s the first thing I thought of when I put the watch on my wrist. This watch is in tune with my lifestyle, and who I am as a person. I think that’s the same thought most people who use the watch will have.Buy this smartwatch on Flipkart 													It’s been several months since the off-shoulder trend made a comeback on the runways but going by its popularity among celebrities (and everyone else!), we can safely say that it is here to stay.Disha Patani’s off shoulder look will take you straight to a ballroomA tease with the off-shoulder gameWe adore this dramatic off-shoulder look!Shruti keeps it casual yet classy with her top Huma’s fun attire is perfect for every mood A pop of contemporary to the traditional with the trend is a must!Sonakshi Sinha’s breezy white top is perfect for a beach vacay. One word that defines Fossil Q Gen 3: 'Me' That’s the first thing I thought of when I put the watch on my wrist. This watch is in tune with my lifestyle, and who I am as a person. The final day of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 gave an indication of what’s going to impact your sartorial choices in spring and summer. Take a look. RufflesSpring catwalks around the world are cascading with ruffles and the Capital wasn’t an exception. While Rina Dhaka included the frilly detail in her saris, kurtas and dresses at the finale, Ashish N Soni juxtaposed them on clean and classic silhouettes to make his ready-to-wear line look young, fun and sensuous. Flash dance shoulderThis is an evolution of the off shoulder trend. Designer Sulakshana Monga adapted the peekaboo treatment for her clothes, flash dance or the ‘accidental’ shoulder show that reveals a little flesh without showing too much was a predominant trend. Monga used Half-on, half-off tops and dresses with single ruffled shoulders exposing only a slice of skin. If you wear this, keep the rest of the outfit simple and let your shoulder do the talking. Sheer fabricSheer fabrics such as chiffon, tulle, mesh, organza and chanderi have been summer staples for long and they made an impactful appearance on the runway at the Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018. From hemlines, tops with sheer insets, skirts and dresses at Monga’s to sheer in Indian wear--embellished sheer lehengas and blouses and saris at the Suneet Varma’s show--the trend was ubiquitous. Traditional embroideryIndian culture and craftsmanship were both profusely showcased on the ramp via traditional motifs and intricate embroideries. From thread embroidery at Pankaj and Nidhi, Krishna Mehta and Charu Parashar to intricate zardozi embroidery seen at Suneet Varma’s show, this ethnic element is here to stay though the silhouettes may vary from western contemporary to Indian.  													With Amazon India Fashion Week Spring-Summer 2018 almost drawing to a close, it was time for some of the fashion industry's best known names to showcase their collections.Anju Modi's line titled Swadeshi was a tribute to heritage designs in khadi with a contemporary twist, like tie-and-dye and asymmetric cuts.Madhu Jain displayed her expertise in juxtaposing different weaves, motifs and textile traditions of the country.Payal Jain celebrated her 25 years in the industry with a collection that's purely an ode to her muse Frida Kahlo and her paintings. Jain had got her friends and family and actor Vaani Kapoor to walk the ramp in her creations.Kavita Bhartia remained true to her love for femininity in the form of pretty florals, summer hues and geometric prints.Shivan & Narresh packed all razzle dazzle in their line of swimwear, dresses and saris with prints inspired by Japanese artist Araki’s works.Huemn's collection had a fearless aesthetic appropriate to counter the dystopian world we live in. Reconstructed shirts, up-cycled denims and hooded jackets were some of the key pieces.Dhruv Kapoor showcased a collection that strives to break stereotypes with an interplay of relaxed fabric, interesting patchwork and motifs, and costume design.  Kavita Bhartia presented her line A Diary of Flowers at AIFW SS18 Day 4Feminine hues, floral motifs ad geometric patterns found their way in Kavita Bhartia's collection Madhu Jain presents her AIFW SS18 lineVeteran designer Madhu Jain's collection displays her strengths in th sphere of craft and textile revival. Fashion for a dystopian world in Huemn's Spring-Summer line for AIFW SS18Designers Pranav Misra and Shyma Shetty make a fashion and political statement with their eclectic line Dhruv Kapoor marries bling with fabric in a muted tone to stunning effect.Each outfit in the Dhruv Kapoor line for AIFW SS18 challenges stereotypes with eclectic pairing of various elements. Detailed skein motifs, and lush flowers inspired by Japanese artist, Araki, in Shivan and Narresh's AIFW SS18 line.Shivan and Narresh presented the Araki series for AIFW SS18. A model in a khadi outfit by Anju Modi.Anju Modi celebrated 25 years in the fashion industry with a Swadeshi collection in khadi. Payal Jain celebrated 25 years in fashion at AIFW SS18.Actor Vaani Kapoor was the striking showstopper for Payal Jain's line celebrating her 25 years in fashion. Day four of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018 saw an abundance of clashing prints, all-white ensembles, dramatic hemlines and statement sleeves. Here’s a round up of the trends that is sure to get your attention: Shades of whiteMany shades of white were spotted on the runway. They offered a stark contrast to the multitude of prints and colours. From Madhu Jain, Kavita Bhartia to Abhi Singh and Ekta Jaipuria and Ruchira Kandhari paired white with white in their collections. If you’re not big on white-on-white, add a few loose fitted casual styles from Payal Jain, frilly and flirty skirts from Kavita Bhartia or a few traditional cotton kurtas from Madhu Jain to your wardrobe and mix and match it with other colours. Shirts under spaghetti strapsStylistas Kim Kardashian and Kendall and Kylie Jenner have been doing this for a while now and designers Dhruv Kapoor and Abhi Singh seemed to have got the drift. Models sashayed down the ramp wearing risqué spaghetti dresses and tank tops over shirts in different sizes and shapes. So ladies, it’s time to bring out your slinky dresses. Print on printThe runway saw an abundance of clashing patterns and prints, proving that this trend for the brave will be big in the upcoming season. While Shivan and Narresh had matching top and bottom sets with prints boasting of forest sights, Dhruv Kapoor matched ditsy florals with vintage prints. Exaggerated sleevesThis is one of the biggest trends for spring summer. And there are so many different types of statement sleeves to suit different types of arms. From billowy bell shaped, ultra long and oversized to ruffled, cinched at the wrist to exaggerated cuffs, there’s enough to last you more than one season. Asymmetrical hemlinesEverything isn’t straight and narrow for summers, designers played with geometry and courted the asymmetrical hemlines in myriad ways. Anju Modi brought the mullet back in fashion—her kurtas had hemlines that were short at the front and long in the back. Meanwhile, Kavita Bhartia, Dhruv Kapoor and Bhanuni by Jyoti experimented with the handkerchief hemline. While Shivan and Narresh had matching top and bottom sets with prints boasting of forest sights, Dhruv Kapoor matched ditsy florals with vintage prints. Exaggerated sleevesThis is one of the biggest trends for spring summer. And there are so many different types of statement sleeves to suit different types of arms. From billowy bell shaped, ultra long and oversized to ruffled, cinched at the wrist to exaggerated cuffs, there’s enough to last you more than one season. Asymmetrical hemlinesEverything isn’t straight and narrow for summers, designers played with geometry and courted the asymmetrical hemlines in myriad ways. Anju Modi brought the mullet back in fashion—her kurtas had hemlines that were short at the front and long in the back. Meanwhile, Kavita Bhartia, Dhruv Kapoor and Bhanuni by Jyoti experimented with the handkerchief hemline.																		Summery trenches, feminine florals, restrained monochromes and classic plaids, were trending on day 3 of Amazon India Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2018.  Lay the trenchesThe summer trench coat is going to be one wardrobe classic in the coming season. The classic trench coat was exquisitely upgraded with thread embroidery by Payal Pratap, deconstructed and made feminine with floral prints by Shruti Sancheti and kept sombre with single tones by Pallavi Dhyanee. Flower powerFloral prints are no longer a surprise for summer, but next season brings big blossoms in all kinds of styles as seen at Shruti Sancheti, Payal Pratap and Pallavi Singhee shows. Pratimaa Pandey, however, used it judiciously by decorating the hems and necklines with floral embroidery. Black and white worldMonochrome is one of the strongest trends this spring summer season. Designers Abraham & Thakore, Rajesh Pratap Singh and Medha Khosla of Anomaly championed the stark black and white contrast. The two shades were interpreted in abstract and clashing prints, stripes and panels. Get creative and work the trend by opting for block separates, a monochrome dress or a monochrome print.  Woven handloomsWoven handlooms are clearly the fabric of the future. With sustainable fashion topping the agenda of most designers, an urban sensitivity was introduced to the fabric. From clean, minimalist work wear to luxurious day and evening wear, handlooms found an easy expression in the spring summer lines of Anomaly, Rajesh Pratap Singh, Abraham and Thakore and Payal Pratap.  Plaid and simplePlaids had a major moment on the runaway of day 3. Checked patterns have been a winter favourite for long, but designers such as Payal Pratap, and Teresa Liasom and Utsav Pradhan of Munkee See and Munkee Do and Pallavi Dhyani gave it fun and colourful interpretation for spring. But Rajesh Pratap Singh decided to keep it staid by taking the conventional way for his shirts, jackets and trousers.																		The collections showcased on day 2 of Amazon India fashion Week SS/18 seemed to have comfort on the top of their priority list. From billowy silhouettes and wide-leg pants to utilitarian jumpsuits and bomber jackets, there was adequate inspiration for girl-next-door. The new bomberDesigner Aarti Vijay Gupta combined sports luxe with her signature quirky prints and easy anti-fit silhouettes. We spotted the printed and fitted bomber jacket, casually thrown over long tees, kurtas and dresses.  Wide-leg pantsRoomy trousers stood out as a dominant trend on the runway. The new, sometimes flared and at other times straight and sometimes with slits was worn with almost everything from shirts and kurtas to dresses. The baggy pants leave about enough room for your legs to not stick to the fabric in summer months. We liked the ones we saw on the runway at Ikai, Patine and Love Bird’s shows.   StripesThe predominant pattern at the Amazon India Fashion Week, this season was the ubiquitous stripes – big, bold, subtle, horizontal, and vertical and in all shapes and sizes. While Ragini Ahuja explored stripes in all its avatars from bold to zig zag, Love Birds and Aarti Vijay Gupta resorted to subtle versions. Billowy silhouettesThis one-size-fit-all trend comes as good news for all Indian women on the heavier side. It is evident from the ramp that designers paid enough attention to the fact that some women need more relaxed styles. Our top picks are the ant-fit dresses seen in Love Birds’s show, the jackets, kurtas and cropped tops in Ragini Ahuja’s collection and the loose, free-flowing tops and dresses from Rina Dhaka’s new line.  Reinvented jumpsuitsDesigner Ashish N Soni expressed his signature creativity in his spring summer line that also marked his 25th year in the industry. He gave the utilitarian jumpsuit an interesting spin by adding to it dramatic saree pallu drapes. This season, wear the reinvented jumpsuit to the formal evening parties and watch heads turn. Warm weather may be months away but comfortable, fuss-free clothes are always on our mind. Who doesn’t wish to get into easy-breezy outfits and hit the outdoors? To help you make sound fashion decisions, we have put together some runway trends from the ongoing Amazon India Fashion Week SS/18 that you can actually wear in real life. From exaggerated lines, metallic hints to bright candy colours, Day 1 had all the inspiration you need for your summer wardrobe. Take a look.Metallic hintsIt's always a good time to be experimental. A good way to add fun and excitement to your wardrobe is to introduce metallic hints to your outfits or accessories. Rimzim Dadu infused metallic hues in silver, gold and blue into her range of re-imagined saris, sculpted statement tops jackets and skater dresses. If you aren’t sure of metallic outfits, begin with accessories. A hint of metallic is sure to get you noticed. Sorbet coloursPassionate pastels or sorbet shades have been making quite a wave on international runways and they made a strong appearance in Anupama Dayal’s show. She used lilacs, lavender, melons and sunset hues on gossamer and light fabrics such as chiffons and Chanderis. A deviation from the pop and neon colours, these shades will add a breath of fresh air to your summer wardrobe. Shoulder obsessionFashion’s fascination with shoulders rages on. The off-shoulder trend manifested itself in Samant Chauhan’s Victorian gowns and Anupama Dayal’s playful jumpsuits. Rock the trend by adding your own clever twists to it--sport the silhouette on your top and pair it with skirts and pants or go the traditional way by teaming a sari with the top. Athleisure boomWearing workout gear as a part of your casual outfit is the new in thing. Nida Mahmood fused age-less Indian art from around the country onto sporty silhouettes to create an athlesiure range in collaboration with active lifestyle brand Deivee. There were cycling shorts, leggings and running saris strutting down the ramp. Oversized ruffle collarsRuffle collars bring to mind images of the erstwhile queens of England. The aristocratic ruffle collar made a comeback in the Indigofera collection by Schulen Fernandes for Wendell Rodricks. They added a sharp colour contrast and an element of intrigue to fluid silhouettes. Outfit topperJackets in varying lengths are the current flavour of the season and are expected to enjoy the exalted status in the next season too. While JJ Valaya used long jackets with streamlined silhouettes over traditional saris, anarkalis and lehenga cholis, the brand Aureole paired hand woven cropped jackets and shrugs with dresses for maximum impact in its show. Day 4 had some stellar shows by ace designers Anju Modi and Rahul Mishra. From classic silhouettes to traditional embroideries and from understated elegance to new age detailing, there was no dearth of fashion inspiration. Here’s what reigned the ramp. Floral storyThe floral story this season is whimsical, elegant and rooted to tradition. Rahul Mishra used resham threads to recreate intricate floral motifs of the Mughal era and mixed them with geometric and abstract patterns, giving them a contemporary twist. Anju Modi too followed the historical route and brought alive floral patterns from Rajasthan. Perfectly imperfect hemlinesAnju Modi added a bohemian yet sophisticated touch to her ensembles by introducing uneven hemlines on her long kurtas. The quintessentially laid-back style lent a certain nonchalance to her classic designs. Single outSingle-hue styles are not only figure-flattering but also make you look taller, so we were happy to spot the monochrome trend in both Anju Modi and Rahul Mishra’s collections.High timeAt the Rahul Mishra show, models sashayed down the ramp in high slit column kurtas paired with flared trousers and lehengas. The waist high slits made the outfits look edgy, contemporary and regal—all at once.Velvet touchAs far as fabrics go, nothing looks as rich and sophisticated as velvet. And Anju Modi, a costume revivalist known for her opulent creations, used it as a canvas for her Kishangarh inspired art work in lehengas, kurtas and jackets. If you aren’t the kind to wear an entire velvet outfit, then throw in a dupatta or a jacket tor a chic, dignified look. Day 4 had some stellar shows by ace designers Anju Modi and Rahul Mishra. So, we weren’t surprised when they found their way into Indian outfits. Day one of India Couture Week 2017 started off to a great start with ace couturiers Anamika Khanna and Rohit Bal showcasing their opulent collections. While Khanna chose to go the international way by putting up an installation of her collection "Happily Ever After" where buyers could touch and feel the clothes, Bal left no stone unturned in putting up a stunning show for his collection "Shahaan-e-Khaas". Here are a few trends that we rounded up for you. Capes take centre stageLast year cape blouses over lehengas made a strong appearance on the ramp. This year, Bal consolidates the purpose of a cape as an essential outerwear by layering it over blouses and lehengas and anarkalis.White is always rightMove over reds and maroons to make way for ivory, which was a dominant colour in both Khanna and Bal’s collections.Versatile separates rule the game Individuality and creativity will make your wedding ensemble stand out and this is what Khanna strongly believes in. Her collection had versatile statement pieces that the bride can mix and match to create a look to complement her mood and personality.The past aligns with the presentBoth Khanna and Bal brought alive the rich craft and heritage of India by reviving age-old zardozi metal and fine thread work on clothes with contemporary form and structure. Most of the pieces were deeply rooted in tradition yet had a global appeal.Sheer fun with fabricsKeeping in mind that the modern bride values comfort over customs, the designers experimented with lightweight sheer fabrics. Most of the pieces were deeply rooted in tradition yet had a global appeal.Sheer fun with fabricsKeeping in mind that the modern bride values comfort over customs, the designers experimented with lightweight sheer fabrics. Day one of India Couture Week 2017 started off to a great start with ace couturiers Anamika Khanna and Rohit Bal showcasing their opulent collections. While Khanna chose to go the international way by putting up an installation of her collection "Happily Ever After" where buyers could touch and feel the clothes, Bal left no stone unturned in putting up a stunning show for his collection "Shahaan-e-Khaas". Here are a few trends that we rounded up for you. Capes take centre stageLast year cape blouses over lehengas made a strong appearance on the ramp. This year, Bal consolidates the purpose of a cape as an essential outerwear by layering it over blouses and lehengas and anarkalis.White is always rightMove over reds and maroons to make way for ivory, which was a dominant colour in both Khanna and Bal’s collections.Versatile separates rule the game Individuality and creativity will make your wedding ensemble stand out and this is what Khanna strongly believes in. Her collection had versatile statement pieces that the bride can mix and match to create a look to complement her mood and personality.The past aligns with the presentBoth Khanna and Bal brought alive the rich craft and heritage of India by reviving age-old zardozi metal and fine thread work on clothes with contemporary form and structure. Most of the pieces were deeply rooted in tradition yet had a global appeal.Sheer fun with fabricsKeeping in mind that the modern bride values comfort over customs, the designers experimented with lightweight sheer fabrics. But heels have their own advantages—they make us look taller, give shape to our legs and posterior and we instantly feel glamorous. However here are few problems that every girl understands when she is wearing heels for too long:You want to look like this And do this  But after a few minutes you end up doing this You wished you looked this sexy while doing everyday chores But instead, this is what happens When you go to a party looking all hot and sexy in the beginning, at then you walk back home like this You want to feel like a goddess when you are dancing But you end up getting to the dance floor like this And then your whole life falls apart when you see this. What kind of sorcery is this. Well, love it or hate it there’s no living without it.  As the growing popularity of cruise shows indicates, between Instagram-worthy beach escapes, destination weddings and glamping, resort fashion has indeed come a long way. Whether you’re reclining on sun loungers or cruising over gorgeous landscapes in a hot air balloon, there’s no excuse to look sloppy anymore, especially when you travel. While the island state of mind is just that—a state of mind—the allure of a glorious coverup, a feather-light kaftan or one of those hand-woven, basket totes is real, palpable and, suddenly, everywhere.  Spring/summer 2017 runways are proof that resortwear can go well beyond throw-on-and-go pieces. Take Miu Miu’s retro Italy-inspired collection, which comprise a line of ruched bikinis, patterned robe-style dresses and teensy twinsets, accompanied by embossed pool slides and appliqued swim caps. Miuccia Prada understands the value of a chic escape. “It’s a celebration of summer and its pleasures,” she mused during the post-show interview. Dolce & Gabbana also sought inspiration from the Italian tropics for its covered sundresses, bralets and miniskirts in fun prints (think pasta, seafood and gelato). The show venue even had a counter serving fresh tender coconut water and models strutted down the runway to the rhythms of the tarantella. Giorgio Armani presented a line of slouchy bloomers, sheer cover-ups and short suits, featuring painterly prints and tassels—just what we need for those soirées under the stars. The accessories followed suit; the flatforms at Prada and Chloé would make for stylish accoutrements on a holiday. For their spring/summer 2017 collection, Delhi-based designer duo Hemant and Nandita elevated holiday basics like swimsuits, shorts, crop tops and sarong-esque skirts using Victorian ruffles and vibrant print play. Nishka Lulla set out to reinvent the pantsuit, working with softer fabrics and delicate embellishments to transform it into a resort essential. Lulla says, “I used lightweight, everyday materials like cotton and tulle in relaxed comfy silhouettes, with frills and flounces thrown in for good measure.” Aparna Badlani, curator and co-owner of multi-designer boutique Atosa, Mumbai, has long recognised the potential of well-made resortwear. “At a point when destination weddings are such a huge phenomenon, the category is finally getting its due,” she says. If there’s one image that captures the exquisite charm of travel, it’s got to be that of actor and socialite Talitha Getty hanging out on the terrace of her Marrakech home, immortalised by photographer Patrick Lichfield in the late ’60s.  It even inspired Yves Saint Laurent to design a line of kaftans that he called Une Passion Marocaine. Designer and TV personality Nicole Richie, who has a perpetual vacation vibe about her, best embodies this spirit today. Her style reminiscent of LA’s boho-luxe aesthetic from the ’60s and the ’70s. Whether it’s through pictures of Taylor’s Swift’s glamorous squad chilling together on a yacht or Olivia Palermo and beau Johannes Huebl’s romantic romp in Greece, travel continues to fire our imagination and inform fashion in the most powerful ways.  Much like with eveningwear, building a bankable resortwear wardrobe takes work. “Start with the basics and build from there. Think kaftans, palazzos, shorts, day dresses and strappy sandals,” says Badlani. According to Lulla, the trick is to invest in lightweight, versatile separates that can be paired with other items from your wardrobe. “Take, for instance, bustiers that you can wear on the beach or with high-waisted bottoms for a night out,” she says. It’s always a good idea to mix luxe pieces with exotic finds from local boutiques and markets to create a look that is uniquely yours. Bon voyage! Abaya is an outer garment worn by Muslim women. It also called burqa in certain countries. This garment is a long robe or cloak, which covers the body except for head, feet, and hands. The traditional abayas are black in colour. But now, these abayas have now got a fashion makeover.    The women, who are style savvy women and love to boast the tradition and trend can try the updated versions. We got in touch with LimeRoad's fashion stylist, Rina S Walia to talk about the new styles:   1. Denim love The long denim abaya is the best for the all-denim look. This can be paired with printed or solid cotton head scarf for any easy outdoor look. Add a pop of colour, by carrying a neon sling bag.    2. Pick the Pleats Pleats are always going to be on trend. Try a black one with colourful pleats at the bottom. Complete the look with a pair of pumps and a black sling bag.     3. Pretty pastels Pastel shades have become the talk of the town. Try a beautiful pastel pink abaya as the go-to attire for days when you want to look effortlessly stylish.    4. Cape Craze Capes are totally ruling the ramps this season. Don't lag! Wear a cape abaya and tune up your feminine charm. It's perfect for summer day outs.     (Abaya images: Limeroad.com)  Gabriela Hearst: Gabriela Hearst is a true-blue Instagram success story. The clothes were a mix of billowing silhouettes, couture, and all the summer hues.    (All images: PTI) One of the most definitive trends for fall is the return of shine on the runways. As designers get nostalgic for the flamboyant ’80s, sequins go gangsta and shiny vinyl finds its way back into our closet. This season sparkle comes imbued with a street sensibility as the more-is-more mantra from our favourite decade clashes with athleisure’s fluid dynamism. Cue the season’s sharpest plissé skirts teamed with a pair of equally luxe sneakers. Designers drummed up a host of options that make an easy transition from the cubicle to the dance floor. We’re looking to Michael Kors’ slashed sequinned mini dresses and Phoebe Philo’s egg-shaped lurex pullovers at Céline for inspiration. “I like bare legs in winter; I like night for day. I like Alexa Chung mixing with Nan Kempner. It’s about the interesting mix,” said Kors in an interview post his show. At Kenzo, Humberto Leon and Carol Lim sent out a line of vinyl dresses and skirts, foil-print trousers and oversized metallic jackets. Isabel Marant flirted with vinyl too in retro styles, adding animal prints and plaid to the mix. “It really goes back to when I would sneak out, aged 15, to punk clubs like Le Palace and Les Bains Douches,” said the Parisian designer. Between Marc Jacobs’ subversive separates at NYFW and Rajesh Pratap Singh’s gilded army closer home, the message is loud and clear—street glamour is here to stay. Designer Sanchita Ajjampur’s futuristic mash of foil, mesh and paillettes, and Gaurav Jai Gupta’s street-style spin on metallic handlooms, further confirm the mood of the times. It’s evident that fashion is making no bones about its Ziggy Stardust-meets-Beyoncé philosophy, and the pop culture influencers are lapping it up. Historically, the first image that comes to mind in this category is that of  ’60s fashion icon and rocker Keith Richards’s then girlfriend Anita Pallenberg who took to the Cannes red carpet in a lurex jumper. Leave it to the Kardashian-Jenner clan to reinvent Pallenberg’s louche luxe uniform as they elevate street style basics like sweatshirts, lace-up boots and trackpants. Kendall Jenner even brought back the chainmail dress from the ’90s. Closer home Alia Bhatt is having a go with unexpected pairings like a camo shirt and a plissé skirt, offering us a fresh take on the trend.      Which brings us to the question of how to do it right. Archana Walavalkar, celebrity stylist and co-founder Stylecracker, says that styling is everything here. “It’s important to blend the look seamlessly, not letting the shiny piece acquire hero status at any point.” It’s a good idea to stock up on basics like hologram sweatshirts, sequinned numbered tees, slip dresses with a glamorous sheen, and metallic denims. If you’re shine-shy, begin with a statement accessory. Let the gleaming heels from Demna Gvasalia’s debut at Balenciaga or Fendi’s festive-edition gold totes give you some ideas. “Go casual with jeans and a tee teamed with embellished sandals. This is easier to pull off if you don’t quite dare to go all guns blazing,” says Ajjampur. Fine jewellery is also following suit by putting a casual spin to sparkle. Case in point: Nirav Modi’s Embrace range of diamond bangles, which stretch like a dream, offer a snug fit and are best worn with denims and a boyfriend shirt. The writing’s on the wall: Whatever your glittery vice may be, it’s time to wear it on your sleeve.   One of the most definitive trends for fall is the return of shine on the runways. The writing’s on the wall: Whatever your glittery vice may be, it’s time to wear it on your sleeve.   Wendell Rodricks is a man credited with many firsts. At a time when Indian fashion was all about opulence and grandeur, he introduced the idea of minimalism. He was one of the few Indian designers to bring eco-friendly textiles to the forefront and also pioneered resortwear in India. To commemorate his contributions to the fashion industry, Rodricks was awarded the Padma Shri title in 2014. While contemporaries are predictably passing on their legacies and labels to family members, the designer has entrusted it into the hands of young prodigy Schulen Fernandes. And he did it in his inimitable style, bang in the middle of the runway at his label's fall/winter showing at the 2016 Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW). In a fun, free-wheeling chat, Rodricks and Fernandes tell us about what's in store for the legendary label.Wendell, after holding the reins for 28 years, you've decided to hand them over to Schulen. Schulen, how did he break it to you and what was your reaction?Wendell Rodricks: I always wanted the label to go to somebody I trusted. Schulen came to me straight from college and she has been with me for four years. She had already started taking a lot of creative decisions for the label. For instance, last season we did the Indica Emporia presentation at LFW with vintage Indian garments. It was completely her vision and work from start to end. I wanted to slowly take the backseat with this label so that I could make time for my other passions. I felt the time was just right for her to take the label and fly with it.Schulen Fernandes: It obviously didn't happen out of the blue. The handover was always on the cards and it took two years of work laying the foundation. However, when the actual moment arrived, it was hard to believe. How are your roles divided in the new scheme of things?WR: I’d like to think of myself as a benevolent dictator (laughs). On a serious note, Schulen has complete freedom to realise her creative vision at the label now and I am happy to have her take over.SF: Wendell will obviously be the mentor. My work will now involve everything from conceptualising collections to actually bringing it to life. I am also excited about the business end of it and we have a competent team to help us on that front.Schulen, tell us a little bit about your debut collection, Trapezoid, for the Wendell Rodricks label presented at LFW. And, Wendell, what did you think of it?SF: I have always loved architecture and geometry. The trapezoid form has been used in architecture from ancient times and it is so versatile. We decided to explore it in fashion with this collection. We used a mix of structured shapes and fluid fabrics working with paper silks, chanderis and a lot of eco-friendly materials. WR: I was really surprised when Schulen came up with the idea. It is a form that I've seen in Inca and Aztec architecture and in our temple gopurams. The Indian woman's body which is narrow at the shoulders and wide at the hips also follows the trapezoid form. This was particularly relevant because for the first time we introduced a size chart specific to the Indian woman at LFW this season. I felt really proud watching the show. The biggest compliment to me and to Schulen was when people told us it (the collection) looked like Wendell Rodricks. When a new creative leader takes charge at a fashion house, change is afoot—what can we expect from the label?WR: I've always focussed on high-end fashion and have never been able to cater to the mid-range. I hope Schulen will be able to expand the reach of this label to more people the way my colleague Anita Dongre has done very successfully. I also want her to take risks with the label and be more experimental.SF: We will definitely retain the minimalistic language and eco-friendly DNA of the label as we move forward. I would like to introduce newer, younger silhouettes and experiment heavily with materials. What lies ahead for both of you? Wendell, do you miss being behind the wheel? Schulen, are you at all daunted?WR: I don’t miss being behind the wheel at all. I can finally dedicate time to things that I’ve been waiting to do. The work on the museum is underway (Rodricks is turning his Goa home into a space dedicated to Goan costumes). The dogs are taking it well but my three cats are giving me grief about the move! I would like to write a lot more. My next book Poskem is about Goa. I hope I’ll be able to turn it into a movie like Chetan Bhagat (laughs). I’d like to teach a lot more too.SF: I am excited about what lies ahead and loving every minute of my new job. Going forward we’ll be extending the brand to include luxury lifestyle segments too.Photographs: Gary Taylor, Vinay Javkar/Lakmé Fashion Week winter/festive 2016 Wendell Rodricks is a man credited with many firsts. At a time when Indian fashion was all about opulence and grandeur, he introduced the idea of minimalism. He was one of the few Indian designers to bring eco-friendly textiles to the forefront and also pioneered resortwear in India. To commemorate his contributions to the fashion industry, Rodricks was awarded the Padma Shri title in 2014. While contemporaries are predictably passing on their legacies and labels to family members, the designer has entrusted it into the hands of young prodigy Schulen Fernandes. And he did it in his inimitable style, bang in the middle of the runway at his label's fall/winter showing at the 2016 Lakmé Fashion Week (LFW). In a fun, free-wheeling chat, Rodricks and Fernandes tell us about what's in store for the legendary label.Wendell, after holding the reins for 28 years, you've decided to hand them over to Schulen. Schulen, how did he break it to you and what was your reaction?Wendell Rodricks: I always wanted the label to go to somebody I trusted. Schulen came to me straight from college and she has been with me for four years. She had already started taking a lot of creative decisions for the label. For instance, last season we did the Indica Emporia presentation at LFW with vintage Indian garments. It was completely her vision and work from start to end. I wanted to slowly take the backseat with this label so that I could make time for my other passions. I felt the time was just right for her to take the label and fly with it.Schulen Fernandes: It obviously didn't happen out of the blue. The handover was always on the cards and it took two years of work laying the foundation. However, when the actual moment arrived, it was hard to believe. How are your roles divided in the new scheme of things?WR: I’d like to think of myself as a benevolent dictator (laughs). On a serious note, Schulen has complete freedom to realise her creative vision at the label now and I am happy to have her take over.SF: Wendell will obviously be the mentor. My work will now involve everything from conceptualising collections to actually bringing it to life. I am also excited about the business end of it and we have a competent team to help us on that front.Schulen, tell us a little bit about your debut collection, Trapezoid, for the Wendell Rodricks label presented at LFW. And, Wendell, what did you think of it?SF: I have always loved architecture and geometry. The trapezoid form has been used in architecture from ancient times and it is so versatile. We decided to explore it in fashion with this collection. We used a mix of structured shapes and fluid fabrics working with paper silks, chanderis and a lot of eco-friendly materials. WR: I was really surprised when Schulen came up with the idea. It is a form that I've seen in Inca and Aztec architecture and in our temple gopurams. The Indian woman's body which is narrow at the shoulders and wide at the hips also follows the trapezoid form. This was particularly relevant because for the first time we introduced a size chart specific to the Indian woman at LFW this season. I felt really proud watching the show. The biggest compliment to me and to Schulen was when people told us it (the collection) looked like Wendell Rodricks. When a new creative leader takes charge at a fashion house, change is afoot—what can we expect from the label?WR: I've always focussed on high-end fashion and have never been able to cater to the mid-range. I hope Schulen will be able to expand the reach of this label to more people the way my colleague Anita Dongre has done very successfully. I also want her to take risks with the label and be more experimental.SF: We will definitely retain the minimalistic language and eco-friendly DNA of the label as we move forward. I would like to introduce newer, younger silhouettes and experiment heavily with materials. What lies ahead for both of you? Wendell, do you miss being behind the wheel? Schulen, are you at all daunted?WR: I don’t miss being behind the wheel at all. I can finally dedicate time to things that I’ve been waiting to do. The work on the museum is underway (Rodricks is turning his Goa home into a space dedicated to Goan costumes). The dogs are taking it well but my three cats are giving me grief about the move! I would like to write a lot more. My next book Poskem is about Goa. I hope I’ll be able to turn it into a movie like Chetan Bhagat (laughs). I’d like to teach a lot more too.SF: I am excited about what lies ahead and loving every minute of my new job. The actress is seen in a pair of Maison Martin Margiela boots with a cape jacket from Rishta by Arjun Saluja and a long black top. This is the most obvious choice. With a shirt dress: Katrina Kaif wore them with a monochrome striped shirt dress from McQ by Alexander McQueen. A pair of shorts, belts (to add some structure) and hair kept open gave her a breezy, casual look, keeping the focus on the boots. With LBDs: Like Molly King. Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Here’s our edit of all the celebrity-approved ways to flaunt the colour-block trend in style  Kareena Kapoor KhanEver thought two bright tones cannot work together? Tara SutariTara Sutaria broke the monotony of her black and white outfit by teaming it with a bright neon skirt, another way of working the colour-block trend.  Athiya ShettyAthiya Shetty opted for a contrasting gown in lime green and beige, working two contradicting hues in the same outfit.  Alia BhattInstead of infusing multiple colours in the same outfit, Alia Bhatt chose contrasting separates in two bright hues, an innovative way of sporting the colour-block trend.					There are risqué trends, and then there is the cut-out dress trend. The peek-a-boo skin-show moment has an understated appeal to it. There are multiple ways in which you can wear the cut-out dress. The geometrical shape can be carved out from the centre, showing your toned midriff or from the sides and the back, accentuating your curves. There is a nip in the air and the weather is finally getting pleasant. Although we do not get to enjoy the perks of a full-blown winter just yet, we can still relish the season with an upgraded wardrobe. You can also make it your workwear staple like Meghan Markle who is an official fan of the buttoned-down shirt dress trend. Every celebrity has a distinctive travel style, but there’s a common love shared for the closet staple kurta. Instead of flexing their sartorial muscles in high-end, street-style brands, the leading ladies have chosen the simple kurta as their favourite. Of course, they amp it up with their Hermès Birkin and Gucci sunglasses, but the dainty kurta sets still takes the centre stage. While Deepika Padukone prefers her kurtas to be form-fitted in bright, jewel tones, Kareena Kapoor is a fan of over-sized kurtas in neutral shades. Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Here’s our edit of all the celebrity-approved ways to flaunt the colour-block trend in style  Kareena Kapoor KhanEver thought two bright tones cannot work together? Take a cue from Kareena Kapoor Khan. The actor styled her aqua-blue bodysuit with a neon green, sequined, pencil skirt. Neutralising the look further with a pair of transparent, strappy heel.  Kriti SanonKriti Sanon effortlessly worked this form-fitting colour-blocked gown. She kept the rest of her look minimal with a pair of dainty, hoop earrings, and centre-parted hair.  Aditi Rao Hydari Aditi Rao Hydari demonstrated a distinctive of wearing the power suit. She opted for an ox-blood and burnt orange asymmetrical pantsuit, which she styled with a traditional choker.  Tara SutariTara Sutaria broke the monotony of her black and white outfit by teaming it with a bright neon skirt, another way of working the colour-block trend.  Athiya ShettyAthiya Shetty opted for a contrasting gown in lime green and beige, working two contradicting hues in the same outfit.  Alia BhattInstead of infusing multiple colours in the same outfit, Alia Bhatt chose contrasting separates in two bright hues, an innovative way of sporting the colour-block trend.					There are risqué trends, and then there is the cut-out dress trend. The peek-a-boo skin-show moment has an understated appeal to it. There are multiple ways in which you can wear the cut-out dress. The geometrical shape can be carved out from the centre, showing your toned midriff or from the sides and the back, accentuating your curves. Recently, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen in a lemon yellow, diamond-shaped, midriff cut-out dress by Dion Lee, at the trailer launch of her movie. The actor teamed the dress with a pair of strappy heels, dainty earrings and hexagon-shaped glasses. You can easily replicate this look at your next Sunday brunch with the girls. Scroll down to view all the celebrity-approved ways of wearing a cut-out dress.  Nushrat Bharucha Nushrat Bharucha styled this metallic, side cut-out dress by Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna with a pair of high heels and pushed-back sleek hair. A party look you can easily imitate.  Janhvi KapoorJanhvi Kapoor raised the heat in this multiple cut-out, asymmetrical Basil Soda gown. The young actor complemented the ensemble with a pair of statement Sophie Webster heels and a stark red mouth. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde broke the solid colour monotony of this bright-coloured yellow dress with a pair of aqua-hued earrings. A smart styling hack you can incorporate in your next look.  Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor effortlessly worked the monochromatic, sequined, side cut-out dress by Prabal Gurung. The actor kept the rest of her look simple with a sleek ponytail, drop earrings and a hint of glitter on the lids. If less is more is your vibe, this look is tailor-made for you. Kiara AdvaniKiara Advani looked like a vision in this double textured, side cut-out dress. If you want to give the sequin and bright colour combination a rest, you can opt for this minimal-chic outfit by Prabal Gurung.					There is a nip in the air and the weather is finally getting pleasant. Although we do not get to enjoy the perks of a full-blown winter just yet, we can still relish the season with an upgraded wardrobe. A fail-safe trend you can bet on is the shirt dress, it’s cosy, comfortable and ultra-stylish. It’s basically a shirt sans the pants, but we’re not complaining.You can style it with a broad belt like Sonakshi Sinha, or wear it oversized like Malaika Arora. Layer it with a blazer and you’re boardroom ready, or team it with thigh-high boots for a night on the town. You can also make it your workwear staple like Meghan Markle who is an official fan of the buttoned-down shirt dress trend. We’ve rounded up a list of celebrity-approved shirt dress looks for you to take style inspiration from. Malaika AroraWant to achieve that laid-back, relaxed, chic look? Take cue from Malaika Arora who styled her oversized grey shirt with a pair of fiery red, ankle-length boots. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde upped her street-style game with this metallic blue, striped shirt, which she styled with a Gucci, belt bag and chained sunglasses. You can imitate this look if you want to give your basic shirt dress an upgrade. Demonstrating how to work this trend the old-school, classic way. Deepika PadukoneIf minimalism isn’t your thing and you’re all about those intricate details, opt for this long, form-flattering, knotted shirt dress by Rajesh Pratap. There is a nip in the air and the weather is finally getting pleasant. Although we do not get to enjoy the perks of a full-blown winter just yet, we can still relish the season with an upgraded wardrobe. A fail-safe trend you can bet on is the shirt dress, it’s cosy, comfortable and ultra-stylish. It’s basically a shirt sans the pants, but we’re not complaining.You can style it with a broad belt like Sonakshi Sinha, or wear it oversized like Malaika Arora. Layer it with a blazer and you’re boardroom ready, or team it with thigh-high boots for a night on the town. You can also make it your workwear staple like Meghan Markle who is an official fan of the buttoned-down shirt dress trend. We’ve rounded up a list of celebrity-approved shirt dress looks for you to take style inspiration from. Malaika AroraWant to achieve that laid-back, relaxed, chic look? Take cue from Malaika Arora who styled her oversized grey shirt with a pair of fiery red, ankle-length boots. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde upped her street-style game with this metallic blue, striped shirt, which she styled with a Gucci, belt bag and chained sunglasses. You can imitate this look if you want to give your basic shirt dress an upgrade. Sonam Kapoor AhujaSonam Kapoor Ahuja wore this black and white, Cover Story dress, designed by Karl Lagerfeld and teamed it with a pair of sleek, black boots. Demonstrating how to work this trend the old-school, classic way. Karisma KapoorIf the idea of wearing a plain shirt dress to work sounds mundane to you, layer it with a blazer and a pair of cool sneakers, just like Karisma Kapoor did. Shraddha KapoorInstead of digging deep in your closet to find that perfect party dress, borrow a formal shirt from your boyfriend, team it with a wide, waist-clenching belt and you have a winning look on your hands. Deepika PadukoneIf minimalism isn’t your thing and you’re all about those intricate details, opt for this long, form-flattering, knotted shirt dress by Rajesh Pratap. Ditch the jewellery, like Deepika Padukone, and allow the dress to take the centre stage. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon kept this day look fuss-free in an emerald green, shirt dress by Nupur Kanoi and styled it with a pair of closed-toe heels and geometrical earrings by Azotiique. Kriti KharbandaKriti Kharbanda was seen working the trend in this printed shirt dress and kept the rest of the look clean with just a high top-knot.   The most recurring sari during the festive season was the sequin laden six yards by Manish Malhotra, another innovative rendition of the classic silhouette by the couturier. The shimmer sari has become a go-to sartorial choice for almost every leading lady in Bollywood. The latest addition to the list is Bhumi Pednekar who opted for an off-white sequin sari, and teamed it with a dainty velvet blouse during her movie promotion. While Bhumi went for a classic-chic look, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen sporting a rose-pink sequin sari with a barely-there blouse. Kapoor Khan punctuated the risqué look with a layered diamond necklace and her signature makeup. Here’s our edit of all the versatile ways in which you can work this trend. Bhumi PednekarBhumi Pednekar is all about the less is more formula, seen here in an antique white, sequin sari and blouse, sans the jewellery. Tara Sutaria  The young and vivacious Tara Sutaria stepped out in a smoke grey, sequin sari and blouse combination for the recent Diwali festivities. To do justice to this all-embellished ensemble, Tara swapped heavy statement jewellery for a dainty layered necklace and complemented it with soft and peachy makeup. Natasha PoonawallaThe all-time advocate of all things extra, Natasha Poonawalla pulled all stops with this sage green sequin sari and styled it with an emerald green necklace, suitable for a Maharani. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon’s take on the trend was a little different from her contemporaries. She styled her shimmering sari with a strappy, backless blouse, chandelier earrings, deep smokey eyes and Mogra bearing low bun. Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor in a sequined black sari is a vision to behold. Step into summers with a fresh hair style to set the tone of the season right. Amp it up with a fresh colour hue, cut it short for a sassy touch-up, beat the heat with ponies and buns, or better still…feel the wind in your hair in style with an exaggerated side parting. Here’s how to take on the sunny spirit, this year:Cool colourWavy bobNaughty knotDeep side partOn-point pony Airport style has recently gained momentum, thanks to the growing paparazzi culture. Every celebrity has a distinctive travel style, but there’s a common love shared for the closet staple kurta. Instead of flexing their sartorial muscles in high-end, street-style brands, the leading ladies have chosen the simple kurta as their favourite. Of course, they amp it up with their Hermès Birkin and Gucci sunglasses, but the dainty kurta sets still takes the centre stage. While Deepika Padukone prefers her kurtas to be form-fitted in bright, jewel tones, Kareena Kapoor is a fan of over-sized kurtas in neutral shades. Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Here’s our edit of all the celebrity-approved ways to flaunt the colour-block trend in style  Kareena Kapoor KhanEver thought two bright tones cannot work together? Take a cue from Kareena Kapoor Khan. The actor styled her aqua-blue bodysuit with a neon green, sequined, pencil skirt. Neutralising the look further with a pair of transparent, strappy heel.  Kriti SanonKriti Sanon effortlessly worked this form-fitting colour-blocked gown. She kept the rest of her look minimal with a pair of dainty, hoop earrings, and centre-parted hair.  Aditi Rao Hydari Aditi Rao Hydari demonstrated a distinctive of wearing the power suit. She opted for an ox-blood and burnt orange asymmetrical pantsuit, which she styled with a traditional choker.  Tara SutariTara Sutaria broke the monotony of her black and white outfit by teaming it with a bright neon skirt, another way of working the colour-block trend.  Athiya ShettyAthiya Shetty opted for a contrasting gown in lime green and beige, working two contradicting hues in the same outfit.  Alia BhattInstead of infusing multiple colours in the same outfit, Alia Bhatt chose contrasting separates in two bright hues, an innovative way of sporting the colour-block trend.					There are risqué trends, and then there is the cut-out dress trend. The peek-a-boo skin-show moment has an understated appeal to it. There are multiple ways in which you can wear the cut-out dress. The geometrical shape can be carved out from the centre, showing your toned midriff or from the sides and the back, accentuating your curves. Recently, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen in a lemon yellow, diamond-shaped, midriff cut-out dress by Dion Lee, at the trailer launch of her movie. The actor teamed the dress with a pair of strappy heels, dainty earrings and hexagon-shaped glasses. You can easily replicate this look at your next Sunday brunch with the girls. Scroll down to view all the celebrity-approved ways of wearing a cut-out dress.  Nushrat Bharucha Nushrat Bharucha styled this metallic, side cut-out dress by Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna with a pair of high heels and pushed-back sleek hair. A party look you can easily imitate.  Janhvi KapoorJanhvi Kapoor raised the heat in this multiple cut-out, asymmetrical Basil Soda gown. The young actor complemented the ensemble with a pair of statement Sophie Webster heels and a stark red mouth. While Katrina Kaif layered her embellished pantsuit on a delicate lace bra, Sonakshi Sinha and Jacqueline Fernandez opted for monotone pantsuits and bralette combinations. Putting their envy-inducing abs on display. Scroll down to find all the different ways in which the celebrities have styled their pantsuits with a sleek bralette. Bhumi PednekarBhumi Pednekar styled her shimmering, sequined suit with a barely-there embellished bra. Making a solid case for balanced opulent dressing. Ileana D’CruzIleana D’Cruz teamed her powder pink pantsuit with a textured bra, breaking the monotony of a plain old suit. Jacqueline FernandezJacqueline Fernandez chose a sunshine yellow suit and bralette, all in the same hue. Giving a lesson on how to work this trend in monotone. Sonakshi SinhaSonakshi Sinha gave her checkered suit a modern spin by layering it over a solid coloured bralette instead of a regular shirt.Sonakshi Sinha put her rock-solid abs on display in this over-sized, powder blue pantsuit, which she styled with a sports bra in a twin shade. Demonstrated the sporty-chic way of wearing the pantsuit with a bralette trend. Katrina KaifKatrina Kaif wore her silver, sequined pantsuit with a lacey bra, showcasing how to work two contrasting elements in the same ensemble.					Colour blocking is a versatile trend that is no longer restricted to just mixing two colours in an outfit. You can colour-block your look by teaming separates in two different hues or by teaming a singular-toned outfit with a contrasting coloured accessory or shoes. Bring out some bold hues and style them together like Alia Bhatt did; or break the monotony of solid black outfit with a dash of colour like Kareena Kapoor Khan. For those who aren’t a fan of busy prints and multiple elements, this trend is a perfect pick. Here’s our edit of all the celebrity-approved ways to flaunt the colour-block trend in style  Kareena Kapoor KhanEver thought two bright tones cannot work together? Take a cue from Kareena Kapoor Khan. The actor styled her aqua-blue bodysuit with a neon green, sequined, pencil skirt. Neutralising the look further with a pair of transparent, strappy heel.  Kriti SanonKriti Sanon effortlessly worked this form-fitting colour-blocked gown. She kept the rest of her look minimal with a pair of dainty, hoop earrings, and centre-parted hair.  Aditi Rao Hydari Aditi Rao Hydari demonstrated a distinctive of wearing the power suit. She opted for an ox-blood and burnt orange asymmetrical pantsuit, which she styled with a traditional choker.  Tara SutariTara Sutaria broke the monotony of her black and white outfit by teaming it with a bright neon skirt, another way of working the colour-block trend.  Athiya ShettyAthiya Shetty opted for a contrasting gown in lime green and beige, working two contradicting hues in the same outfit.  Alia BhattInstead of infusing multiple colours in the same outfit, Alia Bhatt chose contrasting separates in two bright hues, an innovative way of sporting the colour-block trend.					There are risqué trends, and then there is the cut-out dress trend. The peek-a-boo skin-show moment has an understated appeal to it. There are multiple ways in which you can wear the cut-out dress. The geometrical shape can be carved out from the centre, showing your toned midriff or from the sides and the back, accentuating your curves. Recently, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen in a lemon yellow, diamond-shaped, midriff cut-out dress by Dion Lee, at the trailer launch of her movie. The actor teamed the dress with a pair of strappy heels, dainty earrings and hexagon-shaped glasses. You can easily replicate this look at your next Sunday brunch with the girls. Scroll down to view all the celebrity-approved ways of wearing a cut-out dress.  Nushrat Bharucha Nushrat Bharucha styled this metallic, side cut-out dress by Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna with a pair of high heels and pushed-back sleek hair. A party look you can easily imitate.  Janhvi KapoorJanhvi Kapoor raised the heat in this multiple cut-out, asymmetrical Basil Soda gown. The young actor complemented the ensemble with a pair of statement Sophie Webster heels and a stark red mouth. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde broke the solid colour monotony of this bright-coloured yellow dress with a pair of aqua-hued earrings. A smart styling hack you can incorporate in your next look.  Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor effortlessly worked the monochromatic, sequined, side cut-out dress by Prabal Gurung. The actor kept the rest of her look simple with a sleek ponytail, drop earrings and a hint of glitter on the lids. If less is more is your vibe, this look is tailor-made for you. Kiara AdvaniKiara Advani looked like a vision in this double textured, side cut-out dress. If you want to give the sequin and bright colour combination a rest, you can opt for this minimal-chic outfit by Prabal Gurung.					There is a nip in the air and the weather is finally getting pleasant. Although we do not get to enjoy the perks of a full-blown winter just yet, we can still relish the season with an upgraded wardrobe. A fail-safe trend you can bet on is the shirt dress, it’s cosy, comfortable and ultra-stylish. It’s basically a shirt sans the pants, but we’re not complaining.You can style it with a broad belt like Sonakshi Sinha, or wear it oversized like Malaika Arora. Layer it with a blazer and you’re boardroom ready, or team it with thigh-high boots for a night on the town. You can also make it your workwear staple like Meghan Markle who is an official fan of the buttoned-down shirt dress trend. We’ve rounded up a list of celebrity-approved shirt dress looks for you to take style inspiration from. Malaika AroraWant to achieve that laid-back, relaxed, chic look? Take cue from Malaika Arora who styled her oversized grey shirt with a pair of fiery red, ankle-length boots. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde upped her street-style game with this metallic blue, striped shirt, which she styled with a Gucci, belt bag and chained sunglasses. You can imitate this look if you want to give your basic shirt dress an upgrade. Sonam Kapoor AhujaSonam Kapoor Ahuja wore this black and white, Cover Story dress, designed by Karl Lagerfeld and teamed it with a pair of sleek, black boots. Demonstrating how to work this trend the old-school, classic way. Karisma KapoorIf the idea of wearing a plain shirt dress to work sounds mundane to you, layer it with a blazer and a pair of cool sneakers, just like Karisma Kapoor did. Shraddha KapoorInstead of digging deep in your closet to find that perfect party dress, borrow a formal shirt from your boyfriend, team it with a wide, waist-clenching belt and you have a winning look on your hands. Deepika PadukoneIf minimalism isn’t your thing and you’re all about those intricate details, opt for this long, form-flattering, knotted shirt dress by Rajesh Pratap. Ditch the jewellery, like Deepika Padukone, and allow the dress to take the centre stage. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon kept this day look fuss-free in an emerald green, shirt dress by Nupur Kanoi and styled it with a pair of closed-toe heels and geometrical earrings by Azotiique. Kriti KharbandaKriti Kharbanda was seen working the trend in this printed shirt dress and kept the rest of the look clean with just a high top-knot.   The most recurring sari during the festive season was the sequin laden six yards by Manish Malhotra, another innovative rendition of the classic silhouette by the couturier. The shimmer sari has become a go-to sartorial choice for almost every leading lady in Bollywood. The latest addition to the list is Bhumi Pednekar who opted for an off-white sequin sari, and teamed it with a dainty velvet blouse during her movie promotion. While Bhumi went for a classic-chic look, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen sporting a rose-pink sequin sari with a barely-there blouse. Kapoor Khan punctuated the risqué look with a layered diamond necklace and her signature makeup. Here’s our edit of all the versatile ways in which you can work this trend. Bhumi PednekarBhumi Pednekar is all about the less is more formula, seen here in an antique white, sequin sari and blouse, sans the jewellery. Tara Sutaria  The young and vivacious Tara Sutaria stepped out in a smoke grey, sequin sari and blouse combination for the recent Diwali festivities. To do justice to this all-embellished ensemble, Tara swapped heavy statement jewellery for a dainty layered necklace and complemented it with soft and peachy makeup. Natasha PoonawallaThe all-time advocate of all things extra, Natasha Poonawalla pulled all stops with this sage green sequin sari and styled it with an emerald green necklace, suitable for a Maharani. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon’s take on the trend was a little different from her contemporaries. She styled her shimmering sari with a strappy, backless blouse, chandelier earrings, deep smokey eyes and Mogra bearing low bun. Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor in a sequined black sari is a vision to behold. The actress paired her sari with a cutout blouse and kept the rest of her look minimal, keeping the entire focus on the traffic-stopping silhouette.  If you’re looking to elevate your festive wardrobe this season, take inspiration from these leading ladies who have opted for some unusual and gravity-defying blouse styles. Every celebrity has a distinctive travel style, but there’s a common love shared for the closet staple kurta. Instead of flexing their sartorial muscles in high-end, street-style brands, the leading ladies have chosen the simple kurta as their favourite. Of course, they amp it up with their Hermès Birkin and Gucci sunglasses, but the dainty kurta sets still takes the centre stage. Take a cue from Kareena Kapoor Khan. The actor styled her aqua-blue bodysuit with a neon green, sequined, pencil skirt. Neutralising the look further with a pair of transparent, strappy heel.  Kriti SanonKriti Sanon effortlessly worked this form-fitting colour-blocked gown. She kept the rest of her look minimal with a pair of dainty, hoop earrings, and centre-parted hair.  Aditi Rao Hydari Aditi Rao Hydari demonstrated a distinctive of wearing the power suit. She opted for an ox-blood and burnt orange asymmetrical pantsuit, which she styled with a traditional choker.  Tara SutariTara Sutaria broke the monotony of her black and white outfit by teaming it with a bright neon skirt, another way of working the colour-block trend.  Athiya ShettyAthiya Shetty opted for a contrasting gown in lime green and beige, working two contradicting hues in the same outfit.  Alia BhattInstead of infusing multiple colours in the same outfit, Alia Bhatt chose contrasting separates in two bright hues, an innovative way of sporting the colour-block trend.					There are risqué trends, and then there is the cut-out dress trend. The peek-a-boo skin-show moment has an understated appeal to it. There are multiple ways in which you can wear the cut-out dress. The geometrical shape can be carved out from the centre, showing your toned midriff or from the sides and the back, accentuating your curves. Recently, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen in a lemon yellow, diamond-shaped, midriff cut-out dress by Dion Lee, at the trailer launch of her movie. The actor teamed the dress with a pair of strappy heels, dainty earrings and hexagon-shaped glasses. You can easily replicate this look at your next Sunday brunch with the girls. Scroll down to view all the celebrity-approved ways of wearing a cut-out dress.  Nushrat Bharucha Nushrat Bharucha styled this metallic, side cut-out dress by Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna with a pair of high heels and pushed-back sleek hair. A party look you can easily imitate.  Janhvi KapoorJanhvi Kapoor raised the heat in this multiple cut-out, asymmetrical Basil Soda gown. The young actor complemented the ensemble with a pair of statement Sophie Webster heels and a stark red mouth. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde broke the solid colour monotony of this bright-coloured yellow dress with a pair of aqua-hued earrings. A smart styling hack you can incorporate in your next look.  Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor effortlessly worked the monochromatic, sequined, side cut-out dress by Prabal Gurung. The actor kept the rest of her look simple with a sleek ponytail, drop earrings and a hint of glitter on the lids. If less is more is your vibe, this look is tailor-made for you. Kiara AdvaniKiara Advani looked like a vision in this double textured, side cut-out dress. If you want to give the sequin and bright colour combination a rest, you can opt for this minimal-chic outfit by Prabal Gurung.					There is a nip in the air and the weather is finally getting pleasant. Although we do not get to enjoy the perks of a full-blown winter just yet, we can still relish the season with an upgraded wardrobe. A fail-safe trend you can bet on is the shirt dress, it’s cosy, comfortable and ultra-stylish. It’s basically a shirt sans the pants, but we’re not complaining.You can style it with a broad belt like Sonakshi Sinha, or wear it oversized like Malaika Arora. Layer it with a blazer and you’re boardroom ready, or team it with thigh-high boots for a night on the town. You can also make it your workwear staple like Meghan Markle who is an official fan of the buttoned-down shirt dress trend. We’ve rounded up a list of celebrity-approved shirt dress looks for you to take style inspiration from. Malaika AroraWant to achieve that laid-back, relaxed, chic look? Take cue from Malaika Arora who styled her oversized grey shirt with a pair of fiery red, ankle-length boots. Pooja HegdePooja Hegde upped her street-style game with this metallic blue, striped shirt, which she styled with a Gucci, belt bag and chained sunglasses. You can imitate this look if you want to give your basic shirt dress an upgrade. Sonam Kapoor AhujaSonam Kapoor Ahuja wore this black and white, Cover Story dress, designed by Karl Lagerfeld and teamed it with a pair of sleek, black boots. Demonstrating how to work this trend the old-school, classic way. Karisma KapoorIf the idea of wearing a plain shirt dress to work sounds mundane to you, layer it with a blazer and a pair of cool sneakers, just like Karisma Kapoor did. Shraddha KapoorInstead of digging deep in your closet to find that perfect party dress, borrow a formal shirt from your boyfriend, team it with a wide, waist-clenching belt and you have a winning look on your hands. Deepika PadukoneIf minimalism isn’t your thing and you’re all about those intricate details, opt for this long, form-flattering, knotted shirt dress by Rajesh Pratap. Ditch the jewellery, like Deepika Padukone, and allow the dress to take the centre stage. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon kept this day look fuss-free in an emerald green, shirt dress by Nupur Kanoi and styled it with a pair of closed-toe heels and geometrical earrings by Azotiique. Kriti KharbandaKriti Kharbanda was seen working the trend in this printed shirt dress and kept the rest of the look clean with just a high top-knot.   The most recurring sari during the festive season was the sequin laden six yards by Manish Malhotra, another innovative rendition of the classic silhouette by the couturier. The shimmer sari has become a go-to sartorial choice for almost every leading lady in Bollywood. The latest addition to the list is Bhumi Pednekar who opted for an off-white sequin sari, and teamed it with a dainty velvet blouse during her movie promotion. While Bhumi went for a classic-chic look, Kareena Kapoor Khan was seen sporting a rose-pink sequin sari with a barely-there blouse. Kapoor Khan punctuated the risqué look with a layered diamond necklace and her signature makeup. Here’s our edit of all the versatile ways in which you can work this trend. Bhumi PednekarBhumi Pednekar is all about the less is more formula, seen here in an antique white, sequin sari and blouse, sans the jewellery. Tara Sutaria  The young and vivacious Tara Sutaria stepped out in a smoke grey, sequin sari and blouse combination for the recent Diwali festivities. To do justice to this all-embellished ensemble, Tara swapped heavy statement jewellery for a dainty layered necklace and complemented it with soft and peachy makeup. Natasha PoonawallaThe all-time advocate of all things extra, Natasha Poonawalla pulled all stops with this sage green sequin sari and styled it with an emerald green necklace, suitable for a Maharani. Kriti SanonKriti Sanon’s take on the trend was a little different from her contemporaries. She styled her shimmering sari with a strappy, backless blouse, chandelier earrings, deep smokey eyes and Mogra bearing low bun. Karisma KapoorKarisma Kapoor in a sequined black sari is a vision to behold. The actress paired her sari with a cutout blouse and kept the rest of her look minimal, keeping the entire focus on the traffic-stopping silhouette.  If you’re looking to elevate your festive wardrobe this season, take inspiration from these leading ladies who have opted for some unusual and gravity-defying blouse styles. From exaggerated shoulders to some risqué cuts with décolletage detail, these statement-making pieces are all you need. Traditional blouses are constantly being reinvented with a modern twist. While Sonam Kapoor Ahuja kept it simple with a scarlet blouse, bearing an asymmetrical front opening. Sara Ali Khan opted for a sheer blouse with 3D floral applique. Raise a toast!Natasha Poly dressed in this Versace gown is elegance personified. Shades of Champaign meet subtle yet shiny makeup and a neat hairdo to perfect her look. If you forgot to notice it in Lima’s style, here’s another reason why you should go overboard when it comes to matching the outfit with your jewellery.  A cape escapeHuma Qureshi concluded her Cannes journey in Anamika Khanna, and we couldn’t have asked for a more gorgeous good bye!  Leather luxeNoel Capri goes bold and basic in a glossy, black Zuhair Murad couture.  Beaming ballerinaGet over little black dresses, red is taking over the season as Alina Baikova’s stuns in Zuhair Murad.  Roaring redDua Lipa is charming over the world with her songs as well as her unique sense of style. She lives up to our expectations as she steps in an extravagant ruffled red gown by Valentino. Asymmetrical cut, drop earrings, and glossy bun are some of the richest trends to take from this look.  Exquisite easeLipa keeps the drama going strong in a figure-hugging black silk dress. Southern France gets lit as stars from all over the world flood the city to attend the 72nd Cannes Film Festival. We have hand-picked some of the most talked-about trends that won hearts on the second day of the event.  The classic red-n-goldAlessandra Ambrosio storms in a dramatic red gown, solidifying our love for thigh-high slits and knotted necklines.  Mermaid magicHina Khan’s Cannes debut is all things sparkle in a stunning silver gown by Ziad Nakad. Her look features the current rage of plunging neckline and peppy play of silver.  Flower powerElle Fanning takes a fresh spin on florals in a floaty dress, made more magical with a milkmaid braid.  Leather loveJulianne Moore comes dressed in a statement Louis Vuitton gown, throwing in just the right amount of leather luxe.  Pretty pastelsFrédérique Bel brings carefree pastel hues to the red carpet, and we’re in awe.  Team textureChris Lee make heads turn in Balmain suit with a strong take on texture.  Shine on shimmerAmber Heard oozes oodles of glam and glimmer, flaunting makeup by L’Oréal Paris. Formal-alleyMonia Chokri make basics look beguiling. Chic sleekSelena Gomez steal hearts in a gorgeous navy blue ensemble, donning a daring deep middle part.
